en: Two hundred frescoes outside the center.
One of the most important botanical gardens in Europe.
Every first Sunday of the month and the previous Saturday over 500 banks fill Piazza Grande and the nearby streets: it is the oldest antique fair in Italy, with up to 30,000 visitors.
The headboard of Val d'Ayas under Mount Rosa, divided into villages such as Champoluc and Antagnod, between Walser architecture, wood craftsmanship and Blue Lake.
A Renaissance villa frescoed inside the walls of a castle, among the vineyards.
Michelangelo and the marble.
The village where the carved portals of the Ponente were born.

Fortilizio dei Dotti destroyed by the Florentines and rebuilt after 1487 for Niccolò Bufalini, transformed into a noble dwelling in the 1930s; rooms decorated by Cristofano Gherardi, the Galleria delle Donne Forti, the moat and the Italian garden with rose garden, green gallery, lemon house and one of the rare historical bosso labyrinths. Open Friday, Saturday, Sunday and holidays.
Museum of peasant civilization set up in the cellars of the Monastery of Montebello, open to the visit.

Neo-Gothic castle overlooking the city, furnished by Captain Enrico Alberto d'Albertis with objects from five continents; today it houses the Museum of Cultures of the World. You will also arrive with the elevator of Montegalletto from via Balbi.
The town, just above the coast, has historical ties with the Arbëreshë community (in italo-Albanian  "Jacari") and offers views of the sunsets of the Tyrrhenian Sea.
Verona before the Romans.
Huxley called it "the most beautiful painting in the world."

In Civita di Bagno, in front of the Gran Sasso, with Roman and Lombard structures and the remains of the cathedral of San Massimo, seat of the first diocese of the territory; visitable in extraordinary openings.
Neo-Romanesque cathedral next to the bishop's palace, minor basilica since 2016; heir to the Norman cathedral of ancient Miletus, seat of the first Latin diocese of southern Italy.
The civil and religious center of the city.
The most impressive remains of the ancient walls, the site of the archaeological museum of the civic pole.
The castle that dominates the village and the frescoes of Ocello da Ceva.

The complex was founded in the 12th century as a Benedictine abbey of Santa Maria di Maniace, partly destroyed by the earthquake of 1693 and then donated to Admiral Horatio Nelson. It includes the residence of the Dukes Nelson-Bridport (called  the Castle) with the Nelson Museum among furnished apartments, family portraits, documents and relics, the church of Santa Maria in Arab-Norman style, the granaries transformed into congress halls, the Celtic cross in honor of the admiral in the courtyard, an English garden and a park with lava stone sculptures and the English cemetery of the ducal family.

Granite Valley of the Retica Alps dominated by Monte Disgrazia (3,678 m) and Pizzo Badile, a climbing and trekking destination: here you will find the Natural Reserve of the Val di Mello, the Sasso Remenno, the ancient thermal baths of the Bagni di Masino and the Sentiero Roma.
Walk on the Roman pavement and the Appia.
The most important Cistercian abbey on the island.

Museo-Laboratorio del Centro visita del Parco, dedicated to the Milanese zoologist who re-introduced suede here: two large halls with panels, dioramas, multimedia and finds. At the centre is the Abruzzo suede; showcases on traditional industries (wool, pasta) and the replica of a Majella cave with rock paintings; the archaeological section dedicated to F. Verlegia goes from prehistory to the Middle Ages, with Roman funeral epigraphs of imperial age and the cast of the Majella man, over 7,000 years old, from the Neolithic village of Fonterossi. Next to it, the botanical garden "Michele Tenor" with about 500 species, many endemic.
The cathedral of the village and the sanctuary of the Madonna del Soccorso, reported by Visit Tuscany among the churches of Montalcino.
The view of the Sibillini.

At about 1,000 meters, town of the Peuketiantes inhabited by the 8th century BC, fortified in the 4th century BC with a double wall (some stones bear Greek letters) and divided into districts by a main road; it was abandoned in the 3rd century BC after a great fire. The House of the Pithoi reconstructs a house of the fifth century B.C. with the four large jars. Open on weekends and holidays from June to mid-November, every day in August, by reservation on other days.

City of the Metropolitan City of Milan with the castle Cassino Scanasio, already Trivulzio and Visconti of Modrone, the Museum of pots in history, the astronomical observatory at Cascina Grande and the protected naturalistic oasis of the Smeraldino and Sorgiva.
The Borgia Palace in Pienza.

Ancient copper mine along the path to Lake Erdèmolo, exploited by the sixteenth century for four centuries: at the beginning of the sixteenth century German miners (Bergknappen) dug a hundred galleries. The underground path reconstructs the original environment with thematic settings; guided tour only, groups of up to 12 people, helmet and cape provided, temperature about 8 °C. Open 10-18 on the weekends of June and September, from Tuesday to Sunday to July and August, on Sunday in October; inside you do not pay by card.

The last village of the Valle Antigorio before the Formazza Valley, Premia combines the thermal baths of Cadarese, with water flowing at 44 °C, the Orridi di Urizzo excavated from the waters of the Toce glacier, the Mineral Museum with over 3,300 Ossolani minerals and the walser fractions of Salecchio, abandoned in 1966 and remained almost intact.

Borgo sul Po grew up around the abbey of Polirone, founded in 1007 by Tedaldo di Canossa, grandfather of Countess Matilde: the basilica rebuilt by Giulio Romano, the cloisters, the refectory and the Civic Museum Polironiano make it one of the major Benedictine destinations of Northern Italy.
XV century church of the center of Bisignano.
12th century cathedral with an imposing bell tower and the chapel of Santa Barbara.
The sea under the promontory.
The ice cave.

Three buildings built between the end of the 17th and end of the 18th century, once united by an air pass similar to the Bridge of Sighs. In the eighteenth century they housed Maria Teresa of Austria, Carlo III of Spain, Napoleon and Mozart, who stayed there three times and played in the room of the noble piano, with excellent acoustics and frescoed ceiling attributed to Antonio Gresta; the upper palace, donated to the municipality, hosts exhibitions and concerts. Guided tours by reservation.
Columbus' family home-tower.
A bathroom with water that sometimes comes warm.

The seaside resort of the Riviera delle Palme, an ancient village of farmers and fishermen of Roman origin: on the seafront the bastion of 1564 against pirates, inland the village Peagna with the paleontological Museum "Silvio Lai" and the small Regional Reserve of the Rio Torsero, famous for the fossils of Pliocene.
The fourteenth century sanctuary of Cemmo.
The headland of Bourbon history over the harbor.
The residence of the Castromediano, lords and archaeologists of Cavallino.

In the center are Palazzo Mesiani-Mazzacuva (late 18th century), today used by the Municipality as a cultural center of Magna Grecia; Palazzo Nesci Sant'Agata (Seventeenth century) on the main square, private; Palazzo Tuscano (nineteenth century) in the upper part, seat of the Visitor Centre of the Aspromonte National Park.

In the Grande valley, inside the Natural Park of the Maritime Alps, lakes, woods and a restored alpine village; Palanfre is the starting point for excursions, including the beech forest of the Bosco Bandito.

A pilgrimage route of 1.8 km (about half an hour) crosses the larch groves of Madonna di Senales to the Marian shrine, with stations carved by South Tyrolean craftsmen: the copy of the miraculous image of Alois Rainer, the Annunciation of Josef Tappeiner, Bethlehem, the Pietà of Josef Santer and Mary with the Apostles of Ulrich Santer. In the church, on the altar of Our Lady, the statue of Our Lady is kept in an ostensory.

Symbol of the village, it is an ancient rock of green tuff about ten meters high that emerges from the sea a few meters from the shore: erupted from Mount Epomeo, it was shaped by the sea in the form that made it famous.
The church at the bottom of the canal.
The white cliffs above the Adriatic.

Among the carruggi of the historical center remain the ancient furnaces in which for centuries the lime was produced, with the Town Hall, the parish church of Santa Maria Maggiore and the ancient towers of coastal defense.
The most scenic water temple in Nuragic Sardinia.
Contemporary art in the town hall.
In the center of Frisanco the square with the seventeenth-century Palazzo Pognici; the parish church of Santi Fosca and Maura is mentioned in documents of 1492.
The Temple of San Cono preserves paintings from the seventeenth century and, in the crypt, the relics of the saint, a place of worship and a great pilgrimage.

On the road to Canelli, at the foot of the hill of Salto, is the house-bottega of Pinolo Scaglione, carpenter and musician friend of Pavese, who guided him through the paths and vineyards of the Belbo valley telling him the local stories: in the novel "The moon and the bonfires" became the character of Nuto. After his death the house became a museum.
In the former Jesuit college, the history of Rimini from prehistory to the twentieth century, with the painting of the fourteenth century.

On the shores of the lake remain the ruins of the villa of the Venulei family, from the beginning of the first century AD, with a monumental spa complex in panoramic position on the lake, coast and sea. The exhibition pavilion "Guglielmo Lera" includes a second Roman building discovered in the 1930s, with a small thermal environment, part of the heating system and the mosaic of the frigidary to fantastic animals in black and white tiles, and tells with a selection of objects the daily life of Massaciuccoli between I and IV century AD; in front, under a large cover, new excavations have brought to light other environments.

The palace of the Piersanti family (since 1728), museum since 1901: furniture, works and family memories, the treasure of silvers of the Sacred Chapel, sculptures and paintings from the 12th to the 18th century from the cathedral and the minor churches, the collection of Mgr. Venanzio Filippo Piersanti, master of pontifical ceremonies, and the archaeological collection Bigiaretti. Open from Thursday to Sunday.

In the former convent of San Francesco, attested from 1232 and rebuilt after the earthquake of 1627, from 1989 the seat of the Civic Museum: a path from prehistory to the Middle Ages with the daunis of the necropolis of Serpente, Pedincone and Casone (74 tombs excavated in 1970-71), a ceramic room apula with red and polychrome figures, a Roman lapidarium and a room on wheat, wine, oil and transhumance. It also houses the Pinacoteca "Luigi Schingo" and a large archive on the cartoonist Andrea Patienza.
Visits only on Sunday mornings by reservation
Kayak and boat in the crater.
A destination of pilgrims from Italy and Europe.
The view from the top of the tower.
The place of the ancient assemblies of the Friulian Slavia.
Fossils, live animals and a fauna recovery center in a single museum.

Inaugurated in 2000 in the former Augustinian convent of Sant'Oliva, it exhibits archaeological finds and testimonies of the history of Cori, including the architectural and sculptural fragments of the Temple of the Dioscuri, a 1:75 scale model and a copy of the statue of Minerva donated by the city of Rome in 1999.
The park on the Celius was built on a site of the flute and trajanean age, with a large green area just a stone's throw from the Colosseum.

Parish church built around the seventeenth century: it contains paintings, wooden statues of the seventeenth century and an organ of the eighteenth century. The patron saint is celebrated at the end of September.

Double walls with ample moat, rectangular towers, a polygonal tower on the south-west corner and two to the north-west, in the current form from about 1300; three gates, including the fourteenth-century Porta di San Genesio with the watchtower, from which you can see the walls and the moat. The entrance of Porta di Sotto is a round arch of 1835.
Three circles of Umbrian-Roman, Roman and medieval walls; from the Piazzale IV Novembre, the highest point of the city, views of the Tiber valley.

Municipality of the Friulian plain known for the shrine Temple of Cargnacco and the nearby historical museum of the countryside of Russia, and for the Neolithic village of Sammardenchia, told in the center historical-archaeological visits.
The view of the Roero.
The Cathedral of the patrons.

The summit of 540 meters is reached by path no. 750 between woods and Mediterranean maquis, starting from Torre Paola on the seafront of Sabaudia or from Piazzale delle Crocette in the upper part of San Felice; from the promontory the view embraces dunes, coast of Sabaudia, lakes of the Park and Gulf of Gaeta to the Pontine islands. One way goes up through one holm oak, the other along the side of the mountain.

In the eighteenth century Palazzo Grassi collects Adriatic marine organisms, the result of research carried out from the second half of the nineteenth century to 1943, with panels and multimedia locations on biodiversity; there is exposed a female elephant shark captured in Chioggia in 2003.
The artifacts of the Castle of Pia.
A fraction that retains pre-Romanic traces.
The Istrian-Veneto living room.
Three-storey brick-covered building, built by Marquis Enrico Gagliardi and now owned by the municipality; hosts the Read & Write Festival.
For a fee; free on the first Sunday of the month and always up to 12 years (secondary source)
Five hundred ascolano.

Municipality of the Modena plain on the Panaro, with the church of San Giovanni Battista rebuilt in 1862, the courtyard of the Palazzo di Donna Clarina and the villas of the river "Riviera" such as Villa Bonasi Benucci, damaged by the 2012 earthquake.

Porta della bassa Valle Camonica, Darfo Boario Terme combines the Boario thermal park, with the Liberty dome of 1913 and four sources, with the rock art of the UNESCO site n. 94 in the Park of Luine and the Corni Freschi, at Lake Moro of glacial origin and at frescoed churches like Santa Maria del Restello, with works by Callisto Piazza.
The dome in the lock hole.
The oldest church in the upper valley.
Seven seaside resorts, from Lido di Volano to Lido di Spina, for years with the Blue Flag.
Romanesque capitals with proto-Christian symbols.
The view that gives the village the name of ... the Balcony of the Ciociaria.
Frassinello is one of the nine municipalities of the core zone The infernots are ancient deep cellars dug directly into a particular rock similar to tuff.
The prehistory of Fucino next to the village on stilts.
The miller's river.
The art garden of the sculptor Maria Dompè dedicated to the partisan Norma Parenti, with spirals of earth, lawn and stone and classical music, near the walls.
The hospice of pilgrims became theater.
A small country courtyard, which can also be visited with a dog on a leash.

Hiking in the woods under the ridge of Mendola overlooking Bolzano, the Lower Atesina and the Dolomites; the best starting point is the Steinegger restaurant, with parking, and it is recommended as a day trip from spring to late autumn.

Ancient medieval entrance with ogival arch next to the Duomo; in the door and in the Cremonini house an Antiquarium with sculptures, mosaics and an epigraph in bronze, and under the door the remains of a Roman bridge of Augustian age on the Stirone. Along Via Frate Gherardo run the Visconti walls.

Remains of the ancient castle of the lords of Bardonecchia, who between 1330 and 1335 submitted to the Dolphins; in 1562 there died the Protestant refugees in the tower after a battle. First restoration in the context of the archaeological park project.

The Jewish community, present in the fifteenth century and formally constituted in 1627, was removed in 1799; the building, with parts of 1729, passed to the Israelite University of Siena and in 1924 to the Municipality. Two factory bodies: on the upper floor the synagogue, in the rest probably school and home of the rabbi; inside a painted window, the niche of the aron ha-kodesh and terracotta pipes perhaps of the miqveh.

A heritage of 34 restored solar quadrants (plus two new ones), dated between 1734 and 1934, recovered with the project "Bellino Solare." The recommended itinerary starts from Ribiera (1412 m) and Chiesa, goes up to Fontanile and along the GTA in the woods, passes under Pleyne, crosses Prafauchier and Celle and arrives at Chiazale (1710 m): about 12 km round trip, 300 m of difference in altitude; the villages are also reached by car.

Borgo dell'Alta Val Venosta from the Romanesque bell towers and sixteenth-century houses, with the church of San Benedetto and its Carolingian frescoes among the oldest in central Europe; above Burgusio the Benedictine abbey of Monte Maria (about 1150), at 1,340 m.

In an elevated position with a view of the Val San Pellegrino and the Monzoni, it was consecrated in 1164, reconsecrated in 1216 and again in 1534 after the Gothic reconstruction desired by Bernardo Clesio; it retains the Gothic part and the original apse, while the current aspect is due to the extension on a project by Giovanni Tiella (1929). The three-nave interior houses works by the Moenese painter Valentino Rovisi, the golden wooden altar by Valentino Poschiavin (1715), the main altar by Martino Gabrielli and the crucifix, the windows and the portals by Cirillo Dellantonio.

The largest church of the village, built in 1741 on a project by Michelangelo di Giacomo, with three naves and eight chapels; the sculptural group of the facade is considered one of the most typical works of the Sicilian baroque statuary. It preserves the painting of the Martyrdom of St. Sebastian by Giuseppe Crestadoro (1789) and the wooden statue of the patron, survived the earthquake of 1693.
The Juvarrian cloister and the memory of the asylum.
Nasine and silver majolicas in the catacombs of San Cono.

The center is enclosed by the fifteenth-century walls of the castle, of which remain a stretch and two cylindrical towers; from the village the view ranges from Mount Ascensione to the Sibillini to the Adriatic and, on clear days, to Gran Sasso and Maiella.

Regional protected area of about 7,700 hectares, established in 1976 and natural park since 2011, with residues of oak trees, pinewoods of silvestre, moors where the calluna blooms at the end of summer, ruins of furnaces and patrician villas with gardens. It is accessible throughout the perimeter, also near the hospital and the train station, and is crossed by about 50 km of bike paths.
First possession of the accounts of Challant, a small town of hamlets between chestnuts and walnuts, with the lake of Villa and the ruins of the family castle.

A place of worship already mentioned in a document of 1125, rebuilt in the eighteenth century by Giuseppe Subleyras; it houses the tomb of Cardinal Ennio Filonardi, a San Sebastiano del Cavalier d'Arpino on the altar of the same name and an Addolorata by Antonio Cavallucci (XVIII century).
Boeri Studio's urban forest towers, awarded the International Highrise Award 2014, and the botanical park without fences that connects Gae Aulenti to the island.
The history of the pass.

Venue of the Municipality, the National Gallery of Umbria and the two major medieval guilds, the Nobile Collegio della Mercanzia and the Nobile Collegio del Cambio; above the portal the bronze copies of the grifo and the Guelph lion, whose originals (1271-81) are in the atrium.

Established on 26 November 1996 in the Romanesque crypt of the basilica, it exhibits about one hundred goods on 251 sqm: marble fragments of three eighteenth-century altars, tombstones from the fifteenth to the nineteenth century including the slab of a togato knight from the sixteenth century, nineteenth-century riggioles, silver sacred from the seventeenth to the twentieth century, reliquary statues, fragments of sixteenth-century tables saved from the fire of 1945 and the altar candlesticks of Aniello Treglia (1704); on the second floor bell liturgical vestments of the eighteenth-nineteenth century. In 2016, a gallery was added in a building next to the basilica. The municipality indicates free entrance.

The village of the Middle Mantovano between Oglio and Mincio, Castellucchio preserves of the Gonzaghesca fortress, rebuilt in 1379 by Ludovico I Gonzaga, the only civic tower, now home to the Museum of the ancient weapons Fosco Baboni; complete the visit the parish of San Giorgio and the churches and villages of the villages.

The walls preserve the original shape; you enter from Porta Venezia, whose name recalls the twinning of 1963 with Venice linked to Maria Manuzio, descendant of the family of printers, and along the belt there is a semicircular tower called "del'Albornoz."
The tools and machines of the Piedmontese peasant civilization.
Walk from the north door to the heart of the Park.

In the Astronomical Observatory of Capodimonte of INAF, more than 140 scientific instruments of the historical collection, inaugurated in 2012 for the bicentenary of the Observatory; free guided tour by reservation.
The heart of the Motor Valley by the sea.
A fragment of the medieval city.
In the castle of Avacelli, it preserves a Crucifix and a terracotta altar painted by the Madonna del Rosario and Mercy, the work of a workshop influenced by the Marches Della Robbia.
In the Palazzo Martini Carissimo, it presents archaeological finds of the Messapic territory.

Mountain country about 700 meters on the north-western slopes of Gennargentu, with a territory rich in Nuragic archaeology: the village of S'Urbale, the village-sanctuary of Abini and the archaeological museum of the area that preserves its finds, as well as the museum houses Satta and Mereu and the lake of Cucchinadorza.
A sober early 18th century Waldensian temple with a unique bell tower in the valleys.
€3.50 with guided tour, €2.50 without, students up to 26 years €2; free with FVG Card
The fraction of the orchards and the two churches.

16th century coastal fortress built by the Spadafora family on an ancient tower, with four angular spurs and garrets; the attribution to the Florentine architect Camillo Camiliani is now questioned. It was used more as a noble residence than as a defence, and inside it preserves elegant decorative stuccoes on the ceilings. Owned by the Region, restored with the Superintendence of Messina, it is used by the Municipality and the Pro Loco for cultural events; it can be visited free of charge on request.

Cell of the Ecomuseo del Biellese in Vermogno that documents the history and techniques of the search for gold over the centuries, explains how the native gold has been brought downstream by glaciers and exhibits auriferous samples of Italian rivers and streams. All year round guided tours, excursions and workshops on reading the landscape of Bessa and on the search for gold (geology, techniques, tools). Contacts: tel. 340 6114854.
A hot bath in the cave of Calipso.
A journey into the prehistory suitable for children.
Franciscan spirituality on the mountain.
Walk through amphitheatre and streets of a Roman city.

The fishing village of white houses on the hills of Vietri, among the most beautiful villages in Italy: in the center the church of Santa Margherita with frescoes of Neapolitan school including those of Francesco Solimena (feast on July 20), votive chapels along the streets and the square where in the evening you will find yourself. About 200 steps down to two small beaches.
An entire eighteenth-century farmhouse transformed into a museum.
The courthouses of the center of Trexenta.
The three women who made the story of Asolo in one museum.
The oldest church, at the top of the village.
A work by Monteverde and the last trace of the castle.

Situated with six furnaces from the I-II century A.D. for bricks, tiles and tiles; two furnaces west of the complex remained in use until the fourteenth century. You can visit only the furnace "A" with a circular plan and in excellent condition, with a cooking top of about 6 meters in diameter above the underground combustion chamber; guided tours and educational workshops.
The sea of Sinnai, towards Villasimius.
13th century church in Romanesque-Gothic style in the Sant'Angelo district. It preserves a protorinascimental fresco of the Virgin with the Child and saints.

Built in the 16th century, with monumental sandstone façade on a large staircase and Renaissance interior with three naves with monolithic stone columns and circular apse; it preserves the altar of the Sacrament in carved marble and the baptistery in local chives covered by a wooden dome, with a statue of the Assumption and a large wooden crucifix.
€4, under 18 free
The 15th century wooden Madonna in front of the village.
seasonal opening like the Pradis Caves, times 2026 in separate site PDF
The tradition of handmade bricks.
The residence of Jolanda di Savoia with view from the Canavese to Novara.
The Hellenistic city and the panorama of the coast.

Next to the church, in the square: not the usual town museum but a collection of sacred Baroque and Rococo objects, including a glass of Augusta of 1750 about, filigree of Bolzano, school banners of the Val di Fiemme and portraits of characters of Aldino like Cardinal Johann Baptist Franzelin. Opening by reservation through the tourist office.
The crypt of the patron saint and the ancient relief under the altar.

Also known as "Madonna della Belta" (Madonna of Belt), it is a seventeenth-century reconstruction of the previous Romanesque church, close to the parish, which has been a popular destination for centuries. We venerate an image considered miraculous of the Madonna and Child enthroned between four angels; on the sides of the main altar two great paintings of the twentieth century of an artist of the village, and on the altar of Santa Cristina a precious altarpiece with the martyrdom of the saint. Open during Sunday Mass at 18.15.
Palace and then prison for over a century and a half.
The Formiae hole in statues.
The popular baroque.

Typical rock settlement of Calascibetta, with caves on several levels excavated in grey limestone, used as a prison in the Middle Ages; in the rock you can see fossil shells of oysters of Pliocene. At Christmas they host the living nativity scene.
A short walk along the walls offers views of the landscape around the village.
Prehistory of the plain.
Centuries of grace received, painted.
The magnificent cathedral in terracotta of the city, seat of the diocesan museum.
You need boots or boots with carved sole; the helmet is supplied
Built probably in the second half of the fifteenth century, it preserves frescoes from the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.

Country of the Tesino basin, at the southern slopes of Mount Silana in Valsugana, among the most beautiful villages in Italy since 2021 and home of Alcide De Gasperi: his birthplace is now a museum, next to the museum Per Via on the sellers of prints thesis and the Arboretum with the Garden of Europe.
The instruments of a music industry in the Marche region.
Borgo sulla Valdichiana, home of the Chianina breed, with a historic centre on a small plateau.
visits by reservation (tel. 0733 223437)
The village above the city of Enea.

Built between the XI and XII century by the Columns on a Roman outpost guarding Via Valeria, with quadrangular plan with cylindrical towers at the corners (later reduced to two) and a front tower. The Colonna, lords from the 12th century, succeeded the Marquises of the Dragon until the 19th century; in 1859 it passed to the Pelagallos. Today it is private property, bound by the Superintendence since 1995.

In the Palazzo Veneziano, elegant seventeenth-century building among the most interesting in the Val Canale, the museum opened in the late 1980s tells geology and prehistory (wild Prato Pramollo and Casera Valbertad), the mine of Raibl and the local enterprises between the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, the daily life of the valley and the traditions of Christmas and Easter with the Krampus, as well as the history of the palace. Free with FVGcard.

Small medieval fortified village about 4 km from Cellere, Farnesian fief, birthplace of Tiburzi; depopulated at the beginning of the eighteenth century, it was repopulated in the eighteenth century by Albanian families fleeing persecutions, remembered by the painting of the Madonna degli Albanesi in the early medieval church of San Sigismondo martyr, who also has a saintly water with three Farnesian lilies. In July it hosts the MUSA festival.
Contemporary Sicilian art.
It rises in the highest point of the municipal territory; the current building dates back to 1622. Inside works by Pietro Cavaliere, brothers Merlo, Orazio Marinali and a canvas of the Maganza.
Sienese frescoes and a 16th century polyptych.
Loggiati frescoed in a hillside village.
The mountain of Leonardo which dominates the flat territory of the country.
A neoclassical temple set in the rock.
Oratory dedicated to the saint who, according to tradition, stayed in Pompeiana on his journey to Provence.
Rebuilt in the eighteenth century by Cosimo Morelli after a fire, it is the symbol of the village of fruit.
Thirty thousand pipes from all over the world.
the MiC card (updated to 7/2/2022) indicates it temporarily closed, with mandatory booking
Out of the crowded routes.

Romanesque church with semicircular apse in Botticino stone, with high medieval and Roman decorative elements re-used in the walls; in the apse a fresco of the fifteenth century attributed to Bonifacio Bembo.
The fortress that dominates the ancient village.
Fossils of the territory in a church of the fourteenth century.
The life of the hinterland of oil, from the mill to the peasant house.

The only copper museum in Sardinia, in the former convent of the Scolopi fathers: the copper section reconstructs the workshop of the Aramai with the original tools and the cart of the street vendor, and shows objects for the house, the fields and the wedding set worked with a cantilever and hammer. The textile section has an ethnographic part on Sardinian weavers and an artistic one with about thirty tapestries in copper, gold, silver, linen and raffia; sounds and voices accompany the visit, including the secret jargon of the ora, s'arromaniscus. Open from Tuesday to Sunday 10-13 and 16-18, closed on Monday.
The glance on the Charlemagne's locks.

In the Franciscan monastery of Maddalena, built in 1487 on a pilgrim's hospice along the Via degli Abruzzi and then home to the Customs of Foggia, school and prison. The collection, opened in 1898 with 335 exhibits and 130 coins and largely dispersed in the war, has fossils and paleolithic finds, statues of the Iron Age and osque ceramics, inscriptions and Roman furnishings, votive terracotta and a Sannite bull in golden bronze, as well as medieval and modern statues and ceramics. In the same complex the botanical garden, a nativity scene of the Neapolitan school, the War Museum and the International Museum of Fly Fishing "Stanisao Kuckiewicz" . Wednesday-Sunday 10.30-18.30.
Historical building of the center, seat of the State Library Isontina.
Fortified settlement with visible remains, in a territory inhabited since the Bronze Age; it is reached with a short cycle path equipped with explanatory panels.

Municipality of the Apennines along the Via Flaminia, the ancient post station Ad Ensem, entirely included in the Park of Monte Cucco between the Catria and the Cucco; in the territory the Romanesque abbeys of Sant'Emiliano in Conjunctoli and Santa Maria di Sitria and the Camaldolese Hermitage of San Girolamo.
Six hundred Lombards.

Also known as the former Cathedral of Letters, it stands on a hill of the Lattari Mountains with the fortress behind it and is today the parish of Santa Maria Assunta and San Giovanni Battista. Built at the end of the 16th century, it has a Latin cross plan and a single nave with four chapels on the right and three on the left; the altar of the presbytery is made with the marbles of the ancient balustrade. In the left transept the Coven of the SS. Rosario holds relics and relics; the statue of St. Anne, invoked by pregnant women, is linked to the tradition of the ... dust of the Saint.
Set up in some casemattes, it recalls the peasant world, life on the river and craft shops, as well as domestic life with furniture, clothes and toys; also exhibited photographs and maps.

The town of the northern hinterland of Milan overlooks the Groane Park, with the Museum of Siolo dedicated to peasant life and furnaces, the historical park of Villa Gianotti and the Basilica of Saints Eusebio and Maccabei.

The 19th-century lakefront, tree-lined, with hotels like the Grand Hotel Victoria of 1885, offers views of Bellagio and Varenna; the Long Lake Benedetto Castelli the Monument to the marble weaver of Carrara by Francesco Somaini, donated by the Mantero family, and along Via Roma the Lido of 1934, example of rationalist architecture with beach and pool. Piazza Garibaldi, the heart of the village, is surrounded by cafes and restaurants.

Valcellina municipality in the Friulian Dolomites Nature Park, with a small building, ice rink, ice park and ski slopes; it houses the Casa Clautana museum and the dinosaur footprints of the Casavento hut, the first found in the Park.

The village of Macerata is one of the most beautiful villages in Italy, closed by fourteenth-century walls in which you enter from Porta San Lorenzo; in the valley, in Montecosaro Scalo, the Romanesque basilica of Santa Maria a piede di Chienti, one of the most beautiful Romanesque architectures in the territory.
At 1116 meters, the first giant bench of the lake area and a panoramic swing, reachable from a path from the Wonderwood park.
Museum dedicated to the ancient traditional feminine costume, symbol of the local identity.
With 14th century bell tower; the village preserves traces of walls, towers, houses and medieval loggias.

Born in 1983 in the middle school, after the discovery in 1972 of a Lombard necropolis during the expansion of the building; closed for flooding in 1991, it reopened definitively in 1998. Three rooms with finds from the Bronze Age to the Renaissance (also from the Roman necropolis of the vicus), a paleontological room with the collection G. C. Politi (more than 400 pieces, including fossils of Solnhofen and Bolca), a stone-stone under the porch and in the garden the Longobard graves, indicated as the only Lombard necropolis preserved on sight in Italy. Open Saturday 14.30-18.30 and Sunday 10-12 and 14.30-18.30; closed in August, from 20 to 31 December, from 1 to 6 January and at Easter. Accessible.

Salento Country a few kilometers from the sea, with the Mother Church of Sant'Antonio di Padova with its eighteenth-century façade, the Doge's Palace of Guarini and the Byzantine crypt of Santa Maria degli Angeli, whose original frescoes are in the museum of the Municipal Villa; in the village of Vaste the Warriors Park and the Museum of Messapian civilization.
The millstones that are still spinning.
The craftsmanship of the valley.

Palace on three floors built in the second half of the nineteenth century for a wealthy local family, with frescoes from the beginning of the twentieth century on the noble floor and valuable concrete floors; in the cellars are re-emerged tanks for oil and well. The garden is a botanical park in the taste of the time, with flower beds, benches overlooking the promenade and the sea and many exotic plants. Today it is the cultural center of the municipality: Biblioteca Civica (Civic Library) . Novaro, Museo MARM and Sala Mostre Hawks.

The highest municipality on the island of Capri: the Blue Grotto, the ancient water lily of an imperial villa, the remains of Villa Damecuta, Villa San Michele by Axel Munthe and the church of San Michele with the majolica floor.
The civilization of Golasecca told a few steps from the river.
Torrente that flows into a deep canyon before joining the Temo, forming waterfalls; it is a destination of trekking routes and marks the border with Bosa, reachable from the highway 292.

access only accompanied by local staff upon reservation (Ethnoanthropological Museum 331 6976973 or Tourist Office 0934 954300 int. 6), free during the feasts of San Paolino and Sant'Onofrio; not accessible to people with disabilities

Ancient town of the Campania plain at the foot of Vesuvius, known for the Festa dei Gigli: a museum that tells the territory from prehistory to the Middle Ages and the remains of a village of the Bronze Age buried by an eruption.

The infernot is a small underground chamber excavated in the Stone by Cantons, without light or ventilation, usually reached from a cellar and used to store the wine in bottle at constant temperature and humidity. Ponzano, linked to Alemat Winery, was inaugurated on May 8, 2016 during ... 2016 , and is connected to the Ecomuseo della Pietra da Cantoni.

Trapanese city in whose territory extends the archaeological park of Selinunte, Greek colony founded by the Megaresi in the VII century BC and destroyed by the Carthaginians in 409 BC, with the Doric temples of the Eastern Hill and the Acropolis; in the city the church of San Domenico, known as the Sistine of Sicily, the Mother Church, the Fountain of the Ninfa, the Civic Museum with the Ephebo and, little outside, the Trinity of Delia.
On the slopes of Mount Cetona the caves inhabited in prehistory and then by saints and hermits, visitable in the park linked to the Museum for Prehistory.

Free exhibition open all year under the Tourist Office: fossil tree trunks of about 260 million years ago from the Giogo di Meltina, 11 panels on the geology of the Tschögglberg and 11 windows with minerals, fossils and geological samples, to tell extinct plants and animals, deserts and seas, eruptions, earthquakes, glaciers and streams.

Church at the beginning of the village, completed in 1820 with baroque shapes, facade in white stone with central window and unique nave. Inside two canvases by Teofilo Patini, the ...Miracle of the Cross and ...Carlo Borromeo with a moribund.

Borgo at the foot of the Pollino National Park, with a medieval centre perched on the hill and overlooking the plain of Sibari; it boasts the church of Santa Maria della Consolazione, the highest example of Gothic Angevin in Calabria, the Civic Museum with the "San Ladislao" by Simone Martini, the Norman castle and the Pallotta Tower. It is the city of bread.

The highest peak of Puglia (1,151 meters), the ... the roof of Puglia... from Lake Pescara there is a hike of about four hours. At the top, at the highest panoramic point of the Capitana, there is a giant bench.
A Renaissance villa-fortress with vineyards and tastings.
The Malaspina palace overlooking the coast above the Po valley.

Country of the Langhe recognizable by the two eighteenth-century bell towers, that of the parish church of San Lorenzo and that of the church of the Immaculate Conception, which houses the Museum of contemporary art dedicated to the painter and sculptor Daedalo Montali; from the village the look ranges on Alba, the plain of Tanaro and, in the distance, the Alps.

Square building on two levels hidden between the houses and reached by the substep     \ on Porci Â Â , it was from the middle of the seventeenth century prison of the Incontrada of Barbagia of Seulo, under the Duchy of Mandas, then of the Sabauda justice and of the Italian State until the closure in 1975. Visitors can visit the janitor's accommodation with nineteenth-century furnishings, the reception office and the female cell on the upper floor, the male cell and the punishment cell without windows on the lower floor; exposed documents of the eighteenth-nineteenth century on the transport of prisoners and medical and spice remedies.
The iron beaten like it used to be.
Neolithic decorations in the woods.
Get on the roof of Puglia.
The temple of the minerals of the Upper Valley.
One of the oldest churches in Milan and model of the Romanesque Lombardy, where St. Augustine was converted: he guards the remains of the patron, the treasure under the porch and a small museum.

In a building designed in 1967 as a convent of the Clarisses, adapted to exhibition space in 1983 and expanded in 1998 with European funds; in 2018 the exhibition was renovated according to the formula of the ecomuseum and in 2021, with the European project WALKofPEACE, a space dedicated to the Great War and the reclamation was inaugurated. The route tells the relationship between man and environment in the Lower Piave from the Roman and late Roman times to the contemporary age: the peasant life before the Bonifiche, the hydraulic transformations of the eastern Veneto, the First World War and the reconstruction of the landscape. Open Tuesday 9-12.30, Wednesday-Friday 10-12.30 (Thursday also 15-18), Saturday and Sunday 15-18; closed on Monday.

The only village on the shore of the lake, on a small conoid at the base of the mountain: in 1896 Giacomo Feltrinelli built a cotton mill around which an industrial village was born with working houses, school, theatre and church. Closed the factory in 1981, the country reinvented itself with tourism: beaches and constant wind (Peler in the morning, Now in the afternoon) make it a paradise for windsurfing, kitesurfing and sailing, with schools and sailing circle.

Opened from 1992, it tells the rural life from 1500 to 1918, when the County of Gorizia was under the Habsburgs, in three buildings: an eighteenth-century structure (cellar and barn), a nineteenth-century one (stalls and barns) and a canopy of the mid-Twentieth century. About 25,000 pieces catalogued: trades such as mason, basket, shoemaker, blacksmith, carpenter and a late 19th century typography; plows from the 16th to the 20th century and tools for sowing, harvest and threshing; weights and measurements before and after the metric system (introduced in the County in 1841); tin boxes of the Monfalcone Passer factory; a vintage school room and a room on women in the rural world. Open Wednesday 10-13 and 15-19, Thursday and Friday 10-13 and 18-19, Saturday and Sunday 9-13 and 15-19; groups with one week notice.
The gallery of the Foundation, housed in Villa Mazzucchelli.
The village suspended on the river.
The baroque sanctuary on the bulwark.

Country on a hill of tuff whose name, attested around 1100, indicates a valley dominated by a mountain: the heart is the "pamphilia" city wanted by Camillo Pamphilj, with the Palazzo Doria Pamphilj frescoed by Mattia Preti, Gaspard Dughet and the Burgundy and the Collegiate of Mattia de' Rossi, the only structures of the ancient nucleus survived the bombings of the Second World War, to which is added the Convent of Sant'Angelo on the homonymous hill.

Country of the Valley of Comino overlooking the Karst lake of Posta Fibreno, Regional Nature Reserve fed by numerous springs, with the floating island called "Rita" cited by Pliny the Old; in the historic center the Naturalistic Ethnographic Museum, on the shore of the water mill of 1810.

The path of the Holy Face, branch of the Via Francigena, runs from Pontremoli to Lucca in about 150 km divided into ten stages and ends at the cathedral of San Martino, which preserves the wooden crucifix of the Holy Face. Camporgiano is on the seventh stage, between Piazza al Serchio and Castelnuovo di Garfagnana; the stretch from Camporgiano to Castelnuovo measures about 10 km.
Museum of Contemporary Sculpture in the seventeenth century Palazzo Pomarici and in the underground excavated below it, with over 400 permanent works and a library.
An ancient place of worship.
The Park explained step by step.

Over 1,400 metres, between beech and oak woods of the Regional Natural Park of the Simbruini Mountains: in winter downhill and cross-country trails in La Bandita, Campo dell'Osso and Fossa dell'Acero, in summer a network of trails; in autumn the woods are yellow and red.

The village of the Langhe, known as the "borgo delle mele" (the "borgo delle mele") is dominated by the castle of the five towers that the Falletti di Alba built from 1429 on a hill above the Bern stream; in the village the parish church of Sant'Eusebio, rebuilt in 1662.
Renaissance in terracotta.
A small church of the lords of Montegnacco.

Farmland of Trexenta north of the Flumini Mannu, dedicated to the cultivation of wheat: the Museum of the wheat in the ancient house Serra, together with the Gothic-Catalan parish church of St. Peter and the Romanesque country church of St. Bartholomew.
He holds a 15th-century triptych from Sienese school.

Built from the 11th century and very transformed until the 18th century, it stands on a hill partly hidden from the houses; it preserves frescoes of various styles dated from the 13th to the 16th century.
Romanesque church on the ascent to the castle, with an arched portal with sharp sixth and a monophora decorated with floral motifs.

It houses the archaeological collection of Ernesto Palopoli, about 2,000 pieces from the protohistory to the Byzantine age, largely from Krotoniatide: among the materials Brettii a clay doll with moving arts, between the Byzantine buckles belt and two box fibula with peacocks, one of which is the museum logo.

Built in 1294 at the request of Cardinal Matteo Bentivenga, outside the walls, in simple Franciscan style; the fifteenth-century chapel of San Bernardino contains fragments of frescoes and wooden works of the fourteenth century, including the Madonna della Stella and a crucifix from San Giovanni de Butris.
Crivelli's polyptych house.

Three structures: an ancient rural house of the eighteenth century, the museum house with permanent exhibitions and the hut of Binò Alpelté, a small alpine pasture built under a rock that acts as a roof.

Karst complex at the end of the valley of Lanaittu, one of the largest caves in Europe: Sa Oche (the voice of the hamlet) has a large entrance with three lakes and rebombs after the storms; On Bentu it develops for about 16 km on several levels and is accessible only to expert speleologists. The river that crosses them resurfaces in Su Gologone. Admission for a fee.

Lake 570 meters between the woods, with turquoise waters to the intense blue, reached by a long staircase and short paths; in summer you swim and there are pedalos, and with the low water appears a small island joined to the shore. From 2024 it is a Local Nature Reserve; from Canale you will arrive on foot in about 30 minutes.
The Vivarini in a village of Montefeltro.

Borgo Bandiera Arancione on the slopes of the Dauni Mountains, with the historic center that rises along the ridge: the abbey complex with the Cave of San Michele and the church of the Annunziata of the 11th century, the Baronale Palace of the Knights of Calatrava and the bread baked in the straw oven.

The only hamlet of Magliano Sabina, on a cliff on the left bank of the Tiber: the castle, mentioned by the second half of the 10th century, controlled the river port and the crossing of the Via Flaminia; destroyed in 1241 in the war between Rome and Viterbo and rebuilt, was then the Orsini. Today the castle is a private residence that hosts cultural events; in the tunnels dug into the rock there is a wellness path.
Woods and views of Montefeltro.

Borgo della Baronia on a limestone hill, among the most beautiful villages in Italy, dominated by the Castle of the Fava; at its foot the valley of the river Posada, inside the park of Tepilora, and long beaches such as Su Tiriarzu and San Giovanni di Posada.
The view of the chestnut groves of Gennargentu.
Theatre that hosts prose, dance and concert seasons.

Inaugurated in 2003, it connects in an itinerary the ancient monuments inserted in the urban fabric: Volcei had a city walls in travertine at the end of the fourth century BC and is known mainly for the Roman phase; you can visit the temple of Via S. Spirit called Caesareum and a public building of imperial age with mosaic floors in Via Canali. Free access every day.
Brunelleschi's last masterpiece.
A basilica linked to the Roman memory of the city.

One of the oldest Jewish settlements in Italy, never closed in ghetto: steep stairs descend from the houses to a central court and narrow passages connect the houses. The ancient synagogue houses the Jewish Museum, called the House of Spirits, for the legend of sudden noises that caused the inhabitants to flee.

Built in the second half of the fifteenth century on the west side of Piazza Mazzini, in front of Sant'Erasmo; the façade has a loggia with a coffered ceiling and on the first floor four windows and the balcony. The council room, with painted ceiling, in the nineteenth century was used as a theatre. It houses the Municipal Art Collection with works from the twentieth century linked to Castel Goffredo and, in the stairwell, a sculpture by Ferruccio Bolognesi.

On the hill of San Michele Arcangelo, the place of origin of the city, it was one of the most important fortresses of Umbria: built in the twelfth century and rebuilt by Frederick II in 1247, in the middle of the sixteenth century it became residence of the papal legates and in 1888 prison, before the recent restoration. The Civic Museum has three sections: archaeology from prehistory to the early Middle Ages, ceramics above all nineteenth century inspired by the sixteenth-century majolica of Gubbio and Deruta, and picture gallery with the great polyptych of Niccolò di Liberatore called the pupil (1471), by San Francesco, and fifteenth-century works by Matteo da Gualdo. It is part of the museum's unique ticket (€6). Info: tel. 075 916078.
In the fourteenth-century Palazzo Pepoli, a multimedia path from the Etruscan Felsina to the present day, also designed for families.
Sulfural water under the sanctuary.

The municipal route touches the workshop of Beatrice Gaudenzi, heir of the Fabiani, coccari      Â"s uninterruptedly since 1730 Â," the workshop of Daniele Giombi on the ascent to the convent of Santa Vittoria, where you can see the manual processing of clay, and the laboratory of Giacomo Bonifazi on the provincial road, with essential objects related to use.

In the village of San Pantaleo, reachable from Via San Francesco: rebuilt in 1579 and enlarged in the seventeenth century, with cusp bell tower. A little further you will find Piazza Savona, the heart of the village.
Inside the archaeological park, built on a Roman cistern, it preserves vases, urns and sculptures found in the excavations between 1960 and 2005.
The Greek colony of Himera and its temple of victory.
Nicola da Penne's portals.
Two small churches linked to the festivals of the country.
Seen from the Amiata to the Argentario.
Countryside, farmhouses and fountains at the gates of Milan.
The salon frescoed by Tiepolo in a villa in Massari.
A unique story in the world.
Wood with wooden statues and picnic area, and easy summer walk along the Ru Courtod.
History, panorama and museums on the hill.

Ethnographic museum in the former restored school of the village Miroglio: reconstructs domestic interiors and old crafts of the first half of the twentieth century with about 600 tools and objects of peasants and mountaineers. Open only by reservation (tel. +39 0174 244481).
A unique collection of ex-vote, with a view of the city.
The largest dovecote in Salento.

Country on the slopes of Monte Alpi on the Lucanian side of the Pollino National Park, known for the thermal baths and caves of Calda inhabited by the prehistory, the MULA+ museum pole and the works of Anish Kapoor and Michelangelo Pistoletto in the thermal park.
The Roman roots of the city, under the patron church.
A few steps from Piazza del Popolo, 2,000 square meters of interactive installations for children from 0 to 11 years, on science, sustainability, art and human body.
The 18th century inlaid furnishings in the church.
One of the most famous beaches on the Riviera di Roma, between Torvajanica and Lavinio.

Opened in 2019 on the noble floor of Palazzo Montani Antaldi: ten rooms of different colors follow the life of Rossini, with the composer's Pleyel piano in the Hall of Mirrors, paintings, scores, sets and videos.

Benedictine monastery founded according to tradition at the beginning of the 8th century by three Beneventan nobles, Paldo, Taso and Tato, at the springs of Volturno; placed by Charlemagne under his protection in 787, under the abbots Joshua, Talarico and Epifanio became a monastic city with about ten churches and about 350 monks, until the 881 raid devastated it. The archaeological park preserves the remains of the monastic city of the IX century, San Vincenzo Minore with the Crypt of Epifanio and its high medieval frescoes, in which the abbot appears among saints and angels, and the basilica of San Vincenzo Maggiore, rebuilt in the twentieth century, with the ring crypt of Joshua. The state archaeological complex, on the border with Castel San Vincenzo, is closed on Mondays (ticket reduced to €3 from 13 March 2026 until the completion of the works on the barriers).
A walk through the palaces of the bishop's city Sabina.

The parish church, with a basilica plan, was built in the early seventeenth century and has been renovated several times; tradition links its origins to the lordship of the Dorias (XIV century). In one of its chapels, the diocesan museum houses the retablo of San Giorgio, the largest in Sardinia, with 54 plates in 14 separable sections painted at the end of the sixteenth century by the anonymous Master of Perfugas, together with a fourteenth-century Madonna, a 16th-century crucifix, a reliquary cross and wooden carvings, silver, remains of a Sardinian female costume of the seventeenth-seventh-century and, from the archive, the parchment of the consecration of Santa Vittoria of 1120 and the fourteenth-century one which appoints Bishop Nicolaus Galuleiu, the oldest known of the diocese of Ampurias.
A section set up in the town hall exhibits some paintings by Matteo Olivero, a painter born in Pratorotondo, who formed at the Albertina Academy in Turin and close to the divisionism of Segantini.

A circular church designed by Palladio at the end of his career, around 1580 by Marcantonio Barbaro, who wanted to give Maser a new parish church; it rises at the foot of the villa, oriented to the east, and the frieze shows the date 1580 with the names of the client and the architect. Tradition has it that Palladio died in Maser that year. You can see with the guided tour between Villa and Tempietto (Saturday, Sunday and Holidays, 1 hour and 15 minutes).
Theatre 18th century recently restored after years of abandonment.
The viewpoint of romantic legend.
The neighborhood on the edge of the market of Ballarò, triumph of the baroque.
Sanctuary 450 meters high, built on an ancient pagan temple.
The church of the saint of Assisi.

Over ten kilometres of largely free beaches; Marina di Patti is the seaside and nightlife center, with the bars of the promenade and the summer breakfast with granite and brioche, while Mongiove is a seaside village suitable for a bath.
the MiC card indicates the closed area every day; the Ticino Park indicates visits with authorized guides (tel. 02 972101)
The lake from above.
Panoramic point on the Murgia, beyond the Gravina, from which you can see the Sassi in front.
Archaeology of water between mills and mills.
discordant times: the MiC card indicates Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday 9-18 and Saturday morning, the guide of the City weekend or by reservation
open only for guided tours, check with the Superintendence

In 1310 ten Augustinian nuns gathered there to follow the rule of Chiara da Norcia, next to the chapel of Sant'Agnese; damaged by the earthquake of 1703 and reopened in 1715, the church was confiscated with the suppressions of 1866. It has a singular eggplant generated by four braided equilateral triangles.
Modern art in the center, close to the sea.
The ethnographic collection.
The Palace of Montefeltro and the findings of Forum Sempronii.
Old-fashioned carriages.
Prehistoric stones along the ancient road to Taranto.
The Romanesque of Anglona at the entrance of the village.
The small medieval village of Leccia with the chapel of the Madonna del Latte, celebrated on June 14th.

Founded in 1040 by the bishop of Novara Riprando with the accounts of Biandrate and entrusted to the Benedictines, it was fortified in the 13th century near a ford of Sesia: there remain sections of moat and walls and three of the four corner towers. The Romanesque church has a two-storey atrium and a pebble bell tower with fishbone; the 15th-century Gothic-Lombard church has a hut façade with rosette and three naves, and the fifteenth-century cloister preserves a cycle of frescoes on the life of St. Benedict. Among the frescoes of the church, Santa Caterina and San Rocco of 1480 attributed to Giovanni Antonio Merli; open every day from 8:30 to sunset.
MiC card indicates closed every day; check opening

Panoramic view of the rocky slope at Stulles with views of Moso and the bottom of the Val Passiria: two structures in the shape of garnet, inspired by the rocks of the area, are an exhibition hall and a panoramic platform and tell the highest waterfall in South Tyrol, the country with the highest birth rate in Europe and the most haystack. Managed by the MuseumHinterPasseier.
The Roman port under the sea.
A 14th-century tower leads to the valleys.
Borgo on a tufa spur above the Neto valley, which at dawn looks like a large stone ship: the Norman castle with the museum, the Byzantine Baptistery and the Cathedral of St. Anastasia.

Municipality of Cilento coast in the Cilento National Park, Vallo di Diano and Alburni, between hilly villages of medieval plant and the coast of Agnone, Capitello and Baia Arena: to see the Marchesal tower of Orthodox, the Lucanian site of the Hill of the Cross and the panoramic stretch of the Red Ripe.

Valnerina municipality divided between the perched capital, with medieval walls, civic tower, the former monastery of San Giacomo and the Ciarlatano Museum, and the hamlets of Borgo Cerreto, Ponte and Triponzo, where sulphurous waters flow known since the Roman age.

Born in 1981 by the Archaeological Group Reunia led by Antonio Cerutti, on the ground floor of the Cultural Center: naturalistic section on the morainic amphitheatre of Tagliamento and on the ecosystems of the river and lake of Ragogna, with dioramas; archaeological section from the Mesolithic to the nineteenth century, with lithic instruments of the lake, an axe in serpentine, a fibula with bronze knight (II-III century), Lombard reliefs, the holy water-capitello of San Remigio (XI-XII century) and coins from the Roman age in Venice. Different times between MiC and Municipality: to be checked.

Until the nineteenth century Vigo was the administrative center of the valley, seat of justice, assemblies and religious power; it is a village spread in six hamlets, among the most beautiful villages since 2017. In Valle the barns, including the oldest of Vigo (1606); in Costa a large fountain with three wash-houses; in Larzonei a house with two bread-ovens; in Tamion, the highest hamlet, the church of the Trinity of 1708; in Vallonga the eighteenth-century church of San Giovanni Nepomuceno. A ring of about 3 hours, suitable for all, touches churches and barns with views of Rodella, Sassolungo and Sassopiatto.
The Etruscans of Sinalunga.
Digged under the hill of the castle, it remained almost intact since World War II, when it protected the population from bombing.
The palace of Francesco di Giorgio Martini.
Two centuries of phones, most of them working.

Built in 1559 and profoundly remodelled in the last decade of the eighteenth century, it was annexed to a shelter for the poor and travellers then demolished, hence the name. Small temple with square plan with table on two levels marked by pilasters; today it is in convenient to the Municipality. Tel. 0831 955236.

It extends from Fossalon to the island of Amphora, between canals and the straw-roofed cottages once inhabited by fishermen; remains of a submerged Roman road connected Aquileia to the port of Grado. Tamerics, poplars, junipers and pine trees; seagulls, herons, germans and terns. It is explored with boat excursions.
Protected natural area along the Po. The municipality suggests trails in the countryside towards the Po Park, the Bosco for the City and the villages La Gorra, Campagnino and Brillante.
only guided tours, season from 6 April to 8 November 2026 (Tuesday and Thursday 10.30 and 14.30, Sunday 10.30); off-season by reservation

Borgo dell'Alta Gallura, known for the Mineral Museum, has been active since 1984 with 800 specimens of minerals; in the village the seventeenth-century parish church of San Nicola di Bari and other eighteenth-century churches, in the surroundings the rocks carved by the wind of Punta Salizi and the domu de janas of Tisiennari.
The house where tradition wanted lived Boccaccio, rebuilt after the war, with the fresco of Pietro Benvenuti, the library and the panoramic tower.
A nineteenth-century example of industrial archaeology on the Serio.
The village nestled among the rocks.

From the upper part of the village a dirt road climbs through the meadows of Monte Calvario; the trail T1 of the Park continues on the ridge of Monte Rotella to Rocca Pia (about 14 km, 5 hours, difficulty EE), with views of the plateaus of the Quarto del Barone and the Quarto Grande, the Plan of the Five Miglia, the mountains of the Parco d'Abruzzo and the Bosco di Sant'Antonio. For the mountain bike there is the mountain bike ring MTB 47 of Monte Calvario (10.1 km, difficult).
See a water sawmill at work.

In the former regulation sawmill, he tells with objects and images the Rules, the centuries-old collective property of the Cortina valley: traditional heritage, management of woods and pastures and the link between the community and the territory.

Section of Paciano of the museum system of the archdiocese of Perugia-Città della Pieve, born from an idea by Don Aldo Rossi of 1994. In the church of San Giuseppe (XII century, partly rebuilt in the eighteenth century), restored, you can see votive frescoes, wooden statues, liturgical furnishings, a gonfalone of Bonfigli's workshop, a painting by Francesco Appiani and an organ by Adamo Rossi from 1795.

In the area of the sanctuary there are still the rooms of a Roman villa of the III-IV century AD, belonging to important families of the Roman town of Terventum: the excavations have brought to light polychrome mosaics and containers for the conservation of oil and wine.
The court of the Malatesti, stage in summer.
One of the great views of the Dolomites, within reach of cable car.

Begin in 1306 at the behest of Tommaso Sanseverino, Count of Marsico, and expanded until the nineteenth century mainly Baroque: facade of the church of 1718, Cloister Grande of 1690 with 84 arches, elliptical staircase of 1761-1763, the historical kitchen; the monks left it in 1807. In the rooms the archaeological museum of western Lucania and, in the cells, a collection of contemporary art. Open 9-19.30, closed on Tuesdays.

Kilometers of white sand and clear water on the Gulf of Squillace, awarded with Blue Flag and Green Flag; the beach is pet friendly and in the free stretches the rescue is carried out by Labrador of the SICS dogs units. Lidi equipped with services and sports activities.
The six-hour watch with a single hand.
Museum and international center of study and research on local musical tradition, dedicated to Celestino Coscia and Antonio Bocchino.
A crypt in the buildings.
The eighteenth century Venetian in a baroque building.

Founded in 1978, it has saved from demolition more than 60 rotabili between locomotives, automotors and carriages, on an external area of approximately 31,500 m2 around a rotating platform of 21 meters, with two sections covered of railway material, models and dioramas; exchanges and tracks are working. It recalls the connection with Turin of 1855 and the industrial railway tradition of the city. Open on weekends with seasonal hours.
Octagonal construction of the XIII-XIV century; it is said to be the first public clock of Piedmont.
In the district of San Nicola, tells the ancient Agrigento from prehistory to Hellenization with over 5,000 finds; the strong piece is the Telamone over 7 meters high.

Set up in the Seminary in 1930 with fossils collected by Antonio Stoppani, geological collections of Giuseppe Mercalli and shells, titled to Stoppani in 1952: 104 windows with almost 6,000 finds among zoology (about 1,400 naturalized animals, including a great crocodile of the Nile), paleontology (about 2,500 fossils for geological era, total collection over 12,000 pieces centered on the Lombard Triassic), geology and mineralogy and archaeology. It offers educational routes for schools.

Birthplace of Abbot Gioacchino da Fiore, at the gates of Sila: tradition places his birthplace under the church of the Assumption and his baptism in the parish of San Michele Arcangelo; the territory reaches to Lake Cecita, where grows a chestnut of about five centuries tied to San Francesco di Paola.

Among the oldest inhabited places in Europe: the National Museum of the Paleolithic on the deposit of Isernia La Pineta, and in the historic center the Cathedral on the Italic temple, the Arch of St. Peter, the museum of Santa Maria delle Nunche and the Fraternal Fountain.

Founded in 1998 by the Naturalistic Group Paleontophile (GNP) and the Municipality, it collects hundreds of fossils of the Quaternary recovered along the banks of the Po: remains of about thirty species, including mammoth, megacero deer, bison and rhinoceros, and rare finds of leopard and spelean hyena. The most important piece is a Neanderthal Man's frontal bone nicknamed "Pàus" which is presented as an exceptional testimony of the species in the Po Valley. It is divided into four sections (paleontology, anthropology, mineralogy and didactics), with a wing dedicated to the findings of the Po beaches. Open Tuesday-Friday 8-13 only by reservation with one day in advance and Sunday 14-19; closed Monday, Saturday, August and on the main holidays; accessible to those who have difficulty in walking.
Built in the mid-nineteenth century at the Tagliamento on the site of a sixteenth-century votive ancona, it was wanted by the rafts to protect the loads transported along the river.

The castle has existed since at least the 12th century, on the site of a Roman fortress, and it was expanded mainly between the 14th and 15th centuries; it includes several buildings decorated with friezes and frescoes. The "salotto" of the village, a civil and religious centre. Building of the late eighteenth century, already documented as church of San Biagio in the early seventeenth century, with facade in local granite. In the nave the marble statues of St. John the Baptist, St. Stephen, St. Bruno and the Virgin with the Child from the ancient Certosa and two bas-reliefs of David Müller of 1611; in the choir the Martyrdom of St. Stephen by Bernardino Poccetti (1608 about) and the Trinity with Carthusian saints by Francesco Caivano (1633). It preserves an 11th century reliquary rebuilt in the 18th century, which tradition wants to donate from Adelaide del Vasto to San Bruno.

Inside the cellar of the Tessari family, in a farmhouse of the first post-war period, exhibits more than 150 tools used in a century of vinification and follows the path from the arrival of the grape in the threshing area to the aging and bottling in the caneval; it is recognized of regional interest. On the hill between Cella and Agrons, it is already mentioned in 1119 in the act of foundation of the abbey of Moggio and the site could go back to the eighth century; on the same hill stood the castle of Agrons, of which the isolated bell tower would be a tower. After the fire of 1430 it was rebuilt from 1431 by the foreman Stefano di Simone di Mena and enlarged in 1722 by the brothers Zamolo of Portis; it is a basilica with three naves on stone pillars, with frescoes of the XII-XIII centuries with the parable of the ten virgins and a rich set of liturgical objects. Visits on request, every day.

One of the four castles of the municipality, built by the Cortesi Counts; today it houses the Town Hall and the Museum of Resistance. From the castle the view widens from the Apennines to the Adriatic sea.

House of writer and traveler Freya Stark (1893-1993), who transformed the garden into a botanical garden with plants collected during the trips; in the park the remains of the Roman theatre of ancient Acelum, discovered in 1879 and dug in the nineties by the University of Padua; restoration completed in 2012.

117 meters high of the isontian Karst, in front of the shrine of Redipuglia, between Fogliano Redipuglia and Ronchi dei Legionari, the scene of bloody fighting in the Great War; a non-binding walk touches the remains of the Dolina of the XV Bersaglieri, open-air museum, and the Mazzoldi trench with inscriptions and engraved drawings. Founded around 1133 by San Guglielmo da Vercelli, who died there in 1142, as a community of monks and nuns led by an abbess; after the earthquake of 1732 Domenico Antonio Vaccaro built the Great Church (1733-40), today in ruins, and with the suppression of 1807 the complex fell until its rebirth in the second twentieth century with Father Lucio Maria De Marino and the Little Brothers of Jesus. Inside the walls, two cloisters, the defensive tower of 1152 built with blocks of a Roman mausoleum, the lower Romanesque church with two naves (XII century) and the upper church of San Luca, begun in 1247 and completed in 1255 under the abbess Marina II, with frescoed medallions. In the former restored Granatic Mountain, it tells of a thousand years of encounters and especially clashes between two worlds, from the 8th to the 18th century, with the incursions of the barbarian pirates at the center; it takes its cue from the inscription in the country church of São Paulo that recalls the destruction of the nearby village of Uras by the Barbarossa in 1515. Multimedia panels, interactive video portraits and life-size holograms, reconstructions of coastal towers and bridges of ships, dioramas, models and vintage weapons, digital reproduction of the retablo of Lorenzo Cavaro and a section on the disappeared village of Serzela. Accessible to the blind and disabled, with educational workshops.

Itinerary on the track opened by the Alps in the early twentieth century, the scene of violent fighting in the First World War, today also of geological interest for dinosaur footprints near the Casavento cabin.

Built in 1825 by the architect Sacchetti, with Baroque and neoclassical influences, where in 1587 there was a small church; it houses the wooden crucifix of Fra' Umile da Petralia donated to the city in 1666 and paintings by Luigi Lo Jacono (1843) and Domenico Provenzano (1902).

Discovered in 1840 by Antonio Federico Lindner, it was opened to the public in 1908 with stairs, walkways and candlelight and then acetylene; the electric lighting came in 1957. The Great Hall measures 389 metres in length, 65 metres in width and 107 metres in height, with the Ruggero Column 12 metres high, the Hall of the Altar and, towards the exit, the skeleton of a cave bear; a seismographic station with large pendulums measures the effects of the tides and the underground floods. On the tower of the Palazzo Comunale, the planetary clock completed in 1583 by Pietro Fanzago: a single hand, turning counterclockwise on a 24-hour dial, and three rotating discs indicate hours, days, months, zodiac signs, duration of day and night and moon phases. Cathedral of the diocese of Tempio-Ampurias, behind the Town Hall: the first church is of the first thirteenth century, rebuilt between 1832 and 1839 and then reconsecrated. The history of the territory from prehistory to the Roman era: weapons, stone instruments, ceramic and glass vases and metal objects from Monte Cila, Roccavecchia di Pratella and from the necropolis, a part of fresco of IV style from a domus on the decuman and fragments of Roman mosaics; there are also coins, jewels and skylights from the excavations of the cryptoportico.

Fortified village on the Gulf of Asinara, founded by the Dorias as Castelgenovese, then Castel Aragonese and from the eighteenth century Castelsardo: the castle with the Museo dell'Intreccio Mediterraneo, the Cathedral of Sant'Antonio Abate overlooking the sea, the fourteenth-century Santa Maria delle Grazie with the Black Christ and, in the surroundings, the Rock of the Elephant with its domus de janas, UNESCO Heritage since 2025.
