First Norman cathedral of Sicily, probably born as the first church of the Latin rite after the expulsion of the Arabs and became cathedral in 1082, when Troina had the first bishopric of the island; it has a beautiful Norman tower. The Oratory of the SS. Sacramento replaces the crypt and transept and the Oratory of the Whites, under the church, preserves the predella d'altar on which Pope Urban II celebrated Mass in 1088.

In the shrine are preserved little less than a thousand tablets ex-vote painted in about a century, between 1870 and 1970: accidents, especially road accidents, with means that pass from animal towing to cars and trucks, diseases such as cholera and Spanish and surgical scenes from the bed of the house to the operating room. The Sicilian Region has studied them in the volume "Miracles to the front"

A hilly village at the foot of Monte Conero, home of the seventeenth-century painter Carlo Maratti, famous for the Caves, an underground network excavated in the sandstone under the old town; among churches with works of Maratti and vineyards of Rosso Conero, the sea is just a few minutes away.

On the watershed between the Lanzo Valleys and the Susa Valley, it tells the history of the Resistance and the events that took place in this territory with films shot with witnesses, CD-ROMs, touring exhibitions and brochures on the routes; the territory of the Ecomuseum has returned to live through rediscovered paths and offers wide views.

In the premises of the primary school, managed with the Centro Studi Storici Alta Valle Scrivia, exhibits fossils collected over the years between the Antola and Aveto mountains, to make the territory better known to those who live or frequent the valleys of the Ligurian central Apennines. The finds cover the ages from the Cretaceous beyond the Miocene and come mostly from deep sea environments.
15th-century frescoes and a baroque marble in chestnut wood.
The place of worship surrounded by nature near the village, among the points of interest indicated by the tourist portal of Modena.
Protected natural area marked by the APT among the places to see in Pergine.

After the medieval walls, rebuilt from 1185 and completed in 1199 with 21 towers, four towers and the gates of Ombriano, Pianengo, Serio and Ripalta, Venice surrounded the city with new walls between 1488 and 1508, of which remain significant vestiges around the historic center. Porta Ombriano and Porta Serio were rebuilt with ornamental function between 1804 and 1807.

Common at the entrance of the Brembana Valley in the Parco dei Colli di Bergamo, mentioned already in 927 and in 1025 as "Villa Lemensis": on the hills the rural hamlets of Bruntino, San Mauro and Foresto, in the village the eighteenth-century parish church of the Saints Faustino and Giovita and the Civic Museum of Natural Sciences "Severo Sini" .
Two hundredth century walls on the border of the Duchy of Urbino.
On the first floor of the Opera Carlo Alberto, interactive space to discover the Alpine world with the five senses.
Country of the lower Lys valley at the gates of the Mont Mars Nature Reserve, between lakes, peat bogs and the historic procession towards Oropa.
The wooded volcanic plateau of the hinterland of Algherese.
A garden between vineyards and medieval walls.

Arbëreshe del Pollino country, founded by Albanian refugees in the fifteenth century, which preserves Byzantine rite and language: the museum of icons, that of dolls and costumes and, in the hamlet of Eianina, a rock chapel of the Basilian monks.
A karst cave with thousands of bats.
Granite and wrought iron of the serresi masters.
The historical context that makes the frescoes of San Procolo understand.
Check with the museum
The largest public park in Florence along the right bank of the Arno, with avenues to walk or by bike, large meadows, the Cornacchie Amphitheatre and a weekly market.

On the southern side of the hill, above the Platani (the ancient Halykos), more than two hundred tombs dug into the rock between the 13th and the 6th century BC, cave and tholos: a long corridor leads to a circular chamber with convex vault. The place is linked to the myth of Camico, the king of Sicily Kokalos and Daedalo; from here comes the group of goldsmiths most important of the indigenous Sicily, with a patera today at the British Museum.
The village and its sanctuary told in four halls.
Yes, time slots (online or at the Infopoint in Piazza Maggiore)

A small town on the western shore of Lake Bracciano, dominated by the Castle Orsini-Odescalchi of the fifteenth century; in the village the Civic Museum in the former convent of Santa Maria Novella, on the lake in Vigna di Valle the Historical Museum of the Air Force and in the countryside the church of San Liberato with the garden of Russell Page.
The monumental baroque with the canvases of the Ligars.
On the trail of Beniamino Gigli.
An outdoor stop with picnic on the lake shore.

Romanesque chapel built around 1210 by Provençal workers next to the domus hospitalis founded around 1165 by the Knights Hospitallers for pilgrims and travelers direct to the Monginevro; dedicated first to St. John the Baptist, around 1250 passed to St. Catherine of Alexandria. Restored, it preserves fourteenth-century frescoes and the baroque altar wanted at the end of the seventeenth century by the prevosto Fantin. Visits by reservation (tel. This appropriation is intended to cover the expenditure of the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF).

Of Romanesque origins, it was consecrated in 1076 on an area considered sacred for centuries and rebuilt several times after earthquakes. The Renaissance façade dates back to 1905, with a portal in carved stone from the 13th century; the Baroque interior, rebuilt in the 18th century, measures 50 by 25 metres and has a major altar in polychrome marble of 1740.
A stone bridge made by nature.
The murals of the ArtU festival, starting from the station.
The civilization of the table grain, next to the grain pits.
Ancient fortified village in an almost alpine landscape, among meadows and mountain vegetation.

The large gravina that encircles two thirds of the country is the largest in the province and one of the deepest in Puglia, with a jump of almost 150 meters. In its caves, probably in the 10th century, the peasants of the nearby farmhouses took refuge to defend themselves against pirate raids: the houses and the rock churches date back to the origins of the country.
The fountain of Aretusa and Alpheus.
The lava wood where in 1537 Annibal Caro disappeared.

Inaugurated in 1982 on the ground floor of the medieval Palazzo Papale di Martino IV, the Etruscan Orvieto recounts with the furnishings of the necropolis of Crocifisso del Tufo, Cannicella, Poggio Ginestra and Porano; there are rebuilt the Tombs Golini of the IV century BC, with scenes of banquet and funeral rites, and a room dedicated to the Federal sanctuary of the Etruscans.
The first Crivelli of the Marches.
The place of pilgrimage of Natuzza Evolo.
Church in the center of the village, with Romanesque bell tower, founded before the ninth century by the family of the noble Eremberto, linked to the Emperor Lotario.

Ancient parish church mentioned already in the 12th century, passed from Romanesque forms to a 16th century Gothic architecture, with 17th century bell tower, valuable wooden altars and a painting by Paolo Naurizio.

The town of Lessinia in the upper Val d'Illasi, where you can still hear the  "tàucias garéida": in Giazza the Cimbri Museum tells the people of Bavarian-Tyrolean origins settled on these mountains between the XII and XIV century, in San Bortolo delle Montagne the old church houses the Museum of Trumpets, and the Cyclopedonale of Val d'Illasi goes up the Progno up to the forest of Giazza.

The imposing rocky massif, whose profile is interrupted by four ridges that descend into ravines; the peaks, the "morconia" rise for more than two hundred meters on the valley and once made it inaccessible. On the northern and eastern slopes remain powerful but fragmentary traits of the Sannitic walls of the third century BC; from above they are seen with the naked eye twenty-eight common. Always accessible.
The loggia with its succession of arches and the Clock Tower, which in medieval times was the bastion of access to the castle.
Ridolfi and Barocci's school in Colbordolo.

The birthplace of the painter Innocent Salvini (1889-1979), who lived and worked all his life here, is a rare example of industrial archaeology of the seventeenth century with remains of an ancient medieval tower: two wheels and working gears moved by the stream Viganella, millstones, sieves and systems of wheat transport designed and automated by Salvini himself. Since 1983 it is a gallery: three rooms with rotating paintings with warm and bright colors on rural life, family and landscapes of the village, and frescoes en plein air in the courtyard; it houses exhibitions and events. Open from 1 April to 30 October Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday 15-18.
Brando and the treasures of the sea of Santo Janni.
The Parmigianino in a water castle.

Quadrangular watchtower of the sixteenth century, isolated on the headland of Capo di Conca, built to spot Saracen pirates; until about fifty years ago it was used as a small cemetery. Visitable by reservation.

An island of about 50 hectares, at most 100 meters high, in front of Cape of the Arena; the erosion dug the caves of Monaco, the Sardines (with stalagmites), the Waterfalls, the Lion and the Blue Grotto, the largest, with intensely coloured water and ancient marine fossils on the walls. You reach it by boat, canoe or pedal boat, and the seabed are rich in flora and fauna of natural interest.
Rationalist city built in the thirties, stopped in 1940: Piazza della Rivoluzione in the shape of D, pastel-coloured buildings and the former public bathrooms with the inscription SOGNI.
A unique water square in Italy.

The villa purchased in 1817 by Ferdinando di Borbone for the Duchess of Floridia, with the English park of Antonio Niccolini, the theater of verzura, the Ionic temple and the view on the gulf; free entrance to the park.

The nineteenth-century garden on the Gambacorta Plan, belonged to the Capuchins, with plane trees planted around 1850, large Figus magnolioides, pines and palm trees, the busts of Garibaldi (1883) and Vittorio Emanuele II (1866) of Civiletti and an amphitheatre for the band.

Between Sesia and Ticino, between plains and rice fields, the city of the dome of San Gaudenzio di Alessandro Antonelli, with the early Christian baptistery, the Broletto and the Visconteo-Sforzesco Castle.

Country church at the crossroads for Montegiorgio and Francavilla d'Ete, lambita dall'Ete Morto; the first stone was placed on November 11, 1579 by the bishop of Fermo and the management entrusted to the brotherhood of the SS. Sacrament with bubble of Gregory XIII.
You go down into an Etruscan hydraulic work.

Documented as early as 917, it is the only remnant of the ancient settlement of Paciano Vecchio; the name ties it to the Paladino Orlando of Charlemagne. As a noble residence, it is now privately owned: you can see along the panoramic walk from Porta Perugina towards Panicale.
Snorkeling and diving between granite, posidonia and wrecks.
The elegant shopping.

In the fort Carlo Emanuele III, erected in the spring of 1738: the first building in masonry of the village, first guard and then prison. Six rooms and a garden: the trap room with tools and plastic, that of the gallantrymen (the boatmen carrying the ore), documents of the first colonization, a malacological collection, the peasant tools and the paintings of Mario Emanuelli.

Municipality between the Selva di Fasano and the sea, with the historic center of the Church Mother of St. John and Piazza Ciaia, the Archaeological Park and National Museum of Egnazia in Savelletri, the rock park of Lama d'Antico and the coast of Torre Canne in the Park of the Dune Costiere.
The prehistoric and Greek Trebisacce.
The red lake sung by Virgil.
A page of social history inside an ancient convent.
One of the masterpieces of 19th century military engineering in the Alps.

Borgo della Riviera dei Cedri on the border with Basilicata, in the territory of the ancient Blanda conquered by the Romans in 214 BC: the medieval historical center perched around the castle, with the belvedere on the squares, and the Antiquarium of Palazzo Casapesenna with the finds of the territory.
The hamlet in the rock.
MiC card (updated 2020) indicates "closed" every day: check (tel. 0771 80108)
With its origins in the VI-VII century, it was transformed several times until the end of the sixteenth century and restored last time in 1930. Open every day 9-18.
The "Castellaccio" (Castellaccio), whose original nucleus dates back to the 11th century, beyond the area of Bousc Daré.

In a farmhouse in the Padule di Fucecchio, founded by the Dei family and in the regional museum network since 2012: agricultural machines and tools, everyday objects, books, photographs, documents and postcards to tell the link between landscape, field work and domestic life, with educational activities for adults and children.

The old town has many historical monuments and residences: the typical  "curti" (curti), many small churches and palaces Bari, Calabrese, Catarozzolo, Maddalo, Magi and Occhineri, as well as the brand residence.
The Baroque of the Capitannata church after church.
The EUR Ministry of Economic Development Museum dedicated to the history of post and telecommunications.
Masterpieces from Tiziano to Morandi in a villa in the green.
Built in the 13th century by Malatesta and rebuilt in baroque forms.
The ferry and cruise terminal designed by Zaha Hadid after the 1999 competition, inspired by an oyster, reported in 2013 by the Ministry among the architectural interventions of high quality.
The oldest part of the city, where a well was dug to irrigate the lands between the rivers Idria and Longano; a document from 1463 links these lands to the Messinian Nicolò Goto.
Tiepolo and the Alps from the hill.
The Arab dome and the baroque forum.
Walk between sea and city.

Along the Alpine valley on the border with Austria, linked to the copper mine of Predoi, which is visited with the train, and to the granary of Cadipietra with the collection Enzenberg; at the end of the valley the church of Santo Spirito in Casere, stop of those who crossed the Tauri.

Established in 1983 and opened in 1989, it has its core in the ornithological collection begun by Angelo Priolo in 1939: about 2,000 specimens of about 400 species, precious for the study of Sicilian birdfauna, with extinct species on the island such as the Francoline and the latea. The geological collection of Luigi Lino includes fossils, minerals, rocks and shells especially Sicilian, pleistocene fauna, volcanic products of Etna and fossil fish; the diorama of the valley of the Rosemary stream stands out, from which the griffins disappeared in 1965 by poisoning and where they were re-introduced with LIPU and Nebrodi Park.
"Parva sed apta mihi": the house of the Furious.

Exhibitions in the palaces of the Gesualdian aristocracy.
The curious locomotive that welcomes visitors.
The morainic lake.

A medieval castle still inhabited.
The miraculous fountain.

A noble residence built at the end of the fifteenth century and transformed into a Renaissance court, frequented by artists, writers and philosophers; it was the Besta until 1726, then divided and used as a farm, bought by the State in 1911 and opened as a museum in 1927. The courtyard has a double loggia on frescoed columns with episodes of the Eneide and medallions of the owners; on the noble floor the salon of honor with the Orlando Furioso, the dining room with ceiling umbrella and the Hall of Creation with stories of Genesis; on the second floor frescoes from other sites Valtellina, Stüe and an ethnographic collection. On the ground floor the Antiquarium Tellinum with engraved stem of the Copper Age (III millennium BC) found in Teglio since 1940, including the Mother Goddess of Caven. Tours from 35 to 75 minutes, also for families and accessible.
The plastic orchard.

High altitude lakes with crystal clear water between rhododendrons, cembri and clear boulders, reached with a challenging excursion that starts from the Val di Scaleres, valley of high mountain intact above Varna.
Orchids, climbing and panoramas.
The last door of the medieval walls.
The underground Turin.
By bike on the sea along the old railroad.
In Via Carducci, with thirteen windows per floor, a sculpted bicaudato siren and a plaque to the aeronautical companies of Count Almerico da Schio.
A sixteenth-century ruin in the vegetation.
The place where Frederick II died.
A pagan temple under a basilica.
The alpine life of an Alpine valley.

The ancient Aristanis, the capital of the judge of Arborea: the tower of Mariano of 1290, the Antiquarium Arborense with the finds of Tharros, the cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, the Gothic of Santa Chiara and, on the sea, the largest Spanish tower in Sardinia.
The most scenic path in Sestri.
Rebuilt at the end of the nineteenth century, it was the headquarters of the Polyptych by Carlo Crivelli; in the sacristy a seventeenth-century canvas by Sebastiano Grezzi di Comunanza.
Ancient frames and theater coatboards in a still alive factory.
The twentieth century Bergamo in images.

An eighteenth-century church whose bell tower is what remains of the Romanesque parish church demolished around 1570; it preserves wooden works by Luchini and a altarpiece by Francesco Barbieri (1687). For three days a year, at the beginning of Lent, on the high altar is set up the machine of the triduum, eighteenth-century wood scenery painted with 365 candles.
A walk in the city reborn after 1783.

Municipality of the Malvaro valley, side of the Val Fontanabuona, on the slopes of Mount Pagliaro; here is the paternal house of Amedeo Pietro Giannini, son of Favalese emigrants and founder of the Bank of America and Italy, today the Museum of the Emigrant.

In the tourist hamlet about 10 km from the village, a long beach of fine ochre sand divided by the mouth of the Rio Mannu and closed by a cliff with natural pools; along the coast also the coves of Guardia is Turcus, Sa Perdixedda Manna and Sa Perdixedda Pittica.
Museum of rural life with a collection of historical objects related to the work of the fields and the food traditions of the territory.
The Renaissance face of the city.
The vacation rooms of the court.
The trails of the feud.

Centro dei Monti Picentini, the land of IGP chestnut, where the Calore river is born: the complex of San Francesco a Folloni, a national monument, the Sanctuary of Santissimo Salvatore at 954 meters, the Castle of Monte, the waterfalls of Calore and the plateau of Verteglia.
Accessible on foot or by bicycle through the orchards of the plain.

City on the Brenta at the foot of Mount Grappa: the Ponte degli Alpini covered in wood, symbol of the city and national monument, the Civic Museum with the largest collection of Jacopo Bassano and the Remondini prints of Palazzo Sturm.

The town of coral, the most populous center of the Vesuvius National Park: the Museum of Coral Liverino, the Roman villa of Villa Sora and, on the slopes, the Villa delle Ginestre where Leopardi stayed.
Ulysses' head and the Odyssey giants.
In the nineteenth century Villa Fabbricotti, in the center of the Parco della Padula, a permanent exhibition on three floors dedicated to the relationship between Michelangelo and Carrara marble.
The sanctuary wanted by Don Bosco.
Winter skiing and summer rock.
The myth of Attheon on Roman stones.
The park museum, with a section of prehistory and protohistory and the Greek paintings of the Tomb of the Diveper.
The symbol of the village, example of Renaissance architecture.
The walled village on the border with the Marches, with the fortress wanted by Galeotto Malatesta in the fourteenth century.
The oil from the valley.
One of the most visited Marian shrines in Emilia.
A black nuragic tower, almost intact.
It rises at the end of the 17th century on the area of a Farnesian bulwark and consecrated in 1722, with Baroque facade and inside a nave with dome.
The heart of the birthplace of Pius XI.
Small fifteenth-century church with frescoes from the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.
The Roman Eporedia.
An Etruscan city with its large mound graves.
Etruscan paintings still in their place.

In the cloister of the sanctuary: the polyptych of Zanino di Pietro, the Madonna of Humility by Andrea di Bartolo, the Meeting of Gioacchino and Anna of the second fifteenth century and, in church, a crucifix of 1320-1330. Visits on request.
The master's grave with the canovian medallion.
Park with fountains, chapels and panoramic views of the village, the lake and the mountains.

An ancient settlement founded by the Peligni in the locality Tavotto-Pantano, depopulated around the ninth century for the Saracen raids that pushed the inhabitants on a cliff further east. It is above all a sacred area with three cult buildings arranged on a two-level plateau at the foot of the Mitra Hill: an Italic temple of Hercules, a sanctuary of Jupiter and a small sacellus of a female deity, of which the perimeters have been carefully reconstructed. It can be reached about 5 km from the village on an asphalted country road and is close to the train stop of the Railway of the Parks, active since summer 2023 on weekends.

Stone houses, eighteenth-century buildings and medieval palaces with ogival windows; in the center are the basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore, the church of the Most Holy Savior with interiors in polychrome marble and majolica floors and the Doge's Palace, residence of the Gaetani d'Aragona (feudatarians from 1383 to 1806) rebuilt between 1700 and 1714. At the top there is a Gothic church dedicated to St. John, with views of the valley of Alife.
The carriages of a Piedmontese house.
The medieval arcades and the Lepanto of Claret.
Hidden pools and waterfalls.
The life of the fields of Salento in Torrepaduli.
Three hundred frescoes and a venerated crucifix.
Villa of Venetian neo-Gothic taste, with arches, Ionic columns, medallions and Gothic plumes; the catalog of the MiC the date between 1886 and 1915 and attributed it to Domenico Zerbi.
Historical villa with garden, inserted by the municipality among the gardens, villas and parks of the city.

About 7 km of Ionian coast along the Salento coast, between Marina di Pulsano and Torre Ovo: beyond the town, which reaches Torre Sgarrata, large beaches of clear sand and fine give water, in the days of tramontana, Caribbean nuances. Sandy backdrop in slow slopes, long stretches of free beach alternated with equipped beaches, and behind large dunes with protected Mediterranean maquis (ginepro cuddle), small marshes and pine forests and holm oaks; in the evening movida.
Getting lost in the alleys.
In 1625, built as a noble residence on the remains of a medieval fortress, it is the heart of the country: the arches of its splendid loggia connect it to the Matrix Church, next to which it rises.
The ibex, symbol of the Park, in a great historic hotel.

First mentioned in 1170 as Bitthe, the village has stone houses arranged amphitheater and connected by narrow alleys, developed around the parish church of San Giorgio martyr; in the center there is the legendary Fontana de su Cantaru.
The towers and walls of the castle of Barbarossa that hosted Petrarca.
The fortress on the sea at the entrance of the old town.
Castello dei marquisi Del Carretto from the 12th to the 14th century, restored by Genoese architects in 1522, with central mast and polygonal belt; the last refuge of the population.

Villa marittima d'otium of the Roman aristocracy, among the best preserved of the Tyrrhenian area: built in the early years of the first century A.D. (Julio-Claudia age) and in use until the 7th century, extends to the sea along the river Reginna Minor, on two or more floors around the triclinium-nympheo turned into a barrel, with mosaics of a hunting scene and a marine tiase. There are rooms decorated with stuccoes and frescoes and part of the viridarium surrounded by arcades and a large bathtub; discovered by chance in 1932, it was completely freed after the flood of 1954. On the terrace the Antiquarium displays frescoes, amphoras and finds of other villas in the area and excavations of Vietri and Tramonti.
The main church of the village, with its Norman origins.
The symbol of the main square.
A hamlet church grown for three centuries on the slopes of Etna.
Liberty building of 1900 rich in polychrome ceramics.

It was the ancient convent of Carmine, whose first stone was laid on 26 August 1480; entrance and portico are what remains of the nave of the Renaissance church of Carmine, of the early sixteenth century, and in the restorations of the façade a large fresco of the Madonna del Carmine has re-emerged. Between 1862 and 1864 Schellino rebuilt it by adding a third floor and the adjacent tower of the Cessi, among the first public toilets. Today it houses the municipality, the Gabetti Museum, the Einaudi Museum and, in the cellar, the Wine shop.

In the territory of Masullas the park of Monte Arci includes the Taraxi wood, the rocky wall of on Columbariu, the underwater lava formation of on Carongiu de Fanari, the split mass of Sa Perda Sperrada and the park of the obsidian of Conca 'e Cannas, the major Sardinian deposit of obsidian prehistoric, exploited by the 6th millennium BC. In the territory there are also the prenurgical menhirs of Sa Pedra Isposa and the remains of twelve nuraghi, including Su Para.
A geological curiosity about the Mongia stream.

Simple façade with rosette and a fresco by Imago Pietatis, 18th century bell tower in Lombard style. Inside the frescoes of the Three-Fourteenth century with the Passion of Christ, the Coronation of the Virgin by the Trinity and the life of St. Anthony Abbot; in the right chapel a wooden crucifix considered miraculous, in the left one the former vows.
The Gorizia art gallery.
Top of the Dolomites Queen.
The commercial heart.
One hundred works of the twentieth century on the theme of Marian.
Science and territory in a university museum.

The municipality takes its name from the Certosa founded in 1396 by Gian Galeazzo Visconti as a mausoleum of the Milanese dynasty, masterpiece between Gothic and Renaissance, with the museum set up in the Ducal Palace; an educational itinerary in the Visconteo Park connects it to the Visconti Castle of Pavia and next passes the cycle path of the Naviglio Pavese between Milan and Pavia.

At the gates of the ancient Capua, along the Appia street stands the Roman mausoleum of the Old Prisons; in the village the chapel of Santa Matrona preserves early Christian mosaics of the fifth century, and behind stands Mount Tifata, with the remains of the temple of Jupiter Tifatino.

The museum brings together five collections: one systematic, with the minerals sorted by class from the simplest to the most complex; one didactic, with the minerals from which the most common metals are extracted; one of the minerals found in the territory of Carro; one of hard and semi-precious stones; one of fluorescent minerals. Tel. 0187 861005.
Birthplace of the poet Vincenzo Monti, museum and information point of the Delta Park.
Transetto, Corridor of the Novitiate and Sacristy on a raised floor with steps

House of Cardinal Branda, built in two phases (the fourteenth-century wing and fifteenth-century joined by chapel and Renaissance loggia): the cardinal's room has Lombard frescoes of 1423, the study of the Hungarian Landscape of Masolino (1435), the chapel of San Martino the frescoes of the Vecchietta (1437-1439) rediscovered in the restoration of 1982; in the sixteenth-century picture the family portraits. The Civic Museum preserves the testimonies of the humanist thought of the cardinal, with frescoes and sculptures of Masolino and Vecchietta.
A Colonna hunting mess with a Roman tomb.
Among the oldest churches in Gravina and its first cathedral, dug into a single block of tuff between the 8th and 10th centuries at the end of the Fondovito district.
Church of the fourteenth century arose, according to legend, at the point where two German pilgrims who brought to Rome a table of the Madonna and Child were forced to stop.
Nature protected behind the dunes.
A 15th-century fresco and a May peasant party.
In the Priamàr Fortress, the museum dedicated to the collection donated by Sandro Pertini to his city and to the works of the sculptor Renata Cuneo.
A seismic observatory of the nineteenth century still in operation, where Marconi experimented.
From prehistoric times to Rome.
Romanesque of the 11th century on the way of pilgrims.
The village where Guerra lived the last years.

It rises where, between the third and fourth centuries, the martyr Saint Pellegrino was buried; the frescoes of the thirteenth century entirely cover vaults and walls. You visit by calling the number indicated on the gate.
Polychrome marbles in a village church.
The state museum with a polychrome wooden Madonna of Jacopo della Quercia, Robbian terracotta and a sixteenth-century table organ still working.
A rationalist city born around the factory.
Listing in extension: the guide covers 4 of the 5 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
A Lucanian town with orthogonal streets.
A nectar for a few.

Built in 1773 on the remains of a rural church older and saved from abandonment in 1947, it façade completed in the nineteenth century and inside baroque frescoed; it is often wrongly called Church of Saint Lucia.
Sanniti, archaeology and local history in a monastery of the fourteenth century.
Gagini marbles and the treasure in the crypt.
A castle in Casentino between tower, loggia and coats of arms.

In the nineteenth-century palace, at the Cantina Comunale dei Vini: the route starts from the study of the land of Costigliole, the "Città del Vino" and continues with the utensils of the wine tradition of the territory, yesterday and today.

Romanesque complex on a site already occupied by a palaeo-Christian cult building, whose fragments are visible outside the apse. The basilica, with three naves with three apses, columns and Corinthian capitals of re-use and wooden trusses, was liberated from the successive additions in the restorations of Luca Beltrami (1890-1892); in the bell tower is walled at half height a votive stone dedicated to Jupiter. The octagonal baptistery of the mid-12th century has a sixteen-window-pierced dome, a matroneo on columns with capitals with plant and animal motifs, Roman epigraphs and a millionth of re-use, and there is exposed the epigraph of the young Arnolfo, who died in 893. Baptistery open Saturday and Sunday, the other days on request (Pro Loco, tel. 340 6433070).
Face to face with the prophets of Guercino.
A small museum of the Italian theatre of the twentieth century.
The oldest manor of the Challant, built around the 10th century and completed in the first fourteenth century by Ebalo I; ruins in the reserve of Lake Villa, 30 minutes walk from the parking lot.
17th century church in the center of the village, with a painting of the Annunciation of Pietro Antonio Ferro di Tricarico.
One of the most important neoclassical residences in Italy, with rooms decorated by Felice Giani for the Milzetti family in the Napoleonic age.
A pedestrian area with the Dolomites in the square.
From the two lakes of the Castles on foot.
One of the ancient mills of the valley, testimony of the productive activities of the past.
The cathedral dedicated to the patron saint of the city, with the Duomo Museum.
Vercelli between faith and music.

The lakes between Liguria and Piedmont.
A walled village at the foot of the Sibillini.
He preserves seventeenth-century Padan canvases, including the Nativity of the Virgin by Lionello Spada and a Crucifixion of Palma il Giovane.
In the medieval Palazzo dei Capitani the agricultural tools and artisans, the domestic furnishings and devotional objects of the Apennine communities, used until the depopulation of the mountain.
Flamingos a stone's throw from the village.
Fine sand and pinewood on the Ionian Sea.
The refuge of St. Francis in the village.

On a height that was perhaps a Roman fortification under control of the Irno valley, in the sixteenth century the Hermits of Santa Maria di Collereto founded a monastery there; in 1604, entered the Augustinian order, dedicated the church to the Holy Spirit. Repressed in 1653 at the behest of Innocent X, it became a hermitage and then a charity; restored since 2003 as a museum, it has rooms, corridors, cells, ancient cisterns and terraces with views from the Irno valley to the Sele valley, the Gulf of Salerno and the Amalfi Coast. It hosts cultural events.
The oldest monument in the country.
Greek Orthodox Church of the 11th century in Piazza delle Tre Chiese, considered the oldest Orthodox church in Italy.
Alleys and buildings around the cathedral.
Villas and views of the ridge.
The ancient nucleus above the lake.

An ancient rural village of Cimbrian origin at 980 meters, under Mount Finnchio, born by tradition as a guard post of Castel Beseno: since 1988 the exhibitions of mural art have painted old and new houses along an itinerary that tells traditions and local customs. The Hofentol waterfall, illuminated in winter, is 15 minutes in the woods.
MiC card (updated 2020) indicates "closed" every day; check openings with the Municipality (tel. 0481 637152)
A piece of North Africa in Sicily.
The peasant civilization of Padana in a monastery.

Residence of the Marquis Colocci Vespucci of the second half of the sixteenth century, at the highest point of the city, with furnishings, objects and paintings of one of the main aristocratic families of Jesine, related to Amerigo Vespucci; reopened in 2013. Guided tours only by reservation on the first Thursday of the month and the third weekend, at 16, 17 and 18, for groups of up to 10 people; the museum is on the fourth floor, reachable only on foot.
Blera's nut graves.

The origins date back to the 11th century; it was rebuilt several times after the Middle Ages, often following devastating earthquakes, it preserves the ogival portal and the rose window of the 13th century. Next is the Doge's Palace, transformed in the eighteenth century.
Tower houses and carpigian scaglioles.
The monumental entrance to the village.
A single nave rock church, rich in folk frescoes, consecrated or consecrated in 1628 by the bishop of Minervino Altobello Carissimi; you arrive there with a path from the Grotto of San Michele.
An ancient sanctuary with views of the valleys of the Alburni.

Museum spread in the historic center, in disused environments that reconstruct the traditional interiors with the objects of pastoral life; the route has six stages: the mill, the oven of the dance, the handicrafts of wool, the ancient house, the shepherdhood and the popular religiosity.
The church built by the community on the village square.

The parish church of Ossimo Superiore is located on the presumed site of a fifteenth-century building, perhaps a castle; it has facade of the seventeenth century and inside seventeenth-century stuccoes and a altarpiece of 1843 by Antonio Guadagnini. Next to it, the Oratory of the Disciplines, home of the confraternity, dated 1658, with portal in stone of Sarnico and closed arched window.
The city as it was before the Panaro detour.
The history of the Oltreppo from fossils to the Roman age, in the Certosa.
Of the perched village remain traces of the medieval walls and the civic tower.

Inaugurated in February 2026 in the Littorio Forest, where at the mouth of the river Gela stood an archaic emporium, probably also port of the Greek city, exhibits the remains of three Greek ships with their cargo: at the center the wreck The 4000 m2 room, designed by Ettore Di Mauro, has a reversed wooden roof and a room with 3D viewers.
The devoted heart of the "Borgo Madonna."

A few kilometers north of Riva del Garda, between dry terraces of olive trees, vines and chestnut trees: the medieval village of Canale, mentioned since 1211, the castle with the fortified village of Frapporta and Lake Tenno turquoise color.
All about the Majella bear.
Seven centuries of history around the tower.
A medieval village remained intact.
Under the Duomo, the crypt of the patron.
The history of science in Pavia.

In the seminary opened in 1846 next to the sanctuary: the Parmigiani Art Gallery with about 50 paintings above all sacred of Bolognese and Emilian school (Ludovico Carracci, Bartolomeo Passerotti, the Masteletta, Luigi Crespi, Filippo Pedrini); the Homnia Opera by Romeo Musa (1882-1960), painter, xilographer and poet, with more than 800 plates and illustrations of the Promessi bridegrooms; the Museum of Natural Sciences Silvio Ferrari is a small archaeological collection, a planetarium with an astronomical observatory and a library of over 25,000 volumes. Open all year round by reservation; in July and August every day except Mondays 10-12 and 15.30-18.30.

The village is surrounded by the largest ravines of Riggio, from the north-west to the south-east, with Basilian frescoes and Greek inscriptions, of Fantiano, Fullonese, with a seventeenth-century Calvary carved in the tuff in a cave, and of San Biagio, with a frescoed rock church.
Viddalba peak, between faith and climbing.
Walk in the green.
Understand, and try, how you were looking for the gold of Bessa.

Country of the Sibillini Mountains National Park at the foot of Mount Bove, with Romanesque churches such as Santi Vincenzo and Anastasio (consecrated in 1093) and Sant'Ercolano, the slopes of Frontignano and the valley of the Ussita stream; after the earthquake of 2016 historical center, monuments and museums are only partially usable.
The story of Mytistran in two stories.

Built in the 16th century with a Latin cross with a trussed roof, it preserves in the middle of the main altar a small oil on a table (45×56 cm) with the Holy Family, a copy of a work by Michelangelo attributed to Marcello Venusti, and frescoes from the early 20th century by Eugenio Allori. During the restorations of the twentieth century a medieval stone altar re-emerged under the plaster; under the sanctuary there is the small beach of the same name.
Walking through alleys, palaces and ceramists' workshops.
The mystery of the vampire child.

The pass of Capanne di Carrega, with the historic tavern and post station on the ancient salt streets, is crossed by the hiking itinerary "Via del mare" and by the long ridge that connects Monte Carmo to Monte Antola. On the homonymous pass stands the historic church of San Fermo.

Protected area between the municipalities of Rubiana and Viù, managed by the Metropolitan City of Turin. The hill marks the border of the territory of Rubiana: the provincial road that goes up from Almese crosses the village and connects the Valley of Susa with the Lanzo Valleys.
A tour of mountain villages with a lot of history.

In the municipal seat, it collects 933 artifacts ordered by origin, from prehistory to the Sannitic and Roman age up to the modern age: among these a protome wolf-head from a public building, probably a temple, the head of a votive statuette, many tiles with stamp of Roman workshops and a stone-stone with an epigraphic corpus useful to reconstruct the history of the country.

In the chapel of the SS. Sacramento holds, in a walled case, the relic of St. Cesareus, patron saint celebrated on August 27 after the dispute between the confraternities of St. Anthony of Padua and St. Joseph for the choice of the saint.
The Guercino in a 14th-century church.
Gothic church isolated between the porphyry quarries near Fornace; near the church were found ancient graves and coins of the emperors Domitian, Trajan, Tito and others.

Collection of 49 pastels donated to the Municipality by Italian and Russian artists, made between 1996 and 2001 mainly on velvety paper: views of St. Petersburg, Jaroslavl and Rostov alongside Italian subjects such as Sanremo, Monviso with the hills of the Langhe and Lequio Berria, with works by Renzo Magnanini, Vladimir Emelianov, Luigi Carbone, Peter Pavlov and others. The City page does not indicate exhibition center or timetable: information in the Municipality, Via Roma 36, tel. 0173 52402.
The Great Federal Shrine of the Nuragics.

It rises where from 700 AD there is documented an oratory of St. Christopher; the new church, decided in 1522, was completed in 1567 by the architect Pompeo Pedemonte and deeply modified in the nineteenth century (reconsecrated in 1887), when the archpriest Antonio Parazzi extended it, transformed its facade and made it a picture gallery. It preserves a polyptych by Bartolomeo Vivarini, a group in terracotta of influence and paintings by Tassinari, Borgani and Andreasino, as well as works by Parmesan, Bolognese, Cremonese, Mantua and Verona.
A sannite tomb in the tuff.
The Tuscolane villas in miniature.
Wood, wrought iron and hand knotted carpets.

The devotional path started in 1590, with 20 frescoed chapels and life-size terracotta groups on the life of St. Francis; from the churchyard of St. Nicholas one of the most beautiful views of the lake. UNESCO World Heritage.

Founded in 1999 at the entrance of the country, it is the only monothematic museum in Europe dedicated to obsidian: multisensory path with cartography, interactive audiovisual and sounds of the workmanship, works by sculptor Karmine Piras and brothers Atzori, minerals and fossils. It tells more than three thousand years of production, from the recent Neolithic to the Bronze Age, and from here start the guided excursions in the Park of Ossidiana; cumulative ticket with guide, excursion and laboratory €16. Open from Wednesday to Sunday.

A small abandoned village, a hamlet of Zungri, mentioned as early as 1280; the name derives from the Greek priest, Pope Leonitius, probably owner of the first building around which the medieval town grew. Damaged by landslides and floods, it was left in the eighties, when the community moved a few kilometers higher; the buildings are mostly stone with brick inserts.
The frescoed cloister survived the earthquake.
The Resistance in Val Sangone told by those who lived it.
€9 whole; €5 reduced; free with the Firenze Card

Museum opened in 2009 in a former bunker of the Second World War: it tells the history and nature of Val Passiria with the visitor center of the Gruppo di Tessa Nature Park, sections on the high Passiria, the mine of Monteneve and on geology and local nature, and the life of Moso and its inhabitants during the war. Outside a fence of the ibex and a climbing wall; guided tours and workshops on request.
Deep sea under a fort.
of private property and under renovation, currently not visitable (card of the Municipality updated to 03/03/2025)

On the plateau of Cima Rest, in the northern part of the Vestino Valley at the foot of the Tombea and Caplone mountains, stand the barns-stallas in stone with the sloping roof in straw: the oldest date back to the seventeenth century and each roof is formed by about 7,500 bundles of wheat straw more than one metre long, bound in such a way as to be waterproof. According to Visit Val Vestino are the only known example in Lombardy of buildings with still existing straw roof; some have been restored as holiday homes. Here again the cheese Tombea, Presidio Slow Food, is produced, and every September since 1979 the Cheese Festival of Cima Rest is held.
Medieval village of Valdelsa among the most beautiful villages in Italy, with the Pretorio Palace, the parish church of San Regolo and the civic museum with a fossil whale of the Pliocene.
On Piazza del Duomo, erected in 1713 in memory of the earthquake victims, with a late Baroque façade and a nineteenth-century dome of over 35 meters.
The oldest church in the city.
Baroque church of the seventeenth century inside the historic center.
The Garda from above.
A Raphaelese school canvas in a village in the Lucane Dolomites.
The symbol of the Lecce baroque.
Ancient defensive fortress at the top of the city, which according to Italia.it hosts the Museum of the Sicilian Middle Ages; it is managed by the Naxos Taormina Archaeological Park.
Massif of 700 meters with the remains of the ancient Erbesso, rediscovered in the fifties.
Milan from above in the park.

The excavations of the 1994 Archaeological Superintendence at Casa Orlando have brought to light the remains of a rustic villa dating from the 1st century BC to the 2nd A.D., including an area for the production of wine; other remains are visible along the road to Santa Cristina, marked by a sign.
The monument from which the Mediofondo Casartelli starts.

Medieval village in the Peligna basin, on the western side of the Morrone and crossed by the river Sagittarius; quoted for the first time in 997, in 1294 was assigned by Charles II of Anjou to the abbot of the Holy Spirit al Morrone, binding his history to Celestine V. Symbol of the village is the sanctuary of the Madonna della Libera.
The Castelmagno and the life of the valley, between museum and path.

The village of the risotto is on the right of Tione on the border with Veronese, with origins in the Bronze Age: the Castello Scaligero restored and opened to the public, the sixteenth-century Villa Gonzaga-Zani referring to the students of Giulio Romano and the Museo Francioli Nuvolari on the Rising Mantua and life in rice.
It is reached by chairlift; it offers a mountain lake and trails. The mountains around Leonessa are skiing in winter and you can go on easy and challenging excursions from spring to autumn.
The 17th century village of Marmilla.
The peasant life inside the caves.

In the medieval castle near the Cathedral, which also preserves the former Napoleonic prisons: sections of prehistory, Roman age (with the reconstruction of the ancient fountain of the Bollente, sculptures and stele) and late antique and medieval age.
It connects Arzachena to Cannigione and La Conia with views of the Gulf of Arzachena, the archipelago of La Maddalena and the protected area of the pond of Saloni.

Summer residence designed by Cardinal Flavio Chigi and built from 1665 on a project by Felice della Greca, with tower, church of San Francesco di Sales, Casino, housing of shepherds, citroniera and cavities dug into the tuff; fallen after 1693, it has been of the Municipality since 2009 and restored since 2020 in the Network of Historic Houses of Lazio, frame of the concerts of Formello Chigi Festival.

Museum of contemporary art set up after the restorations of 2001 in the attic and along the ancient walkway between the two towers of the castle: works especially of contemporary Italian and foreign artists, also Piacenza, between painting, sculpture and photography, exposed in rotation.

Ancient sacred forest in Jupiter, 17 hectares of centuries-old candelabra beech trees with maples, wild pears, hornbeams and badgers, in the Majella Park since 1992; a 2.8 km ring with 70 m of altitude leads to the hermitage of Sant'Antonio (XIV-XV century). Hiking and horseback riding in summer, cross-country skiing in winter.

Centre between the Roman Castles and the Prenestini Mountains, about 38 km from Rome, with the remains of the Torraccia, the two-tiered nymph of the residence of the Emperor Maxentius (beginning of the fourth century), and the Railway-Museum of the Colonna Station, which preserves the last section of tracks of the old Rome-Fiuggi line.
The castle of the five towers, the heart of the historic center.

Built around the year 1000, repeatedly pillaged and destroyed, it was expanded and rebuilt by Colonna, Barberini Colonna di Sciarra, Massimo and Brancaccio. In the ancient chapel there is the cycle of Renaissance frescoes of ...Giuditta and Holoferne.Today it houses the Museum of Rural Civilization.
Wide pastures, high peaks and a small lake, with the chapel dedicated to Our Lady; a destination for excursions and snowshoes.
Gerolamo's Venetian polyptych from Santacroce.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 0 of the 5 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
Caves in the valley to the west of the old village, reachable by a path in the vegetation, where in autumn 1943 they found shelter from the bombings over 500 civilians.
In the cemetery of Pratica di Mare, director Sergio Leone is buried, who asked to rest here, where he had shot some of his films from the 1960s.

Built in the fifteenth century by the Quadra di Villatico on Venetian models, renovated in the eighteenth century: double façade with stone elements of Sarnico, interior frescoed with two naves, seventeenth-century altarpieces by Andrea Asper and a canvas from 1645 with the view of Chiari Murata. It is one of the five suburban churches related to the Quadre, protagonists in September of the Palio delle Quadre (since 1978).
Archaeology and Risorgimento sections, in the city of the landing of Garibaldi and the Mille.

Castle wanted by the abbot Aligerno in the 10th century to defend Montecassino, with the pentagonal tower of 20 meters of the 12th century; key point of the Gustav Line, devastated in the war, restored and opened in 2015.
The center crosses along a long road flanked by porticoed houses, between streets and ancient houses; in February the carts of the Carnival of Castlein parade.
The popular music of Montemarano, home of the tarantella.
Memory of the Jewish community of the village.
Place of devotion linked to the Marian apparition of 1557, with a view of the lower city.
the MiC card is closed every day of the week; check if it can be visited by appointment
Apulian peasant life.
The Senate Palace and Don Sturzo.

In the building of the agricultural cooperative "La Cerere" was founded in 1910, managed by Pro Loco: the living part reconstructs a bedroom from the 1930s with a wash-house, a kitchen, a stone oven and a pantry with barrels and dams; the country side exhibits a Sicilian cart, a small field of wheat, historical agricultural tools such as a sower and a monument in spikes donated by the artisans of Foglianise in 1999; in the center three cases with local varieties of bread and wheat, panels on the cultivation of wheat and a projection room. Visits every day 9-13 and 15-19, by telephone reservation.
A spectacular gorge just a stone's throw away.
The Etruscans of Chianti.
Two waterfalls in the territory of Farnese; the Salabron is formed by the Olpeta river.

Born around 1170 as a quadrangular tower guarding the lands of the Badia di Frassinoro, then a castle mast erected by the Montecuccoli in the thirteenth century; after 1429 it was the seat of an extensive podestria until 1797. The restored tower can be visited and at the top has a 360-degree panoramic balcony on the valleys of the Dolo and the Dragon and on the peaks of the Cimone and the Cusna.
In front of Corte Trapp, it has been documented since 1345 but the current building is from the eighteenth century; it preserves several works of art and a early Christian tombstone.

The 14th century Mastio annexed to the Civic Tower, once a high part of the fortress and barracks of the village, connected to a stretch of walls; damaged in 1944, it returned to public use in 1997 and houses the municipal library (more than 3,000 volumes) and the historical archive, with documents from 1402 to 1866 and the maps of the Cosci and Gerini families. In the centre there are still sections of the medieval walls and towers.
Cinquecento fortress with frescoes by Amico Aspertini and the dovecote attributed to Vignola.
Next to the Palazzo Comunale, the oratory of 1699 has a late Baroque Rococo façade; restored in 2003-2004, it houses valuable paintings and the Credenza with the statue of Saint Monica.
temporarily closed to the public for organisational and management reasons (MiC)

It exhibits parchments, furnishings, vestments, sacred goldsmithery, ex-vote and a crib, with objects from the 15th to the 19th century coming from the church of Sant'Osvaldo. Open Tuesday 9.30-11.30, Wednesday and Saturday 15-17.

Outside the village, on a hill reachable from the tracturo, the tower of Santa Maria dei Vignali of the XII-XIII century, surrounded by more ancient Sannitic fortifications and the remains of a medieval village.

Multimedia Museum dedicated to Davide Lajolo (1912-1984), born in Vinchio, partisan with the name of battle "Ulisse" since 1943, director of "L'Unità" (1948-1958), deputy and Viareggio Prize 1977 with "Veder l'erba" on the side of the roots ""; retraces his life as partisan, journalist and writer. Individual and guided tours by reservation (groups up to 30 people), audioguide in Italian and English, accessible to disabled people. In the village there are also the birthplace with plaque (Via Ramaudio 4) and the bronze bust of Floriano Bodini on the stairway between Piazza Vercelli and Piazza San Marco.
The adjoining church is closed for the earthquake 2016; information to the parish, 0733 431832

Born from the collection of master Tommaso Dattoli, formed in about thirty years: three rooms with agricultural tools, domestic tools and tools for the processing of milk, wool and broom, a room that reconstructs the farmhouse and a group of wooden objects between bread stamps, molds and dolls.
Architect Tobias Brenner's work contains books, writings and photos from the Russian community of Merano.

Long sandy beaches, frequented also by surfers, from Bagni Mauro, the last plant in the province of Savona, to Bagni Pinuccia further west; the Nautilus Beach is the largest beach in the municipality and has a space for dogs. In front of the beachfront lighthouse you can also surf at night.
It preserves carpets, tapestries and saddlebags woven on ancient horizontal frames, with live demonstrations of the women of the country; in August the exhibition of the tapestry and carpet is held.
Woods and blooms above the valley.
The triangular square in front is one of the most beautiful places in Bologna.
Complete the tour of the churches in the center.
The pier for a walk overlooking the sea and mountains; in summer the boats leave for Liguria.
The MiC card (updated to May 2020) is closed every day; Common tel. 0963 321091
The town's stage square.
Farmhouse of the nineteenth century restored with original furnishings, to show how it was a typical Cimbrian house; on summer evenings it hosts stories about the past.
The arch mirrored in the Metauro.
Woods and wild peaks on the south side of the Amiata.
A votive church with a circular plan.
Waterfall on the river Tammarecchia, reachable by a path made in December 2020; on the same stream stands one of the two Jelardi Mills, of the seventeenth century.

It preserves paintings from the XVI to the XVIII century and on the ceiling a nineteenth-century fresco by Giovan Battista Canal with the Assumption of Mary among Saints Jerome, Antonio Abate and Lucia.
Between sea pine trees and Mediterranean maquis, wide views from Castiglioncello to the Gulf of Baratti; paths to the Fonte dei Poggetti with wash basins and windmill.

The territory is rich in archaeological sites: on the top of the Piani d'Invrea a small Neolithic menhir dominates the city and the sea; on the hill of Parasio, near the ancient church of San Donato, you can see the remains of the Roman-Byzantine castrum.
Watch the glass blow live.
The fifth civilian in the square.

Oratorio campestre della parishe di San Silvestro until its elevation to the parish on April 3, 1959, preserves a wooden statue of the Madonna and Child of the XV century, the main altar of 1711 and a marble parapet of 1736.

Country of Arbëreshë roots overlooking the sunsets of the Tyrrhenian Sea, with the church of San Giovanni Battista on the remains of the castle and the parish museum; on the coast of the Gulf of Sant'Eufemia Gizzeria Lido, capital of kitesurfing, the Tower of Capo Suvero and the Isthmus of the Lighthouse with the beach of Turrazzo.
The twelve monolithic columns.
A complex nuraghe with a rare Etruscan bronze.

Regionally oriented nature reserve established in 2006, of 898 hectares, one of the largest in Italy: it includes the sites of Community interest "Palude del Conte      . Dune di Punta Prosciutto" and "Porto Cesareo" and it is in continuity with the protected marine area and the reserves of the eastern Taranto coast; there are paths in nature.

It tells the tradition of hemp rope, practiced in the village for at least two centuries and by most of the inhabitants: tools and machinery of different eras, strings and objects in rope, historical photographs of ropemakers at work and videos of the last generations. Open from March to October on Sundays and holidays, 15-19; closed from 15 July to 15 August.
Church of the late nineteenth century; inside a floor in Palladian style with three pieces of a mosaic.
On the trail of the hermit Saint Nile.

About 6,000 traditional objects from the Alpine valleys and the Brescia plain collected by the painter Giacomo Bergomi: agriculture, breeding, crafts, domestic work and rituals of the cycle of the year and life, with gallery for temporary exhibitions and library. Free admission; closed in August.

Housed in the sheds of the old factory (the 'farie') of Remanzacco, museum after in 1965 the production Tonutti moved to a new place, preserves machinery and atmospheres of that time and documents a century of production of agricultural tools and machines. Four sections: industrial archaeology (machines and tools, some still working), agricultural (with a steam engine operating a threshing machine), about eighty vintage cars from 1915 to today (including a Ford Model T, Rolls Royce, a DeLorean, a Ferrari F40 and Lamborghini) and about 75 motorcycles from the early twentieth century to the eighties. Open every day 9-17, without reservation; guided tours.
13th century tower, reopened in 2024 with the exhibition "Nel signo dell'acqua" on five floors, dedicated to the transformations of the city related to the watercourses.
The ethnographic museum dedicated to Giuseppe Pitrè, at the Chinese Palace.
The castle church.
The only national monument of the city, founded in 1292 and completed in 1474 in Lombard Gothic, with frescoes of the fifteenth century.
The Lombard Renaissance in marble.

Karst cavities formed about two million years ago at the foot of the village, dug into the rock, with a descent of about 20 meters along a staircase as wide as the cave; born as a place of pagan worship, it is mentioned for the first time in a parchment of the year 1000 preserved in Montecassino. It has a neoclassical entrance, frescoed vault, columns and a marble statue of the Archangel, celebrated every year on 29 September. Visits on request, entrance fee.
The two surviving columns of the Roman forum.
In the attic of the Palazzo Comunale the barrels batteries where the traditional balsamic vinegar of the city ages.
A Masaccio on Francigena.
The richest portal in the city.
Theatre collected in the historic center, with rectangular hall and balcony gallery.
The cellars of Val Nure.
An interior covered with paintings and a Luca Giordano.

Two nineteenth-century pillars mark the ancient Porta Napoli, access to the historic center with the information office of the Pro Loco; in the center the Baroque Palazzo Morelli, with elegant portal and wrought iron balconies, and the former 18th-century Town Hall, today the municipal library.

Beach about two kilometers one kilometer from the village along the SS 129, of clear and fine sand mixed with shells and pebbles, with clear water and seabed that descends quickly; the hills of maquis behind frame a pond and the mouth of the Cedrino. Often windy and frequented by surfers; about two miles away lies the wreck of the KT, half a German landing of about 70 meters sunk in 1943. Accessible to the disabled, with equipment rental, large parking suitable for campers, bar and refreshment.
Municipal theatre inaugurated in 1883 on a project by Ireneo Aleandri, with a horseshoe room, two orders of stages and a loggia, up to 250 seats.

Discovered by chance in 1952 by digging a well in the mine of San Giovanni, it was formed in rocks of the lower Cambrian about 500 million years ago: walls covered with crystals of dark brown barite, a room over 25 meters high with stalactites, stalagmites and a small lake.

Inside the Municipal Library, it exhibits in showcases about 150 specimens of animals or their parts protected by the Washington Convention (CITES), in force in Italy since 1980; the route is designed for children, families and schools. Hours from the MiC card: Monday and Wednesday 9-13 and 16-18, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 9-13, Saturday and Sunday closed.

Villa veneta, formerly Secco, Dondi dall'Orologio and Zasio, built between 1566 and 1576 by the crescasco doctor Giovanni Antonio Secco, with loggia with three arches and two towers; the noble floor contains frescoes from the Metamorphosis of Ovidio (Scilla, Mercury and Argo, Apollo and Dafne, Kefalo and Procri), a hunting room and a room of Genesis, while the eighteenth-century oratory replicates the Holy House of Loreto and every 10 December a blade of light strikes the altar. Purchased by the Municipality in 1979, it houses the collection donated by Roberto Bassi Rathgeb, more than 400 works with paintings by Moretto, Moroni and Palma il Giovane, by Magnasco, Fra Galgario, Ceruti and the Longhi, and works by Lombardy of the nineteenth-nineteenth century; the museum was inaugurated in 2018 and also hosts photographic exhibitions.
The last leud that sails.
The history of the mine and its miners.
Kayak and birdwatching between pines and eucalyptuses.
Lawns and woods above the village.

Seaside town at the foot of the Gargano: the Swabian-Ange castle with the most important collection of daunie stems, the Archaeological Park of Siponto with the metallic wire basilica of Edoardo Tresoldi, the abbey of San Leonardo and the wetlands of Frattarolo and Lake Salso.
At Porta Bassano, it is the entrance to the walkway of the roundabout and seat of the Tourist Office IAT; it houses re-enactment rooms with medieval equipment.

Neoclassical village with quadrangular plan, rebuilt after the collapse of 1771 by Pope Clement XIV with the name of Castel Clementino, with three monumental doors and two main streets that cross. From 1915 to 1955 there was a large prison camp, today the Park of Peace, told by the House of Memory.
Oval walled village on the hills between Valdelsa and Val di Cecina, with two round towers of the fifteenth century and the fourteenth-century Fortress.
Five centuries of copper beaten by Force's caldera.
The lively heart of the island, born from a lake.
today hosts a kindergarten (Emilia-Romagna Tourism)
Some of the oldest metals in Italy, in a small town museum.

In the former Jesuit College, overlooking the courtyard of the Prisons next to the church of St. Ignatius (built by the Jesuits at the end of the 16th century), it collects household objects and tools that tell the country's rural past, its socio-economic history, culture and traditions. The complex also houses the library.
One of Italy's most beautiful late-Gothic cycles.

Documents, historical images and objects of the Monferrato trams: two Lanzo's Henschel & Sohn locomotives, a late nineteenth-century freight wagon, an electric accumulator locomotive and an American Davenport locomotive, as well as telegraphy and telephone equipment, signalling lamps, timetables and track and sleeper samples with the original brands.
A private collection open.
The sanctuary of pilgrimages in May.
The Romanesque silhouette that stands on the marina, with an intact crypt.
See the griffins flying on the Tagliamento.
Two hamlets that preserve ancient architectures, with buildings dating back to the fifteenth century, the seventeenth and the nineteenth centuries.
A village that marks time with 57 sundials.
Birdwatching near the Po.

In Levigliani, next to the ticket office of Corchia, the museum tells the uses of stone and Apuan marble: sacred art in marble, colored marbles now little hollowed, baroque engravings, kitchen mortars and for medicinal herbs, a section dedicated to the biologist Emilio Simi, discoverer of the Antro del Corchia, and a tomb in box of the Ligurian Apuans from the nearby necropolis (III-I century BC). The Museo di comunità "Lavorare liberi" tells the history of the Comunello and the Cooperative Condomini Levigliani, which has been riding Monte Corchia for over 50 years, with tools and the reconstruction of a quarry with wire cutting.

The hamlet, 8 km from Cori, preserves the remains of the ancient gate, the baronial palace Castello Salviati and the sixteenth-century church of San Giovanni Battista; near the Lake Giulianello, natural monument since 2007.

The bell tower, which was incorporated into the brick façade completed in 1866; in 1927 Giuseppe Castellucci renewed it in neoclassical forms with a large dome inspired by San Lorenzo di Firenze. Inside, the wooden choir of master Diocletian (1667) and a small museum of sacred furnishings in the old sacristy.

City on the tuff cliff between Umbria and Tuscia: the Cathedral with the Chapel of San Brizio di Beato Angelico and Luca Signorelli, the Well of San Patrizio and an underground city of Etruscan caves and tunnels.
MiC tab indicates closing times on every day: check openings
A rare early medieval basilica in a tiny village.
The parish, decorated with stuccoes, preserves a processional cross in bronze of the 11th century, a banner of Adeodato Malatesta and rich vestments.
Barns, fountains and churches of a popular Ladin village.
The tower of the free municipality.
The high speed station of Santiago Calatrava, a white steel wave and 483 meters long glass, and the three bridges called Vele, the new symbol of the city.
the castle is private property, visits with the Walking Tour in fixed dates (€10, free up to 14 years) according to Visit MRL
Garibaldi in Aspromonte in multimedia version.
The plan Gonzaghesca under the arcades.

The parish was born outside the castle moat and rebuilt in the eighteenth century, when the large Baroque staircase was added. It preserves a canvas by Durante Nobili da Caldarola, pupil of Lotto, dated 1546, and a painting by G.B. Fagiani with the view of Mogliano in the eighteenth century; reopened after a recent restoration.

The 18th-century manor villa of the Gandini Morelli Bugna Bottagisio, which in 1859 hosted Francesco Giuseppe and Napoleon III in the days of the Armistice of Villafranca; the Municipality bought it in 1997. The museum, born in 1959 from the exhibition for the centenary of the meeting, is on the first floor noble since 2014 and has been reordered chronologically in 2022/2023: weapons, prints and relics of the armies of the wars of independence, documents and objects of the villafranchesi who fought between 1848 and 1866 and volunteers Garibaldi; on the ground floor three rooms with paintings of the legacy Martinelli, including works from Verona of the early twentieth century. Open Saturday 15.30-18.30 and Sunday 10-12 and 15.30-18.30, closed in August.
Umbrian frescoes at the top of the village.
Memory of the Knights outside the walls.
The MiC card (updated in May 2020) indicates the museum closed every day: check the opening (tel. 081 5737125, museumarzano@hotmail.it).
The market in the cloister.
The defenses of the village and the Water Gate.
The nativity scene that gave Calvi the name of "Country of the Nativity."

Church of the XII century, the oldest among those mentioned by the sources, which preserves the altar triptych painted in 1482 by the Lucca Michele Ciampanti with the Madonna and Child and the Saints Giovanni Battista, Vito, Modesto and Pietro.
Sea, cliffs and Mongerbino's natural arch.

A galley-shaped village set in the rock, inside the Regional Park Gola della Rossa and Frasassi, with its ... covers along the walls, the Baroque Saint Lucia with the historical Cartoteca delle Marche and, along the Esino, the Romanesque-Gothic Abbey of St. Helena.

In the center of the village, it is located on the area of a Benedictine church of the 11th century; the present building, classicist with 17th century reworkings, dates from the end of the 16th and the beginning of the 17th century. It has a single nave with a barrel vault and four chapels on the side; on the first right there is the retablo of Santa Maria, coming from the church of the same name. The feast of the saint is celebrated at the end of June.
A Roman bridge fortified in the Middle Ages, a rare example in Lombardy.
The only museum dedicated to the champion of Coriano, with motorcycles, helmets, suits and trophies of the Sic.
Small church in the surroundings of the village, with essential Romanesque lines and no architectural virtuosities.

The coastal tower is made of square brick on a small height near the beach, built in 1568 in the sighting line desired by Carlo V against the incursions from the sea; the upper and lateral parts were added in the last century by the families who lived in it. Since 1981 it has been from the Province of Teramo; the historians link the archaeological remains in front of the tower to the port of ancient Hatria (Atri). Today it houses a research and veterinary training center, a library, the information point of the Marine Protected Area and a Museum of the Sea in preparation; guided tours.
Built between 1779 and 1781 in neoclassical forms as a care and health facility; renovated, it now houses exhibitions, cultural events and the civic library.

Cittadina of the hills of Basso Molise with a medieval historical center dominated by the cathedral Basilica of San Pardo, whose Gothic façade is 1319, and a low town born around the archaeological area of the Roman Larinum, with the amphitheatre of flavia age and the mosaics of the thermal baths; in the Ducal Palace the Civic Museum preserves the mosaic of the wolf with Romolo and Remo.

A hilly village of the Parco delle Serre between Lake Angitola and the Serre plateau, at the foot of Monte Coppari, with noble palaces with granite portals, a medieval tower and two museums: that of peasant and artisan civilization, awarded at the European Museum of the Year Award, and the Museum Polo in the former nineteenth-century spinning mill.
The Santa Rosalia cave in the woods.
The oldest plow in the world.
The white beaches of Tuscany.
A 16th century fresco in the library.
Two small museums in a quiet part.
The 18th century terracotta façade.
A Longobard Abbey on the Via Francigena.
Once a rich Benedictine abbey dependent on Farfa, it retains a beautiful Romanesque portal.

Founded in 1985 by the municipal administration in order to preserve the etnoanthropological traditions: a single compartment on the ground floor reconstructs a land house of the early twentieth century, with tools and objects of the cultivation of wheat, vine and olive trees; in the façade a remarkable eaves in coppi. Quoted from the guide "Musei 2008" of the Touring Club. Open Tuesday and Thursday 9-13, other days by appointment with guided tours of the staff of the Municipal Library.
The mother church with the baroque bell tower.
City exhibition space for contemporary art.

15th-century church along the ancient Valeriana street, perhaps finished in 1532 as indicated by the date on the stone portal Simona; bell tower with mullioned windows on each side. Inside a Madonna with Child and St. Anthony of Padua and a marble saintly aquarium of Vezza d'Oglio with the coat of arms of the Federici.
Giant wooden sculptures, including Frino, Spirito del Bosco, along the paths of the villages of Forni and Avoltri, and the statue of Mother Nature that overlooks the village.

High Renaissance-style castle on the Venosta Valley, residence of the Messner family, with about 1,500 years of history: the museum is dedicated to the spiritual dimension of the mountain, with sacred mountains (Kailash, Fuji, Ayers Rock, Ararat, Olympus), Tibetan objects, masks from five continents, frescoes, sculptures, an adventure library and meditative spaces. Open from the fourth Sunday of March to the first Sunday of November, 10-17 (last entrance 16), closed on Wednesday; from the paid parking Juval P1 on the SS38 electric shuttle and about 15 minutes walk, or trails from Ciardes and Stava (1-1.5 hours). Not accessible to those with motor difficulties.
Founded by Abbot Pierre Chanoux at the end of the nineteenth century to make known and protect the alpine flora; it blooms in summer.

Benedictine monastery founded around 1150 by Ulrico di Tarasp and his wife Uta, at 1,340 m among the highest vineyards in Europe: the highest Benedictine abbey in Europe, inhabited by monks for about 900 years. White complex around a large courtyard; in the Romanesque crypt frescoes of the founding era with a unique representation of the angels. The museum tells the life of monks according to the "ora et labora" with exhibitions on Marienberg and Mary. Open Monday-Saturday 10-17.

Church in red volcanite in Gothic-Catalan style of the early sixteenth century, in panoramic position in front of a nuraghe; until the nineteenth century it was called San Giorgio de Ledda and was the original seat of the great retablo. The feast of the patron saint is celebrated in late April.
A room of 19th-century wonders in the high valley.
Medieval village of Chianti Classico surrounded by vineyards, documented by the IX century and Florentine since the end of the thirteenth century.
15th-century church in the Friulian late-Gothic style overlooking Piazza Italia.

One of the two promontories that close the bay of Mattinata; the visits are organized through the visitor center of the Park. From the site come the stone scudi on columns used as funerary signs and the ambers exhibited in the first and third sections of the National Archaeological Museum.

Borgo del Fermano rises next to the Roman center of Falerio Picinus, founded in 29 BC and monumentalized by the Augustan age: today it remains the archaeological park with the Roman theatre, among the best preserved of the Marches, and the Archaeological Civic Museum. After the earthquake of 2016 historic center, monuments and municipal museums are partially usable.
The ruins of the Jesuit oval church.

A place of worship already in Roman times, it was built almost certainly in the 10th century over the remains of a pagan temple; of pre-Romanesque origin, it has a sixteenth-century bastion linked to the raids of the barbarian corsairs.
A medieval arch with a legend of love.
The history of the Italian song inside a vintage train.
The underground mystery of the village.

Città della sartoria nell'interra anconetano, with fourteenth-century walls, Piazza Mazzini and the panoramic loggia from the Conero in Loreto, the Bramantesco Town Hall, the Pieve with the tomb of the explorer Giacomo Costantino Beltrami and the museums of the Marche biroccio and the Battle of Filottrano in 1944.

Typical karst village with its ancient nucleus behind a small tree-lined square, between alleys and wells, famous for its precious limestone quarries; it hits the large station, exchange port until 1918.
The baroque sabaudo at the top of the stairway of Leja.

Born in the 12th century as a fortified settlement called Dragonerium, whose walls were largely demolished in the second half of the 18th century: medieval traces remain between Gothic capitals, blackbirds and porticoes of the main street. In the center medieval and baroque churches, noble palaces and the Loggia del Grano.

In the former convent of St. Francis, it collects fragments of sculptures and inscriptions from the Picena to the Roman age, with strong ties with Egypt: two Egyptian sculptures (a female deity and a head of Serapide) found at the Sanctuary of the SS. Crucifix, fragments from the Serapean and Roman statuary from the age of Augustus to that of Hadrian and Antoninus.
One of the three frescoes of Italy.
Cross-country skiing in the pines.
A frescoed hermitage and a viewpoint on the Brianza plain.
Visit only on request according to Visit Tuscany
Rock complex of about 1300 square meters with origins around the year 1000: two overlaid frescoed churches, a monastery and houses; it houses contemporary art exhibitions.

Built around the middle of the seventeenth century for Gotthard Frisiani, on a project attributed to Francesco Maria Richini, incorporating as wing a fifteenth-century body of the previous castle; the interior frescoes with a profane subject are Montalto brothers. U-shaped plant with central body, two wings and ample park: the left wing, the oldest, has ogival windows, wooden floors and fifteenth-century frescoes; to the north a portico with three fornics on granite binated columns of Baveno, inside a staircase of honour.

An ancient silk factory built in 1872 by Leo Romanin-Jacur, with a central body for the machinery and spinning rooms and two side wings porticoed; inside the Museo della Filanda, multimedia and immersive, revives the work of adults and children in the ancient spinning mill with a sensory experience.
Borgo delle Crete Senesi with a 14th century civic museum and, not far away, the abbey of Monte Oliveto Maggiore.
Mammoths and saber-toothed tigers from Valdarno.
Built between the 13th and 14th centuries and decorated in Baroque times on a project by Massimiliano Soldani Benzi; there is the relic of the milk of the Virgin donated by Count Guido Guerra.
open every day from sunrise to sunset only from April 15th to June 30th; in the other months visits only by reservation

16th century building whose premises and gardens tell the history of the city and of the noble families that succeeded each other; symbol of the family that ruled Pozzallo, today houses the municipal library.
Church of the hamlet Rovella erected in 1884 on the initiative of the well-off local Pasquale Bonanno, with facade of neoclassical hut and portal in stone arched to the sixth.
A hidden Lombard church.
A century of toys in a historic home.
the MiC card indicates opening only from 1 July to 15 September, with obligatory booking

The highest city in Sicily, almost a thousand meters away: the Lombardy Castle enlarged by Frederick II, the Fortress of Ceres with the Museum of Myth, the Duomo, the octagonal Tower of Frederick II and, 14 km away, the reserve of Lake Pergusa.

Single nave church with side chapels and rectangular presbytery concluded by the apse, decorated with reliefs and mural paintings; on the south side the slender bell tower with square plan with octagonal cusp.
Seven hundred years of art in Pistoia.
At the end of Vicolo Terravecchia the great palace born for defence and then residence; the Porta di Capo is the only surviving door of the medieval walls.
Temporarily closed according to Italia.it

Attested in the Teresian cadastral of 1721, it hosted several times Carlo Porta between 1801 and 1815; the Ballabio created brolo and formal gardens with fountains, nymphs and stone mosaics, Giuseppe Bovara designed the gate in 1816 and Piero Portaluppi restored it in neo-baroque style in 1911-1913. Since 2003 it has been a municipality and park, which are located in the center of Flora Autoctona; the historical gardens are visited on Saturday morning not festive, with views of the Briantian lakes from the entrance.
