Prenuragic tombs dug into the rock, with an atrium, a vaulted cell and two funeral chambers; in the territory there are also 64 nuraghi and twelve tombs of Giants.
The garden of tulips and maze.
The monument symbol of the city.
An island of spot and crystal clear sea to be turned by boat.
To be checked: the price changes according to the current exhibition
Sulfural water at about 375°C of the ancient Etruscan and Roman settlement of Saturnia; at the Waterfalls of the Mulino natural outdoor pools famous in the world.
The MiC card indicates "Closed" every day (site abandoned, waiting for redevelopment); italia.it indicates instead that since 2010 it hosts the City Museum

The hilly village of the Cilento National Park, Vallo di Diano and Alburni, Caselle in Pittari has a high part, "u' Castieddu" with medieval tower and mother church, Mount Pittari with the Cave of San Michele, the swallowery of Bussento and the Lucano settlement of Laurelli.
The saint's personal memories.
MiC card (updated 2020) marks every day as closed and Let's Marche reports museums only partially open

On the ground floor of the former convent of San Michele Arcangelo, on one of the two hills of Montecelio, the museum dedicated to the archaeologist Rodolfo Lanciani, family of the place, exhibits around the cloister finds of the entire municipal territory from prehistory to the seventeenth century. The most famous piece is the Capitolina Triad, with Jupiter, Juno and Minerva sitting with eagle, owl and peacock: the most complete and best preserved example of the group. Renewed, reopened on March 15, 2025 together with the Municipal Historical Archives; open Saturday and Sunday 10-18, reservations on tel. 0774 616107.
The crossroads of the courses Vittorio Emanuele II and Umberto I and the piazza della Torre del Palazzo, where is guarded the Bull from which the procession of Forgive starts.

The medieval village rises on a hill about 3 km from the coast; according to tradition its oldest nucleus was founded by the survivors of the destruction of Kaulon. It is enclosed by four Urbian gates and preserves walls and the remains of the Norman-Byzantine castle, which dominates the highest points of the town and has been recently restored. In the local traditions the Easter Cunfrunta and, every three years, the procession of Sant'Andrea d'Avellino () are located.
The industrial archaeology of oil.
The 400 at the end of the walk.

Purchased in the seventeenth century by Cardinal Federico Borromeo, who hosted seminarians and theologians during the plague of 1630 and died in 1631; Gilberto IV Borromeo, then bishop of Novara and cardinal, designed the renovation, initially entrusted to Filippo Cagnola and completed in the twentieth century by architects Fausto and Giuseppe Bagatti Valsecchi. Today it hosts the International University of the Second Renaissance; how to visit the museum not indicated in the reading sources.
In the Codacchiola district, documents the daily life of the community.
Co-operative Wine of the Heat.
The house of the writer Marino Moretti overlooking the canal harbour, with original furnishings, books and papers.
The Romanesque churches of the village.
Liberty villa built in 1905 on a cliff overlooking the sea, now owned by the City of Capri.
The funerary kiosk monument with pyramidal cover of the early Augustian age, rebuilt in a public garden at the entrance of the village, from the necropolis of Pian di Bezzo.
Baroque church with the dome covered with iridescent majolicas; with San Simplicio is one of the two main identity symbols of the city.
Roman origins.
Small Italian theatre hosted since the eighteenth century in the Old Public Loggia, the first seat of the City, where shows and events are held.
Typical architecture with rascards in wood of Franco-Provençal origin and strong houses entirely in stone.
17th-century church that preserves a highly venerated simulacrum, celebrated at the end of May.
Early Christian frescoes in a quarry.

Two rosé stone villages on the opposite sides of the landslide of Mount Toc, in the Friulan Dolomites Park, marked by the Vajont catastrophe of October 9, 1963: you can visit the crowning of the dam, the Visitor Centre with the exhibitions on tragedy, the Vajont Ecomuseum and trails like that of coal and the Val Zemola.
€11, reduced €9

The Reformed Cistercian monks began at the beginning of the seventeenth century the present building, on the site of a church and houses of the Humiliates of the 14th-XV century; cast out the monks from the French in 1805, it was hospital, button factory, prison, barracks and craft workshop. Today it houses the Town Hall, the civic library and, in the cellars, the municipal historical archive.
Walk in a Roman cistern.
Country shrine with a stretch of Roman road nearby.
The sunset on the rocks.
A fifteenth-century hydraulic work overwhelmed by Bruna.
Corso Umberto is the main street and the heart of social life, with bars and shops; the promenade on the bay is the place of aperitifs and fish dinners.

Ancient walled village with a Renaissance character, divided into regular blocks: the walls have been flattened and the moat of the basement castle, and the ring road follows the path; of the two doors only the southern one remains. Along the main street there are sixteenth-century arcades with arches of every shape, once home to shops, artisans and taverns, on an original cobbled restored; there is also the eighteenth-century residence known as the Villa, with portico with Doric columns. Around, barns, stables and farmhouses tell the rural world.

Above 1500 meters the beech forests cover 10,000 hectares, in an area with more than half of the Sicilian flora and 70 species of orchids; in the Vallone Madonna degli Angeli live about 30 specimens of Nebrodi fir. Among the destinations: the convent of the Madonna dell'Alto, on a cliff overlooking Mount Etna, the Piano Cervi and Pizzo Carbonara (1979), the highest peak of Sicily after Etna, from Piano Battaglia; the tourist office is free to guide to seven excursions by Carl Gardner.
Friulian plain on foot or by bike between streams, mills and villas.
17th-century residence overlooking the Sile, now home to cultural events, exhibitions and ceremonies.
By bike along the Mincio to Mantua.
Seaside resort with unspoilt Mediterranean scrub and white sandstone dunes, close to the calanchi of Cutro and the Marchesato.
The tradition of ropers.
The castle became an Academy.
The sixth stage of the St. Francis' Way starts from the Cathedral of Santa Maria Maddalena and runs 18.7 km through the city and the Marcigliana Nature Reserve to Monte Sacro, in Rome.
Baroque Latin Cross Church, founded before the year 1000 and restored for the first time in 1781. On September 2, the statue of the saint is carried in procession to the main square.

Consecrated in 1571 and already decorated with paintings and sculptures, it was rebuilt between 1880 and 1892 on a project by parish priest Angelo Noacco with different orientation, crypt and baptistery obtained from the ancient apse, which preserves part of the frescoes; the old bell tower (1638-1775) was maintained and a new built not far away. Interior with three naves with polygonal apse.

The main town of the island, between the port, born in 1854 from the opening of the ancient Lake of Bagni, and Ischia Ponte, dominated by the Aragonese Castle; around, the beaches of Lido, the bay of Cartaromana with the thermal springs in the sea and the Tower of Guevara.
The Etruscan Mountains of Tolfa.
A church suspended on the sea.
The symbol of Turin and the view of the Alps.

Holiday resort of the upper Seriana Valley at the foot of the Presolana (2.521 m), the "quegina delle Orobie" (Golden Flag) since 2022: between Castione, Bratto and Dorga Liberty villas from the early twentieth century, churches with furnishings of the Fantoni di Rovetta, the sanctuary of Lantana, the rural village of Rusio with the ancient San Péder, the Valle dei Mulini and the view of the Salto degli Spos.

The National Museums of Lombardy can be visited with the castle only by reservation for groups of at least 15 people; the National Museums of Lombardy have pages on the ...Collezione Strada and on the National Archaeological Museum of Lomellina, not readable: check where the collection is displayed today

The area that hosts the Giant, also known as the Giant supporting the mountain, is a relief of about 4 meters for almost 5 sculpted in a large block of living rock, the Moon's Stone, by the Luzzane sculptor Giosuè Meli, who completed it in 1841 at the age of 25. It is located on the steep slope of the Valle dell'Acqua, in the Costa district, near the river Bragazzo; the posture of the figure recalls the iconography of Pietà.
The Medieval Castrovillari.
Nature and fresh in the woods of the Dauni Mountains.

Opened in 2015 in the Palazzo Marchesale, renovated in the sixteenth century by Giovan Battista I d'Azzia and Giulia di Capua. It exhibits late seventeenth and early eighteenth century majolica in blue monochrome on white, including albarelli, the dish with the Myth of Callisto by Angelo Antonio D'Alessandro and the Amatoria Cup, and the production of the laertine workshops of Seven and Nineteenth century. Open from Tuesday to Sunday 10-12.30 and 16-18.30, closed on Monday.
not indicated: for access contact VIVI Ardesio office, Piazza Monte Grappa 3 (tel. 0346 466265)

On the promontory of Bari Vecchia, between the Swabian Castle and the promenade, the former convent of Santa Chiara, born from a church of the thirteenth century of the Teutonic Knights dedicated to Santa Maria degli Alemanni, next to the former convent of San Francesco della Scarpa; today the headquarters of the Superintendence.
Panoramas from the sea to Majella on a mountain of ancient settlements.

The deposit was active from 1937 to 1964, with nine wells and a hundred kilometers of tunnels up to 179 meters deep, recovered and reopened in 2006 as a museum; in the lamp shed, tools, photographs and videointerviews.

The center, enclosed by remains of medieval walls, preserves the chapel of the Immaculate, the Clock Tower and portals with dates and Latin mottos; the Doge's Palace was built at the beginning of the eighteenth century by the Ghezzi dukes on the remains of the baronial palace, with the coat of arms and motto NON SIBI SED ALIIS, while Palazzo Chironi rises at the end of the nineteenth century on the site of the castle.
The MiC card indicates "Closed" every day; the city reports guided tours by reservation (tel. 0122 54104)

Sanctuary built in 1227 on the hill of the Serrone, outside the ancient walls, and consecrated by Bishop Andrea of San Marco; according to the most likely version reconstructs the old church of the Assumption damaged by earthquakes. Gradinata, balustrade in tuff and portal are by the architect Niccolò Ricciulli of Rogliano; after the earthquake of 12 February 1854 the Greek cross plan was transformed into a neoclassical Latin cross, with Baroque façade and city coat of arms. Inside the Byzantine-style wooden Madonna della Serra (XII-XV century), the Baroque altar of St. Francis, the wooden choir of Giovanbattista Altomare (XVIII century), the Holy Family of Rocco Ferrari and the Sacred Heart in marble by Giulio Barberis.
The Roman forum of today.
A Renaissance sanctuary suspended between Bramante and legend.

Municipality of the Euganean Hills, seat of the Regional Park: at the foot of Mount Lonzina stands the Benedictine Abbey of Praglia, with fifteenth-century cloisters and the monumental Library; in the sixteenth-century Palazzetto dei Vicari there is the contemporary art museum Dino Formaggio and on the summit of the Monte della Madonna the sanctuary entrusted to Praglia in 1508.

Designed at the end of the fifteenth century by Luca Fancelli, it occupied almost the entire main square and was frescoed; it was largely destroyed in the battle of 15 August 1702. The name comes from a tax on the grain that was collected there; above the portal remains the coat of arms of the Gonzaga in colored porcelain.
The historic heart of the city, among towers and excavations.
Church of 1464 and convent erected by the Capuchins in 1540; it preserves two paintings from the late eighteenth century.

On the square the Collegiate designed by Domenico Schiero (1750-1767), with mosaic apse of the Sacred Heart (C. De Angelis, 1950), a altarpiece of the Flagellation attributed to Giulio Romano and a bell of 1247 from the abbey of Valvisciolo; in front of the monumental fountain of Michele Tripisciano, inaugurated in 1890 with the arrival of the water of Mount Carpino wanted by Leo XIII, with dolphins, cups supported by telamoni and a lion.

The Plan stream (Pfeldererbach) is thrown into the Passirio with two jumps of about 19 and 18 meters, admirable by panoramic wooden walkways: from Moso you cross the first road bridge and after about 50 m you take left the path to the walkways. Bus stops ...Moos... Dorf... or Moos.
The medieval village on foot.
The square and the medieval tower.
The nineteenth-century temple in Moorish style, one of the most beautiful buildings of the nineteenth-century Italian, with the community museum.
The 19th-century theatre.
The party that illuminates the bell tower.
Romanesque-Renaissance church built on a pre-existing church in the Dirupo district, recognizable by the large hemispheric dome visible from almost all the center; inside altars and Baroque canvases.

In the watchtower of the 12th century restored in 1995: agricultural tools, millstones and tools of peasant life before industrialization, donated by the families of the country. Free admission; temporarily closed for damage to the earthquake 2016.

The ancient village, developed mainly in the Middle Ages among hills and woods above the Peligna Valley, preserves remains of megalithic walls and fortifications, the Palazzo dei Papi, the palace of Baron Alesi dei Paparelli and the church of Santa Maria degli Angeli.
The symbol of the country and its highest point of view.
The oldest authentic work of Perugino.
Two outings of serpentinitic ophiolite, rare dark green rock clusters of eruptive origin and geological importance, in the two villages a few hundred meters away about 10 km from Serramazzoni.
The rock wall that dominates the village.
Concrets with fantastic shapes.

The mountain town of the lower Val di Susa, mentioned in 1029 as a flourishing parish church in a document of the Abbey of San Giusto di Susa, with a hundred villages; at its border the Colle del Lys, with the natural park and the Ecomuseum of the Resistance.

The only remains of the ancient castle of Suzzara, remembers the family of Matilde di Canossa and is the symbol of the historical past of the city; the provincial source has a date of it not unique (XIII or XIV century).
The municipal tower called "the bell tower," in the square.
The hemp and wine of the Val Vibrata as they used to be.
Inaugurated in 1939, it preserves the image of the Madonna del Rosario painted on a boulder which, according to tradition, grabbed a traveler during a flood of the river Erno.
A painted astrological calendar, unique in the world.
Monastery and parish complex built between the 11th and 18th centuries in the historic centre, at the entrance of the Val d'Ayas.

Born from a Cistercian female monastery of the late 12th century, it passed to the Mornics, Carolina Maumari, Walter Kees and De Marchi, who gave it the eclectic aspect and in 1939 donated it to the State. The route of the museum house touches 14 rooms with original decorations and furnishings, including the Neapolitan Black Room, the Music Room, the Mornic Room, the Neorococo Red Room and the Fermi Room, where Enrico Fermi held his last lessons in 1954. Since 1953, the convention center hosts the summer courses of the Italian School of Physics.
Roman Milan.
Four thousand exhibits and an immersive set-up in two locations.
Panels with reproductions of the works of the painter Angelo Morbelli, who lived in the hamlet Colma.

16th century palace attributed to Pellegrino Tibaldi, home of Prefecture and Province, with staircase of honor, Doric courtyard, the Civic Tower of the Clock of medieval origin and a garden with marble fountain of Baveno.
A small Farfense church.

The museum and documentation centre, housed in the premises adjacent to the Town Hall, contains testimonies and images of the feast of San Domenico and the Serpari. The Study Centre has a large library dedicated to the most popular events in Abruzzo and organizes educational activities for schools and visitors. Times not indicated by sources: contact the Municipality (tel. This appropriation is intended to cover the costs of the implementation of the programme for the period from 1 January 2014 to 31 December 2014.
A small church overlooking the valley.
Aligi Sassu's color math.

Borgo della Valle di Comino with a historical centre walled from the 13th century and palaces from the 16th to the 19th century, the Baroque collegiate church of Giacomo Del Sole and, in the hamlet Roselli, the seventeenth-century sanctuary of Santa Maria delle Rose; the civic museum houses the remains of Cominium and the former Roman vows of Pescarola.

Borgo dell'alta Val Bormida founded in 1206 by Marquis Enrico II Del Carretto, among the most beautiful villages in Italy: the fortified bridge of the Gaietta, the castle and the Napoleonic Museum in Villa Scarzella; truffle land.
The Calabrian baroque with stuccoes and frescoes.
World famous climbing next to the dam.
The early Christian heart of the island.
The dark-room sundial.
The medieval symbol of the city.
Farm life.
The great Marian shrine of the Sibillini.

On the banks of the Orba, it is a closed agglomeration formed by a central noble courtyard with palace, church and park, to which four rustic courts have been added over the centuries. It was the center of a vast feud spread over the municipalities of Predosa, Alexandria, Bosco and Fresonara, with numerous farms, meadows, pastures and streams; still today it is surrounded by cultivated fields. It was opened on FAI Spring Days 2016, 2017 and 2018.

In the south wing of the ancient Augustinian monastery, the museum created by the ethnographer Giuseppe Šebesta defines itself as a museum of technique and popular technology.About 12,000 objects in 43 rooms tell how Alpine people faced the scarcity of resources. There are the agricultural hall with the collection of ploughs, the large water machines (mill, sawmill, sweat and noria, in operation until the sixties of the twentieth century; the mill was dismantled piece by piece and reassembled here by Šebesta), the rooms of the peasant house with the stüa and curiosity as the bugs scare bears. Since 2002 the Provincial Archives of oral tradition has been located there; open from Tuesday to Sunday and Monday holidays, 10-18.
Inside the thirteenth century with a barrel vault and frescoes of the fifteenth century well preserved by Ottaviano Nelli da Gubbio; it was the seat of the Monte di Pietà.

At the highest point of the Parco della Pieve, two concentric rows of stone seats around a drilled circular bench: here the representatives of the Community, usually on May 1st to elect the Scario and August 15th, voting with marbles inserted in the forum. In the sixteenth century there were held trials for witchcraft: 28 condemned, 18 at the stake.

Sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy sandy beaches of Olivella and Fondachello, the Bay of Corsari, the bay of Solanto and the coves of rocks with clear seabeds rich in posidonia and curls; the Scoglio della Formica is a reference point for underwater fishing.
The life of the miners in the valley, with a life-size gallery.

In a 19th-century palace donated by the Settanni family, on the path of the ancient moat and overlooking the course: on the first floor there are rooms with painted ceilings for exhibitions of the capitular heritage, the second didactic workshops and restoration of wood; other paintings are exhibited in the ancient sacristies of the Matrice church.
Read Pavese walking in its places.

Country on the Po with eight centuries of history: the Mission chapel with frescoes of the fifteenth century, the parish church of Santo Stefano, the sanctuary and the remains of the castle of Cantogno and the Path of the Ochette along the river.
The largest center of the Pollino National Park, in the King's Conca: the Aragonese castle, the medieval quarter of the Cìvita and the Franciscan protoconvento of 1220, home of museum and theatre.
The river with clear blue waters that crosses the city.
The campaign of kings.

A neoclassical mother church, restored several times between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, which preserves the main sacred works of the country, including the cycle of frescoes by the painter Toscani on the miracle of the Madonna della Consolazione: according to tradition in 1798 Our Lady and her angels saved the country from the plundering of French troops. In front, next to the Town Hall, the Bell of the Bicentenary merged in 1998 by the Fonderie Marinelli of Agnone, with the inscription   Â"Città della Solidarietà" (City of Solidarity).

Detachable section of the diocesan Museum of Tortona inaugurated in 2009, occupies two rooms on the noble floor of Palazzo Spinola overlooking the central hall. It exhibits paintings and sculptures, often unpublished, from the parishes of Val Borbera, many without a resident parish priest, with panels that connect each work to the church of origin.
The sacred art treasure of Valsesian craftsmen.
The collection donated to the city in 1927 by Count Giuseppe Primoli, son of Princess Carlotta Bonaparte, with his collection of works of art.
The most beloved Marian sanctuary in Trentino.
Cinquecento cards, plants of the French fortress, drawings of Venetian engineers (1593-1797), coins and medals of the foundation and documents of the Italian period until the retreat of Caporetto.
the source indicates the inside of the church of San Domenico at the moment not visitable

From the Porta ai Campi (14th century) on Piazza Cavour you can climb up via Roma, lined with medieval buildings and houses, to Piazza Matteotti, the heart of the castle since its foundation, with the 13th century Podestà Loggia covered with noble coats of arms and the Palace of the Municipal Historical Archive. Of the three doors there is also Porta Fontana, to the west; at the top of the village the remains of the medieval fortress among the olive trees.
Walk in the Ibleo Liberty.

Historical structure of fortified military architecture, today also cultural center, acquired by the City at the end of 2013 with the federalism state, thanks to an agreement with the State and the Ministry of Culture. You will visit with guided tours on special dates, such as National Castle Days (May 2024 Sundays, 15-16.30, adults €10 and under 14 €5), with recommended reservation on the fort's website.

In the former church of St. Peter, built on a classical temple: stone sculptures of the ancient and medieval city, liturgical furnishings, statues and paintings from the Middle Ages to the contemporary age, and the fresco of the Madonna del Latte. Closed on Monday.
The door in the sixteenth-century walls from which you enter north of Via Fillungo; in the square just inside there is a tourist office.
Centre of Anglona on the border with the Gallura marked by the Coghinas, with a history that starts from the Paleolithic: the archaeological and Paleobotanic museum with the mother

Documented from the 10th century, in the center of the village of San Giovanni, owes its current appearance especially to the changes of the eighteenth century and preserves a crucifix of the fourteenth century. From the village the view ranges from the Valley of the Beaches and from the peaks of the Alpe di Catenaia to the hills of Chianti.
The square that corresponds to the ancient Jewish ghetto, stage of the medieval itinerary of the city.

Marchirolo, in Valmarcarcarolo, keeps in the Gipsoteca Spazio Sculpture Pellini Bozzolo the plasters of the sculptors Eugenio and Eros Pellini and Adriano Bozzolo, linked to the local tradition of the gessers and the "picapietra" (paintings) and from the parish church of San Martino you go up to the church of San Paolo, a panoramic point and leads the paths of the Cadorna Line towards Monte La Nave.
Roman and Lombard fortress, recently restored; the archaeological excavations inside have brought to light a necropolis with funerary furnishings.
Quieter than Marina.
The pink flamingos just a stone's throw from the beach.
The large bridge that leads to Palazzo Chigi and Piazza di Corte, symbol of Ariccia together with the palace; underneath is the Vallericcia.
according to Italia.it access to abandoned houses was not allowed

The Calore rises from Mount Accellica and forms several waterfalls: the most famous is the Lavandaia Waterfall, at the foot of the Sanctuary of the Santissimo Salvatore, under a bridge of the 1st century BC and with the ruins of a mill active from the 15th century to the fifties; the Maronnella Waterfall, hidden in the green and dear to the fishermen of trout; the Fascio Waterfall, towards Acerno, an artificial basin of fascist epoch over eight meters high, with a bridge without parapets.

At the gates of Parma between the Taro and the woods of Carrega: the Romanesque parish church of San Prospero on the pilgrim's street, the Court of Giarola with the Museums of Pomodoro and Pasta, the museum of the daily newspaper of Ettore Guatelli in Ozzano Taro and two regional parks.

Inaugurated in 1808, wanted by nine families of the village in the Napoleonic era and called "Concordia" in the ideals of the French Revolution: 99 seats between stages and audiences, boxes entirely in wood and bell plan for acoustics; vault and boxes frescoed by Cesare Agretti and his son Luigi, then 15 years old (1892). Closed in 1951 and collapsed the roof, it was restored with the autotaxation of the inhabitants and European funds until 1993; in 1997 it was twinned with the Farnese Theatre of Parma. Gina Lollobrigida debuted there in 1945. Shows and guided tours by the Society of the Theatre of Concordia (Tel. +39 075 8780737).

Country of about 1,900 inhabitants on the left bank of the Aterno, in the valley once inhabited by the Vestini; in the hamlet of Stiffe, on the edge of the Regional Park Sirente-Velino, open the Grotte di Stiffe, while a short distance from the village there is the small karst lake of Sinizzo.
Dedicated to Richard Whateley West, who portrayed the light of the Mediterranean in his works.

Civic museum with the original plaster models of the sculptor Giulio Monteverde, born in Bistagno in 1837, which cover his production from 1870 to 1917; part of the collection was donated by his daughters in Genoa in 1919 and partly returned to Bistagno with donations and loans. Open Saturday and Sunday from spring to autumn, in other periods by reservation (tel. +39 0144 79301, +39 366 5442354); adheres to Castelli Aperti.
The karst of the valley.
On the Appia street, on the trail of Cicero.

The grenade of San Marco cuts into two the center: on the one hand the Terra district, an intrica of steep alleys, on the other the Santa Caterina district, built in the nineteenth century on an orthogonal plan. The two districts are joined by a high viaduct, the Garibaldi Bridge, from which you can see the churches and cave settlements overlooking the gravina. The name of the city would come from the Latin "massa fracta" (fracta), a fractured rock.

Maritime villa of Julian-Claudia age (1st century A.D.), with reconstructions in brick from the 2nd century, partly incorporated in the eighteenth century farmhouse of San Limato. At the lower level a cryptoportico in mixed work; to the north the spa district with frigidarium in black and white mosaic with marine animals, tepidarium and calidarium; to the south three residential areas with niches, apses and mosaic and marble floors.
The view of the plain of Gela.
The handmade ceramics of the Coast.

A simple and safe route that runs along the river Tresinaro to the village of Cà de Caroli and to the bridge of Via del Cristo, with resting areas and panoramic points; it is part of the Spallanzani Path, which in 1988 had the official starting point in Ventoso.
Museum that collects and exhibits testimonies of the peasant civilization and archaeological finds found in the municipal territory, related to the native populations. Tel. 0183 90200.
The arches of the gladiator's amphitheatre.
Place dedicated to Our Lady and venerated from the fourteenth century, when there was found a statue; the current building is from 1851.
The symbol of Friuli's reconstruction.

On the banks of the Oglio, between the plains, Franciacorta and Sebino, Palazzolo is dominated by the Tower of the People, about 92 meters high, erected on the Mirabella Tower of Rocha Magna; in front, beyond the ancient bridge, the Medieval Rocchetta. From 1428 under Venice, as St. Mark's Lion remembers on the tower, it is also the end of the historic Railway of Sebino.

In the Flaminio district the house-study built between 1922 and 1925 by the Norwegian-American sculptor, lived in Rome from 1898 to 1940, with the monumental statues of the utopian project of the "World City."
The small neoclassical church built between 1797 and 1819, with the concave façade and the interior with central plan with a coffered dome.
The gate of the eighteenth century in Catania.
Faithful reconstruction of floating mills that inspired Bacchelli's novel, moored at the dock and visited in every condition of the river.
The oldest church, on the remains of a Roman temple.

The village rises from the coast of the Strait towards the slopes of Aspromonte and is formed by two districts: the medieval nucleus around the castle (Suso), once walled and with a gate, and the eighteenth-century-nineteenth-century quarter of Praci to the east. Walls and many palaces have been lost, but the streets still follow the concentric circles of the ancient ramparts. It is reached by train to Lazarus and then by bus.
The "city of enchanted stone" with one of the most beautiful squares in Italy, the Romanesque churches with white and green stripes and the Robbiano del Ceppo frieze; the "Santiago d'Italia."
Borgo della Valdichiana Sienese at the foot of Mount Cetona, whose caves have been inhabited since the Neanderthals.
A Gothic Madonna in a country shrine.
The theatre of 1880, entitled to the musician Massese Alessandro Guglielmi.
Romanesque Basilica of 1062 in the open countryside, in Calmedia, rest of the ancient Bosa vetus, with the thirteenth-century façade in red trachyte.

Born as a prehistoric castle, the hill was the scene of clashes between Romans and Istrians, then castrum and finally fortress, refuge of the population during the raids, especially Turkish. Inside the walls stands the sanctuary of the Blessed Virgin Assumption, a pilgrimage destination, built in 1512 and repeatedly expanded and restored; according to tradition, Our Lady left a mark on a nearby rock, considered a symbol of fertility. The wedding of the karst weddings is celebrated there.

Born from the geological collection that the doctor conducted Domenico Dal Lago collected by visiting patients and donated to the City in 1929; catalogued in 1975 by Paolo Mietto of the University of Padua, it was established as a museum in 1982, opened in 1995 in Villa Valle and transferred in 1999 to Palazzo Festari. Fossils and finds of the Valle dell'Agno retrace almost 300 million years; in the garden, wooden reconstructions of a velociraptor and a pteranodon, steel silhouettes on the evolution of life and a stratigraphic pyramid. Saturday with timetables indicated by the museum, the other days upon reservation.
A rare round cathedral.

On the southern slopes of Monte Grappa, among hills that open onto the Veneto plain, Romano d'Ezzelino offers the wild Valle Santa Felicita for trekking, mountain biking and free flight, the villa Ca' Cornaro with its nineteenth-century park, the remains of the castle of the Ezzelini on Colle Bastia and the Museum of the Car Bonfanti-Vimar.
The belt of about 570 meters with 14 towers that closes the village, built by Siena to defend against Florence; Dante compares it to the giants in Hell.
Vincenzo Pagani's shovel.

The church of San Lorenzo Martire was built in 1693 and is housed in an 18th-century olive mill restored in front of the farm Sant'Angelo de' Graecis, also called Abazia di San Lorenzo, born in the 12th century from the rocky settlement of Lama di San Lorenzo. It exhibits tools of olive-tree processing; behind the palace there is an ancient citrus grove. Open Friday and Saturday 17:30-20:00, best contact first.
The collection of the greatest antiques of the nineteenth century: sculptures, paintings, weapons, carpets in the blue rooms of his palace.

Neoclassical villa of the late 18th century on the lakefront, residence of the accounts Print: originally in U, lost its two wings in 1806 to make room for the Napoleonic road of the Sempione. Manzoni, married in second marriage to Teresa Borri, widow Print, attended her since 1839 and remained there for a long time between 1848 and 1850, writing the discourse "Del novel storico" and the dialogue "Dell'inventione" . Today it houses a bank, apartments and offices: you can see it from the outside.
The nineteenth-century theatre of the city, still fully active.
The Norman Cathedral.

Narrow streets, noble palaces and workshops of artisans who produce traditional objects; in the buildings you use the gentle stone, which takes its name from one of the surrounding mountains. The village rises in a wide plain in the heart of the park, where the National Park was established on 9 September 1922.
To know the nature of the Dauni Mountains.
The bell tower, perhaps from the 11th to the 11th century, has a very rare tiara cusp in Valle d'Aosta, perhaps in memory of the popes in Avignon.
The archaeology of Barbagia.
The wrapper façade.
The founding king, on the waterfront.

The municipality of the Cilento National Park, with its hamlets Camel, Mercato and Vatolla; in Vatolla the philosopher Giambattista Vico lived from 1686 to 1695 in Palazzo Vargas, now the seat of the Vico Foundation, and according to tradition he read under a secular olive tree of the Convent of Pietà.
The pedestrian path that in about 20 minutes climbs from the center to the abbey of Santa Maria del Monte on the Spaziano hill.
The lake tour is just a stone's throw from the village.

In front of Stresa, it is the only one of the Borromean Islands inhabited in a continuous way, with narrow alleys and a market of handicrafts; in Ferragosto a procession of fishing boats carries the statue of the Assumption around the island. The Palazzo Borromeo, already home to Arturo Toscanini, is private and not visitable.
The beautiful old town with the portico market, the churches and the civic theatre, stop of the Via del Volto Santo.

Leucopetra, white stone in Greek, is the rocky wall about 150 meters high on the sea that dominates the cape of Capo d'Armi; it appears in the Tabula Peutingeriana and Strabone placed there the end of the Apennines chain. Since 1867 the lighthouse that marks the border between the Strait and the southern Ionian coast has been operating there. In 43 B.C. Cicero, fleeing to Greece, was stopped here by a storm and hosted by his friend Publio Valerio, as the Letters to Atticus recall.
The mother church of the village, the heart of Piazza del Duomo.
A naturalistic path between prehistoric castelliers and Roman traces.

Next to the parish church of Sant'Agata: works of the church such as the Spousalizio di Santa Caterina di Bicci di Lorenzo (1430) and Robbian terracotta, and finds of Mugello from the Paleolithic to the age of metals with the reconstruction of a prehistoric village.

Village on the hill with fifteenth-century door, ancient tower and streets from stone arches set like a Roman camp; the name recalls the console Claudio Marcello (155 BC). View of the Gulf of Poets with Tino and Tinetto.
The walk on the walls to the sea.
The peaks of Ussita with a view to the sea.
A century of Abruzzo peasant life, room by room.
Palace built in the second half of the sixteenth century, today municipal space for exhibitions, conferences and cultural events.
Sanctuary of the Madonna della Libera, symbol and patron saint of the village, celebrated on the first Sunday of May.
The treasure of the High Town.
Two castle villages in the Orvieto countryside.
Fanzago's ciborium and De Matteis' canvas.
The small village inside the castle belt, with the houses Formentini, Dornberg and Tasso that house the provincial museums.

The town of Valnerina is a world pilgrimage destination for Saint Rita (1381-1457), with the sanctuary at the top of the village and, a few kilometers away, Roccaporena with the birthplace and the Scoglio of prayer; in the walled center the churches of St. Francis, St. Augustine and the Collegiate, the museum of Palazzo Santi and the church-museum of St. Anthony Abbot, and on the plateau of Chiavano the Roman remains of Villa San Silvestro.

At 1,370 meters, in a clearing of the beech forest of the Orecchiella Park, it gathers about 400 species of the flora of the Lucca Apennines and the Apuan Alps, including rare or endangered plants and species of medicine and popular food, divided for environments: woods, pastures, moors, bogs, gravels, rocks. Among the blooms, from spring to summer, peonies, lilies, orchids, gentian, the Apuan widow and paradise.
The cloister of the Franciscan monastery dates back to the fourteenth century and was once used as a citrus warehouse.

A place of Waldensian worship has been documented since 1692, a hut with straw roof replaced by loose in 1724; after long disputes the current temple was built in 1828-29. Inside wooden floor, gallery raised on three sides, pulpit and pipe organ in front of the entrance and semicircle benches.
Two jumps of water a few steps from the village.

About 4 km of fine sandy coast, on whose beaches was recorded the nesting of the sea turtle Caretta caretta; the marina, repopulated stablely after the earthquake of 1947, has grown since the Sixties with seaside tourism.
A walk to close with the ham of the country.

The Gothic gate that closes the old town was demolished by the Municipality in 1878 and rebuilt by Camillo Massimo in 1880. The name of the village derives from the Roman gens of the Rubri, settled in the area after the submission of the Equi in 304 BC.
The two wars told in a castle.
Look for the "diamond" on the archangel's finger.

Church of the XII-XIII centuries with the altar of the Rosary made by Lombard artists called "i Fiamminghi" (Flemish).It preserves the mummy of a woman of the seventeenth century, the "Morta di Agrano" (Morta of Agrano), for a long time object of popular devotion and numerous ex-vote.
In the historic center the 14th century Cathedral of Saints Peter and Paul; in Tarvisio Bassa the eighteenth-century church of the Blessed Virgin of Loreto.

An easy ring of 28 km (about 2 hours by bike) that leaves and arrives in Gavirate and, counterclockwise, touches Biandronno, Bodio Lomnago, Azzate, the Schiranna, Calcinate and Voltorre; it crosses the village of Biandronno in full and in the first stretch passes from the boarding point of the boat to Isolino Virginia. Along the tour the beaches of Cazzago Brabbia and Bodio Lomnago, the church of Our Lady of the Lake and the Cloister of Voltorre.
A city of the dead with a regular plant.
visits on request, today used for conferences
The churchyard of the winds.
Visitable only on request with reservation required (tel. 0828 332684)

Among the best preserved medieval villages of Bergamasca, on a rocky spur above the Brembo, you can only reach it on foot for ancient mule tracks. Built on several levels (market at the bottom, houses at the center, church at the top), it has a high street porticoed with stone arches, wooden beams and cobbled; the imperial eagle granted to the Tassos is still visible on a wall. The valley road of 1592 isolated it, preserving its appearance.
Country of the Reggian plain gathered around the Fortress Estense, which houses the Coppelli art gallery and the agriculture museum, with a private car museum and the 17th century parish.
Roman tufa tufas with water.

Seaside resort at the south-eastern end of Sardinia, with about twenty beaches in the protected marine area of Capo Carbonara, between Porto Giunco and the pond of Notteri with flamingos, Simius, Campulongu and Punta Molentis, the islands of Cavoli and Serpentara, the Spanish Old Fortress and the archaeological museum of submerged treasures.
Free beach in the natural park towards Torre del Lago, with spontaneous dunal vegetation that protects it from erosion.
In front of the Palazzo del Bargello: who turns three times around the fountain and gets wet, in front of a eugubino that certifies it, gets the \'patente da madto \'.

Well-preserved medieval fortress of the Marquis Longhi De Paolis since the end of the sixteenth century; there was imprisoned Pope Celestine V in 1296, who according to tradition died there after ten months using the step of the altar as a pillow. You can visit the cell, the small sanctuary of Celestino V built by the Longhi, furnishings and relics mostly nineteenth century and the case with the embalmed body of the little Francesco Longhi Caetani, who died at five years. Visits by reservation required.
The cross on the spur.

Abbey founded from 1027 on a small church before 910; the complex was largely demolished in the second half of the eighteenth century and remain the church, the bell tower of 1293 (abbot Allebene), the ancient cemetery, the rectory and a stone well of Istria. Inside the sarcophagus-Mausoleum of Marsilio I da Carrara (first half of the fourteenth century), an ancient pavement mosaic (X-XIII century) and a polychrome terracotta group of the Deposition attributed to Andrea Briosco (XVI century).

The castle was built by Orvieto in 1052 to guard the northern border; the imposing walls remain and the North Gate, the ancient entrance to the base of the Mozza Tower, while the South Gate opens the other side of the center. Inside the walls colorful squares, alleys and an ancient medieval well.
After the rocky detachment of 19 January 2017 the Municipality inhibited access to the stairway of the sanctuary, waiting for the safety and reopening of worship: verify the current accessibility
Everything turns on foot in no time.

Quoted in 1308 as Monasterium S. Petri de Valle was located outside the village in Votta; in 1601 Bishop Julius Santucci ordered its reconstruction in the village and the new church was inaugurated in 1621. The façade is simplified by a nineteenth-century restoration, inside with three naves with six side chapels and barrel vault, holy waterworks with shell in red marble of Levanto; the bell tower with square base on three orders marks the profile of the village.

Tower of sighting on a rocky ridge near the sea, of the system of coastal towers built between 1559 and 1567 against Turkish raids; square plan on three floors (deposit, accommodation of soldiers, battery), with entrance at the top reachable by a staircase. It was called Torre d'Acqua Perropata for a nearby waterfall; the tradition binds to San Benedetto a cannon blow that sank two Turkish ships, remembered every year by a procession of boats.
A 12th century parish and the remains of an abbey.

From the church of San Paolo the path in the woods in Alpe Paci crosses the works of the Cadorna Line: escape routes, niches where supplies were kept and two small barracks to shelter. Continuing towards the summit of Mount La Nave, two paths lead to the observatory, with an entrance arch.

Aiello is the point of arrival of the first stage of the Celestial Way, from Aquileia (about 16.6 km, 4 hours and a half, slight difficulty), and departure of the second towards Cormòns (about 18 km, 5 hours, 140 m of difference in altitude).
Monumental entrance of the Upper City that testifies to the Venetian domination.
The waterfall mentioned by Dante in the canto XVI of Hell, reachable on foot from San Benedetto in Alpe in less than two hours.
Roman mosaics next to the sanctuary.
The house of the painter Vittorio Cerami, survived the battle of Capo Matapan in the Second World War, keeps his paintings and letters from the front.
The fourteenth century portal and the wheel of the exhibits.

It rises on a high sandstone cliff, reached by a stone bridge with several arches, and dominates the Camastra Valley. On the site of a Byzantine hermitage, it was rebuilt in stone by the Normans in the 11th century, renovated by the Angioini around 1250, transformed by the Orsini Del Balzo in the Renaissance and then into a noble residence, with the last major intervention in the 18th century. It has two courtyards, the one representing the mast, drawbridge, shoe walls, portals and Renaissance balustrade; the cliff is recognized as a geosite. Visits by reservation at the municipal offices.

A cylindrical tower up to 27 meters high built in 1289 by Charles II of Anjou as an outpost to defend Gaeta, with belt and two doors to land and to the sea; it rises on the remains of Roman baths, visible from a glass floor with calidarium and frigidarium. It was long of the Caetans, damaged in war and then restored with a Renaissance portal brought by Gaeta.

Fortified building on the eastern tip of the ancient hill of Eraclea, in the Old Borgata: it testifies to the feudal past of Policoro, with under the "casalini" the small houses of the farm workers. You can see it from the outside.
Walk under the historic arcades.

Borgo del Molise centrale with the medieval quarter of Morrutto, the walls with three doors, the abbey palace with the coat of arms of Cardinal Orsini (later Pope Benedict XIII) and churches with paintings by Giuseppe Castellano; about 2 km, on Colle Rimontato, the italic temple of the Sannitic age.
The pastoral culture of the Cuneo Alps in one museum.

Regional Park established in 1984, one of the first in Lombardy, along the 73 km of the Mincio; without timetables or gates. In Ponti it extends from the village to the river, with the area of the Swamp retrained with hedges and a walkway; there passes the cycle path Mantua-Peschiera, also walkable, with branch for Ponti.

Protected oasis of international importance on the right bank of the Piave, established in 1971, owned by the State property and managed by the Carabinieri Biodiversity of Belluno: 92 hectares of wetlands, riparian forests, meadows and shrubs with 45 species of nesting birds, eight of amphibians, hares, wild boars, deer and deer, and rare orchids in the meadows. Open 8-18.

In one of the boats of Palazzo Tullio Altan, one of the most illustrious in the territory, tells on several floors the rural life: the kitchen with the fogolâr, the room with the mattresses of corn leaves, the bachiculture with many types of cocoons, spinning and weaving. The complex includes an Italian garden and, beyond the wall in the Chamber, a restored romantic park with a collection of vintage roses.

Above the historic centre remain part of the tower of the ancient medieval castle and traces of the oldest defensive structures; it is reached on foot and is among the Pavesian places signalled by the Foundation.
Sienese painting of the fifteenth century outside the museums.
A 16th-century fraternity oratory.
The most spectacular viewpoint in the city.

Borgo 500 meters between the valleys of Potenza and Chienti, home of Vernaccia di Serrapetrona DOCG: the fourteenth-century church of San Francesco with the polyptych of Lorenzo d'Alessandro, the square with Santa Maria and Palazzo Claudi, the lake of Caccamo and the castle of San Venanzo on Mount Letegge.
Seven thousand years of history of the territory on the Po.
A walk between the noble palace and the churches of the village.
Snorkeling under the Faraglioni.

A village of medieval origins of the Lepini Mountains, about 110 km from Rome on a spur of the Monte Nero, grown around the Baronale Doria Pamphili Palace that today houses the EtnoMuseum of the Lepini Mountains; 850 meters is the Hermitage of Sant'Erasmo (XI-XII century), reachable on foot between holm oaks and olive groves.
A huge Gothic basilica, a stone's throw from the MANU.
€6, reduced €4, family €16

Small church that in 1612 belonged to the confraternity of the "good death" (Good Death), it is accessed by a large seventeenth-century arch and houses an altar in golden wood, a crucifix considered miraculous and a canvas with Salome and the head of the Baptist.
Sanctuary of the village of San Pietro dedicated to the Madonna of Light, celebrated on September 8 with the arrival of thousands of pilgrims.
Dedicated to the patron, whose sarcophagus it preserves, built on the remains of two previous sacred buildings.
The walk at the height of the walls, 11 meters high, to see the city from a new perspective.
Treasure and royal tombs for a fee

From the summit you can enjoy a panorama from the sea to the Alps; a hiking ring of the Aveto Park starts from the Scoglina Pass (in the municipality of Favale), crosses a beech forest to the Aquapendente and the top and returns to Barbagelata along a stretch of the Alta Via (about 4 hours, medium difficulty). A walled village about 100 meters above sea level, on the promontory of the Circeo linked to the myth of Ulysses and the Maga Circe: the Tower of the Templars with the exhibition "Homo sapiens" and habitats, the Grotta Guattari of the Neanderthals, the acropolis of Circe and the paths towards the Circe Peak in the Circeo National Park.

Opened on 22 April 2001 at the initiative of Velia Micheletti and a group of children of emigrants, it collects personal cards, photographs, documents, letters, passports and old suitcases of Roasians from the end of the eighteenth century. The route reconstructs the first migrations to Africa and the figure of D'Alberto, a pioneer who worked on railways and roads and was nicknamed King of the Golden Coast, with traces of the port of Takoradi, the bridge over Zambesi and the Independence House of Lagos. From May to October open Saturday and Sunday 15-18; other days by reservation (tel. 0163 87818 / 333 7232028).

Built above the castle, it is the only fortified building and the largest of the village, with a large portico; today it houses the College of Rogationist Fathers. The hamlet, an ancient fortress linked to the Abbey of Farfa, has a viewpoint with a wide view of the Parco dei Monti Lucretili and houses the MusAq, museum dedicated to the royal eagle of Monte Pellecchia. Born as a small country church dedicated to St. Peter in Vulpiate, it takes its name from the resemblance to the Sacred Mount of Varallo; already in the sixteenth century it recalled faithful for the image of the Virgin who gives a pear to the Child. A central plan with elliptical compartment and ten chapels, it was frescoed for decades by the Valsesian Lorenzo Peracino (1748-1781), with the large dome of the Coronation of the Virgin and Paradise (1765-1767) considered the masterpiece; sculptures of Dionigi Compassola and neoclassical statues of Giuseppe Argenti (1841-1842). Open every day from 8 am to 6 pm.

Elegant palace of 1732 overlooking St. Peter's Square, home of the exhibitions of the MUDI (Museo Diffuso), including a section dedicated to Adolfo Porry Pastorel, mayor from 1952 to 1960.

Born as a pier to defend the beach from the Vomano gravels and the marshes, it became a pier with the renewal of the area in 1983; it stretches for more than one hundred meters to a roundabout overlooking the coast. In the former church of San Francesco (1368), enlarged and frescoed in the Quattro e prima Cinquecento, reopened in 2003 after the earthquake of 1997. It has a shaped cross from the second half of the thirteenth century, the great polyptych by Niccolò di Liberatore, known as the pupil, painted in 1483 for the main altar of the Duomo, the Encounter of Gioacchino and Anna at the Aurea Gate of Matteo da Gualdo with his frescoes and his circle, and two Longobard furnishings from the necropolis of the Portone, in storage by the Museum of the High Middle Ages in Rome. Fortified nucleus of the village with Renaissance palace, two towers (one pentagonal) and the cell in which the brothers held St. Thomas Aquinas in 1244-45, then transformed into a chapel; the Doge's Palace had five floors, the last three demolished after the earthquakes of 1703 and 1915. Sections of mineralogy, zoology, malachology (shells), paleontology, a herbarium and a scientific library. Sibillini plateau at 1509 m, between the municipalities of Fiastra and Sarnano: panorama of the peaks of the Marche and the Adriatic, violet blooms, narcisi, peonies and orchids between May and June, walking and mountain biking trails and winter ski slopes.

Meilogu village built in red trachite, with the parish church of San Lorenzo and the Romanesque church of San Michele donated in 1113 to the Camaldolese, the contemporary art museum of the Fondazione Logudoro Meilogu and, in a nearby valley, the Romanesque complex of Santa Maria di Cea.

Village on the plateau south of Orvieto with the fourteenth-century church of San Biagio and the historical park of Villa Paolina; in the territory the Tomb of the Hescanas, the only Etruscan sepulchre of Umbria with the original paintings on the walls, and the thirteenth-century castle of Castel Rubello.

On the main altar the polyptych of the Assumption of Gaudenzio Ferrari and the wooden statue of the Madonna dell'Aiuto (1602) by Fabrizio De Magistris; bell tower of 1584. Closed on Wednesdays.

The most important church of the Vimercate parish dates back to the 10th century and is a key example of pre-Romanesque architecture in Brianza, with a Romanesque bell tower. Country of the National Park of Maiella linked to the family of Benedetto Croce, known above all for the archaeological park of Iuvanum, Sannite city and then Roman town of Carricini on a plateau at 972 meters, with hole, basilica, theatre and acropolis of the temples.

Small village of the Monferrato astigiano between wheat fields and pastures, dominated by the large eighteenth-century castle with park and geometric garden; the pumpkins are the gastronomic specialty of the village.

Village between hills of vineyards and olive groves in Trapani, dominated by the Norman-Svevo castle wanted by Frederick II: historic center in stone "campanedda" with the districts of Giudecca and Rabato, the remains of the Mother Church collapsed in 1968, the Museum Pole in the former Jesuit College and the village of the Bronze Age of Mokarta.

Medieval village on the hill Sant'Angelo, between the Ausoni Mountains, with the castle tower, the gates of the ancient walls, the church of San Michele Arcangelo and the Collegiate Church of San Giovanni; the Museum of the Lands of Confine tells its border history between the Papal State and the Kingdom of Naples, and in the territory the karst of Campo Soriano opens.

Monastery complex founded in the ninth century in the Calore valley, in the Middle Ages was one of the most important religious centers in the area and played a role in the spread of Benedictine monasticism in the South; destroyed and rebuilt several times after invasions, earthquakes and lootings. There are still parts of the ancient church, sections of mosaic floor, fragments of frescoes and other medieval structures, in an archaeological area that documents the monastic life. The centre tells about 5,000 years of man's work in Val Petronio: an interactive museum in the former school of Masso, an excavation area that brings back to the Age of Copper (about 3500 BC) and the Galleria XX Settembre, a copper mine active in the nineteenth century and indicated as the only mine that can be visited in Liguria with an underground route. Excavations indicate that Mass is the oldest copper mine in Western Europe. Guided tours: from 15 June to 14 September Wednesday and Friday at 18, Saturday and Sunday at 10.30 and 18; from 15 September to 14 June on Sunday at 10.30, 14 and 16. Tel. 0185 469139.

The cable car ...La Panoramica is usually open from May to October and climbs to the Pradel plateau at 1,367 metres, with views of the lake and the village; from here a 20-minute path (or a chairlift) leads to the La Montanara mountain hut, and starts the trails towards Cima Paganella.

Large boulder in the historic centre: from its top the look ranges from the Maritime Alps to the Gran Paradiso. From the viewpoint of Piazza Primo Maggio, at the entrance from Collegno, you can see the Alpine arch with the Monviso in the center.
