Villa of the fourth century A.D. discovered during the works of the Palermo-Messina motorway, with large polychrome mosaics of African taste comparable to those of the Villa del Casale and Tellaro. The small antiquarium, opened in 2001, exhibits ceramics, amphorae, terracotta, goldsmiths, coins, a bronze circus card and marbles of the villa. cumulative ticket with Tindari €11.20 (reduced €5).
The fortress between the city and the abbey.

This old church, to distinguish it from the new parish with the same dedication, is located on a Romanesque building of the thirteenth century, which has been renovated several times. It contains frescoes from the 15th and 16th centuries, including a San Cristoforo and episodes from the life of Simonino da Trento.
Large rocky ridge overlooking the village, in the heart of the Pollino National Park.
Designed by Michelangelo Pistoletto in the former Trumpet wool mill along the Deer, an example of industrial archaeology, the centre of exhibitions and projects.

The medieval square tower, much renovated over the centuries, is the rest of the restored castle and dates back to the period when Orosei was the main center of its curatory. In the same enclosure stands the church of Sant'Antonio Abate, in volcanic stone, with a single nave with wooden roof and a cycle of frescoes of the fourteenth century; next, on 16 January, the fires of Saint Anthony light up.
The temple on the hills.
Romanesque church of the historic center.
A tour of Venetian country villas, seen from the outside.
Understand how to build with raw earth.
The palace and the Quirinale square, with collections of statues, paintings, tapestries, carriages, watches and porcelain.
The mother church of the village, rebuilt in the eighteenth century.
A historic garden with lemon trees in the heart of the village.

Small hilly municipality of Molise, on the Celano-Foggia tracturo, where you can visit the complex of Santa Maria di Casalpiano: Roman villa, medieval necropolis and Romanesque abbey linked to Montecassino since 1017.

At the foot of the cliff of the castle narrow alleys, noble palaces, stone portals and courtyards; in Piazza III Novembre the collegiate church of Santa Maria Assunta, with facade of the seventeenth century on older structures, and the fountain of Moses with the coat of arms of accounts. Palazzo Marchetti and Palazzo dei Panni recall the civil life between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries; at the foot of the castle the Rilke Promenade touches the places mentioned by Rainer Maria Rilke, who stayed in Arco.
The viewpoint on the village.
For the prehistory and archaeology of Cremasco.
Frescoes and a procession since 1479.
Villa designed in 1860 by Virginio Vespignani, in a park with rare trees and the "Sentiero dell'Amore" (Love Path).
One of the most spectacular rock villages in Italy, with five floors of caves.

Oval-shaped center, about 180 by 90 meters, enclosed by the walls, with the oldest parts dating back to the end of the thirteenth century. In April the patron saint of San Giorgio, in July and August the Middle Ages Festival and the fried fish festival all'ascolana.
A high-altitude trip to the Terminillo.
A mountain sanctuary at the edge of the forest.
Architecture of Gabetti and Island with views of the Alps.

Built at the end of the fourteenth century and renovated in the eighteenth century, with frescoes in the bell tower indicating an earlier building from the first half of the fourteenth century. It preserves painted wooden statues attributed to Clement Zamara (1478-1540), including the Complainant on the Dead Christ, a group of eight life-size figures.

Borgo on the ridge between the valleys of Cremone and Ete Morto, overlooking the Sibillini, known for the tradition of wicker weaving; it houses the altarpiece of Lorenzo Lotto della Madonna in glory with the saints (1548), the baroque staircase of San Gregorio Magno, the remains of the 14th-century fortress and the Apollo Theatre of 1844.

Church in white stone probably built in 1286, as a plaque says, transforming a chapel of 1201; two aisles of different width, perhaps one for the monks and one for the inhabitants, divided by massive octagonal columns, façade in hut with stone shelves. There are still vaulted monastic environments, part of the cloister and a tower.
The oldest church, survived the fire in 1223.

It rises on a sacred building of the IX-X centuries, with the portal of the masters Rodolfo and Binello of 1201 richly carved; the interior was rebuilt in neoclassical style between 1772 and 1819 by Giuseppe Piermarini. On the square, the ancient Roman forum.
the MiC card (updated to May 2020) reports      \ Closed } every day; please contact Tel. 0961 912102 before the visit
The monks' woods.
A medieval tower guarding the Lipuda.
Jazz in a mansion.
A piece of war under the hill.
The symbolic place of the city of memory.
Under the cathedral, four chapels built between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries; in the Chapel of the Resurrection a Pietà in marble by Giovanni Bandini (1597).
Guided tours organized by the Archaeological Group of the Municipality
The ancient navigation told on the site of an Etruscan port.
Moretto and Ferramola in the largest church in the diocese of Brescia.
Nicola Grassi and a baroque altar in the parish church.
Traditional games.

In the underground tunnels under the historic center ages for two years in oak barrels of Slavonia the bitter Braulio, recipe of 1875 of the pharmacist Francesco Peloni with local herbs such as gentian, juniper and absinthe; the visit to the infusion room and filtration, alcohol storage and cellars. Visits Wednesday and Saturday.
The statues and canvases from the Certosa.

Wild and romantic gorge traversed by stairs and bridges, sixth stage of the Path of Peace and touched by several rings from Caldaro and San Giuseppe al Lago, including that of about 1 hour and a half from the Vogelmeierhof.
The village of times.
The donkey-back bridge on the Nervia that Monet painted in four works.
The Senator family of the Insteii and other local stories.
Reservation required

Born between 1150 and 1170 as the hospice of the Knights Hospitallers for the pilgrims going to Rome (documented from 1171), it was fortified in a square manor with corner towers and courtyard with three orders of loggias, in the final fifteenth-century form of the architect Fioravante Fioravanti from Bologna. In 1502 there was held the Diet of Magione, the conspiracy against Cesare Borgia described by Machiavelli in the Prince, re-enacted every summer; Benedict XIV (1746) and Pius VII (1805). In the Romanesque chapel of St. John the Baptist two frescoes by painters of the workshop of Pinturicchio (Nativity; Madonna and Child among Saints John the Baptist and James). Still owned by the Order of Malta, at the center of a farm.
The cathedral has a Baroque appearance today; below is the Crypt of the Mummies with the confreres of Death, dating back to 1485.

Set up in a typical courthouse house in the historic centre, opened in 2003 and managed by the Cultural Circle ARCI Ghetonia, it exhibits domestic objects that tell traditional crafts, customs and rites; it has a library of about three thousand publications on the anthropological, linguistic and cultural origins of the area and on the links with Greece, an emerotheque and a collection of videos. Free admission; working hours 9.30-12.30 and 17-20 (May-September) or 16-19 (October-April).
The traces of a protohistoric fortified village.

Città del Tavoliere linked to wheat: the Piano delle Fosse preserves more than 600 grains excavated in the ground, next to the Museum of Wheat in the former Dominican convent; in the territory there are Torre Alemanna, the only fortified settlement of the Teutonic Knights remained in the Mediterranean, and the sanctuary of the Madonna of Ripalta on the Ofanto.
One of the most ancient Roman local markets, in a structure of the 1920s in Piazza Alessandria.

Heir to the Roman colony of Iulia Concordia, it preserves around the cathedral of Santo Stefano the Byzantine baptistery of 1089, the bell tower of 1150 and the archaeological areas with the early Christian remains of the Trichora Martyrum and the Basilica Apostolorum, as well as the Roman bridge, the thermal baths and the walls of the ancient city.
The city of the opera told with sounds and videos.
It is one of the most evocative buildings in the village and houses the Municipal Historical Archives and the Municipal Library.
The Romanesque on the hill above the city.
The most beautiful Romanesque in Europe, free.

Cited in 1057 and almost entirely rebuilt in the sixteenth century, example of a late-Gothic alpine church: monumental protire of 1536 by Matteo Rode of Melezet, façade with the procession of Vizi and Virtues, frescoes from the fourteenth to the sixteenth century, the ancon of the main altar of Jean Faure of Thures (1677) and, in the sacristy, the museum of vestments.

Permanent Museum was founded in 1989 on the initiative of the association "Ribera Verde" (Ribera Verde), which has collected over 4,000 finds of rural civilization, pastoral and handicraft of the territory; tools of ancient peasant art and agricultural machinery have been recovered, catalogued, restored and made accessible to the public.
The walking path that connects Riomaggiore to Manarola.

Small underground cell excavated in the "Pietra da Cantoni" (Pietra da Cantoni), the sandstone typical of the area, accessible from the cellar: like the other infernots, which exist only in Monferrato and were dug by the inhabitants between the late nineteenth and early twentieth century, it served to preserve the wine thanks to constant temperature and humidity, dark, absence of ventilation and silence. It is part of the UNESCO Award of 2014 and is located at the restaurant Fer.Mo.

It preserves the collection of Otello Sarzi (1922-2001), among the main innovators of the puppet theatre: about 3,500 objects used in about twenty shows, puppets of the Commedia dell'Arte, the masks of Emilia Sandrone and Fagiolino, about twenty barracks and theatres, archive and library.
Rapolla's sarcophagus.

New Florentine land of Valdarno founded as Castel Santa Maria and completed in 1337, with walls and fourteenth-century towers around Piazza della Repubblica; in the territory the Balze del Valdarno with Piantravigne, the sanctuaries of Pernina and Montemarciano, the frescoed oratory of Campo Arsiccio and the reserve of the Valley of Hell along the Arno.
The frescoed living room of Trento.
14 € (reduced 2 €, free under 18 years)
The castle with the high white stone tower and the crenellated walls, with an Italian garden and a courtyard inside.
The peasant civilization told in dialect.
Already in the fourteenth century, it conserves a wooden crucifix of the sixteenth century and paintings of the seventeenth century.
The life of a time in the castle cellars.
On the hill, noble palaces, monuments and churches survived the earthquake of the eighteenth century, which destroyed most of the country and redesigned its plant.

Walk in the historic center of the summit along the castle and its park. The bell tower was erected by Asti after 1257 as a symbol of an autonomous community and rebuilt in 1754 by the master wall Antonio Broglio, with dials of the clock of 1756 and 1780; behind the tower a panoramic balcony.
The cathedral that Sigismondo Malatesta had Leon Battista Alberti put on; inside Giotto's Crucifix and Piero della Francesca's fresco.

Country of the lower Val di Susa at the foot of the Sacred of San Michele, along the Via Francigena, known for the Neolithic site of Riparo Rumiano, the Museum Laboratorio della Preistoria and the sanctuary of San Pancrazio on the rocks above the village.
To be combined with the visit of the Fossil Forest.

Established in the 1930s (opened on June 9, 1934 with Ugo Procacci) in a seventeenth-century building, already home to the Confraternity of San Michele and San Vincenzo. Six rooms with liturgical vestments, sacred goldsmithery, paintings and wooden sculptures from the 14th to the 16th century: among the works the Annunciated Virgin of Matteo Civitali, a polyptych by Francesco di Andrea d'Anguilla, a altarpiece attributed to Vincenzo Frediani and a Flemish tapestry of the early 16th century. Open Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday afternoon with seasonal hours, on Sunday by reservation; free entry with free offer, guided tour €2 upon reservation.

Palazzo Ducale, residence of the Farnese family, who owned it until the extinction of the family in 1668; is part of the Latium Historical Houses Network and overlooks Piazza della Rocca, indicated among the things not to be missed.
The miniature valley.
The monastery of Saint Camilla Battista.
Walk and cycle in the green with a view of the Molise mountains.
The sacred art of the Dominican convent of Zagarise.

It takes its name from a small valley at the foot of Mount Delma; since 1991 the Pezzola family has cultivated its historic vineyards and produces Franciacorta Metodo Classico made from Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc grapes. The site is in a farmhouse of the fifteenth century also used for meetings, tastings and events, flanked by a structure for production and vinification since 2010. For visits and tastings contact the cellar (tel. 030 611404).
From Porta Brescia you enter the fortified city; from here a pedestrian path leads to the bastions Tognon and Feltrin, on the western front of the fortress.

Medieval plant with concentric circles around the castle, with stone alleys that lead to terraces on the valley: to the west the narrow houses and hung from the feudal period, to the south the noble palaces, to the east squares, fountains, convents and monumental buildings. Always accessible.
Under the Rotondo Mountain, the highest peak of the municipal territory, the gorge of the Acquasanta with the homonymous waterfall opens; in Bolognola the sources of the river Fiastrone are born.

Country of Sulcis whose ancient village, abandoned in the eighties for the infiltrations of the lake of Monte Pranu, houses the former Romanesque cathedral of Santa Maria di Monserrato (1213-1282), seat of the diocese of Sulci, with the Spanish House and the Museum of the territory; around, the park of Monte Pranu and dozens of nuragic sites.
The walls that still draw the center.
The Baroque church founded in 1619 by the Counts Ottonelli with the convent of the Scolopi and the Romanesque parish church of San Silvestro, founded in the 8th century.

Centro della Valle Caudina elevated to town by Carlo di Borbone with decree of 30 August 1745, near the sources of Fizzo that feed the Carolino Aqueduct: on top of the hill remain walls and gate of the castle founded in 1033 by Rainulfo, in the village the church of the SS. Annunziata di scuola vanvitellina, la chiesa alcantarina della SS. Concept and the Telephone Museum.

Considered of the IX century and renovated over the centuries, it has a cylindrical tower, a round walkway and an internal portico with ogival arches; a staircase leads to the Sala dei Baroni. Among the guests are St. Thomas Aquinas, Isabella Colonna and Giulia Gonzaga. Visitable by appointment.
In September the relic of the Sacred Cingolo is shown and venerated publicly by the pulpit, one of the central moments of the city festival.
The path of the monks to the panoramic tower.

Outside the walls the small lake of morainic origin, famous for its heart shape, reflects the village; all around the natural reserve extends. From the square of the church of San Giuseppe a short staircase descends to the lake.
From Neolithic to Roman times in the Sele valley.
Built in the fifth century, decagonal exterior and octagonal interior, with the mosaic of the twelve doves-apostles and a tomb with Longobard decorations of the eighth century.
The village of one of the most elegant castles in the Valle d'Aosta, the Renaissance residence of Giorgio di Challant with the fountain of pomegranate.
The marina between terraces and vineyards, with the Saracen Tower of 1596 and, at the Caletta del Saraceno, the remains of the Roman fish pond and the Villa dei Domizi Enobarbi.

Built in the Belle époque, it soon became the fashionable spa resort of the Central European aristocracy; destroyed in the First World War, it was rebuilt in Liberty style and inside it contains frescoes by Carlo Coppedè.

At the foot of the Asolani Hills, Maser is the village of the Villa Barbaro, designed by Andrea Palladio for the brothers Daniele and Marcantonio Barbaro and frescoed by Paolo Veronese, UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996 with the Palladian villas of Veneto; next stands the Palladian Temple of 1580, and among the hamlets of Coste, Crespignaga and Muliparte there are ancient churches, oratories and the hilly path of the two Fortress.
closure for work to secure the entrance of Villa Speranza, extended until 31 May 2026 (notice of the Municipality updated to 24/04/2026); reopening not confirmed
In a room of the Civic Museum on via Laurentina are exhibited memories of the singer-songwriter, buried in the cemetery of Ardea, including a letter from Mina and its 22 LP.

The church of the Annunziata, seventeenth-century with three aisles with stone columns; San Nicolò, in the heart of the village, with the façade restored on top of a large stone staircase; in the lower part of Sant'Antonio Abate, with three aisles, with Norman-style portal, bell towers, wooden statues and oil paintings.

Indicated as the most valuable artistic element of the country, it has a Greek cross plan; documented from the end of the sixteenth century, it was completely rebuilt shortly after the mid eighteenth century.
Stone symbols.

Birthplace of the poet Giuseppe Giusti (1809-1850): on the first floor antique furnishings set by Piedmont romance, on the second a large documentary section; in the library intact the best known portrait of the poet, by Giuseppe Bezzuoli; multimedia installations with readings of his verses.
Spreading of rocks born from a series of landslides during the last glaciation, which lie under the castle: an almost lunar landscape crossed by a dense network of paths.

Built on the Romanesque church of Santa Maria, visible in the crypt, with Renaissance façade, octagonal bell tower inspired by those seen by Pius II in Germany and five altarpieces of the Sienese school, including a Madonna of Matthew of John.
Climb suspended
Twenty-two churches and views of the Aeolians.
The Sibyl and the first Greek city.

It preserves the 61 manuscripts, almost all of the XIV-XV century, of the library that the saint instituted in the convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie, one of the most important collections of Franciscan books from the fifteenth century: classical texts, Fathers of the Church, right and grammar, four autographs with sermons and homilies and a letter to St. John of Capestrano; also exhibited two ancient maps of Monteprandone and a coin of 1652 by Carlo II Gonzaga-Nevers.
Public garden with rare plants and statues of Calabrian famous worldwide.
opening on request (Touring Club)
Founded in 1440, with mural paintings.

Founded probably in the fourth century on the remains of a Roman temple and rebuilt at the end of the thirteenth century and in the seventeenth century, it has no façade: the portal of 1512 opens onto a small porch. Inside the ciborium with cosmatesque newsstand of the thirteenth century, remains of fourteenth-century frescoes in the apse, the Madonna delle Grazie of the fourteenth century and a Romanesque crypt with re-use columns.
We're going to be tied to Celestino V.
An abbey built with stones of Roman Suasa.
The tower on the bastion.
The marbles of the Roman Terracina.
the Sirente-Velino Park has announced seasonal closures and reopenings of the gorges, with reservation obligatory at the reopening of 19 May; check before leaving

In the sixteenth century Palazzo Sassi de' Lavizzari, donated to the city in 1922, archaeological finds and works from the Middle Ages to today, the numismatic collection Sertoli and a precious wooden stüa.
Cinquecento wooden altars in high Valcellina.

On the Cervaro stream along the ancient Strada Regia delle Puglie, built in 1810 with a system patented by Ferdinando II of Bourbon: the last watermill still working in Puglia, today museum of ancient crafts and grinding of ancient grains such as Senator Cappelli.

Probably born with the settlement around the 11th century, it was destroyed with the bell tower by the earthquake of 1980 and rebuilt in local stone preserving the original external appearance, reopened to worship on 4 August 1991. Inside there are wooden statues of San Felice, Maria SS. of Constantinople, San Giuseppe, Sant'Antonio da Padova, San Vito, San Vincenzo and San Francesco di Paola.
In the woods on the trail of medieval silver miners.
The best preserved fort of the Tonale belt.
The patron saint in Gaginian marble school.
The starting point of each round of the center.
Where the Santa Rosa Sfogliatella was born.
About 1,100 species of roses from all over the world on the slopes of the Aventine with a view of the Palatine.
The symbol of Tricarico, visible from all over the valley.
Built at the behest of the Bishop of Turin Landolfo around 1037, it is considered one of the major buildings of the Piedmont Gothic; inside the Gallieri Chapel.
The oratories of the ancient confraternities.

The municipality of the agri have been built in the area of the ancient Atella, a city flourished from the fourth century BC under the influence of Capua: the National Archaeological Museum of the Atellan Agro tells the story, while the village of Teverolaccio preserves a sixteenth-century house and the eighteenth-century farmhouse.
The funeral complex of the La Scala family next to the church of Santa Maria Antica, one of the best examples of European Gothic art; in history is the place where Juliet pretended to die.

Set up by the Municipality in 1998 with the collection donated by Kurt Ryba, in honor of Peter Mitterhofer, who invented the typewriter in Parcines: over 2,000 objects (about 400 in the museum and 1,600 in a showroom) tell the story from the first wooden model of 1864 to the 1980s, with the cipher machine \"Enigma" of the Second World War.

Frazione di Olbia tra i golfi di Cugnana e di Marinella, born in 1964 on the initiative of the Venetians Luigi and Nicolò Donà dalle Rose, with architecture inspired in Venice: the main square is Piazza San Marco. Port tour with 800 berths, walk along the seafront, Piazza Rudalza and the beach i Sassi; at the end of August the Big Game of offshore fishing.
See a 16th century water hammer at work.
The castle that gives the name to the city, with views of the coast.
The underground basilica of Formia.
Contemporary art in the wool mill.

The large canal bridge of the Carolino Aqueduct, which Carlo di Borbone entrusted to Luigi Vanvitelli to feed the water games of the Reggia: he worked from 1753 for 17 years, with a cost of 622,424 ducats, for a pipe of about 38 km from the sources of Fizzo at the foot of the Taburno. Here the aqueduct emerges in a structure with three orders of arches 60 meters high and about 500 long, remembered by two epigraphs of 1759 at the level of the road. From the foot of the arches a road climbs along the Longano mountain between the ruins of the church of San Carlo and the mills built by Ferdinand IV in 1795. Free access every day; the upper walkway opens only during the initiatives of the Reggia.

Ample park with innovative features for its division into thematic areas and with attention to the protection of biodiversity; the Municipality presents it as a space for relaxation, the play of the little ones and the outdoor sports activity, as well as as as a meeting place and aggregation.

The centre of the Vallo di Lauro, dominated by the Lancellotti Castle, of Lombard-Norman origin and rebuilt at the end of the nineteenth century; the birthplace of Umberto Nobile, to which the museum in Palazzo Pignatelli is dedicated, with the remains of a Roman villa at the convent of San Giovanni del Palco.

Ruins inside the Aymerich Park: the main tower dates back to the 11th-XII century and in the 18th century became a prison; the castle has two floors and a valuable portico. During World War II the nearby caves served as a refuge.
Excursions between granite and cork.
A small theatre decorated by the author of the Phoenix.
The tower of the Quarda, simply called "Torretta" at the entrance of the port.
See basilica website (variety with functions)

In the complex of the medieval church with ancient cemetery, chapel of 1547 and Romanesque bell tower, the museum preserves pre-Romanesque and Romanesque finds and collections of local flora, fauna and minerals, with temporary exhibitions.
More than 180 works painted on the walls of the buildings of the Capitol district.

The municipality presents Brendola as the gate of the Berici at the foot of the Berici Hills. It is the birthplace of Saint Maria Bertilla Boscardin, whose peasant house is a destination of devotion, and the Town Hall of Villa Piovene hosts a permanent exhibition of archaeological finds.
The lagoon between two tomboli, historical oasis of the WWF in Tuscany, where you can see numerous species of birds, including flamingos.

The ruins of the cloister, a Gothic entrance gate dating from 1475 and a wooden altar dating back to 1694, remain among the Observing Friars Minor, who arrived at Naso in 1475, and there is also a Madonna attributed to Gagini.

The sunny plateau above Bolzano, a holiday destination for about 450 years and accessible without car by cable car and train: the earth pyramids, one of the highest in Europe, the Corno del Renon (2,260 m) with a 360° view of the Dolomites, the Commenda of the Teutonic Order in Longomoso and the museum of beekeeping at the Plattner farm.
Panorama on the Palentine Fields and medieval churches.
Art Nouveau villas and hotels, Coppedè and déco surrounded by parks with Mediterranean plants.
Hiking and canoeing on the mountain lake.
The mastium of over 30 meters.

Village of stone houses, narrow alleys and steps on a sandstone ridge. Since 2016 the CVTà Street Fest, directed by artist Alice Pasquini, has brought on the walls of the country works by artists such as Biancoshock, David de la Mano and Martin Whatson, today a call for visitors.

Small beaches with shallow and sandy seabeds around the Aragonese castle, suitable for children, from which the boats for excursions to the sea depart; italia.it mentions it among the Blue Flags of Calabria.

Area equipped near the lake, indicated by Italia.it as the largest adventure park in the region: acrobatic trails with walkways suspended among the trees, didactic woods, Trail Frassati and a village on the trees.
The Ghibelline village of Brunforte.
The balcony of Montale on the plain.
Open to the public in general only during shows or events
On Viale Roma, it has a portal with bas-relief depicting a choir of angels; next to it stands the former convent of the Capuchins (1705), today the Museum of Cork.
difficult access: visits only possible for expert speleologists, others enter only for a few meters

The parish church (already abbey) of the 12th century, rebuilt in Gothic style after an earthquake and restored several times. In a chapel it houses the wooden statue of the Black Madonna of the Crowned, coming from the church of Castel Mancino, today destroyed.
A 16th-century square watchtower, about 20 meters high, part of the coastal defensive system designed by Camillo Camilliani and Tiburzio Spanocchi; restored in 1995 by the Superintendence of Trapani.
Old Dorga's puppet altars.
1954 dam that closes the valley, today lowered and inserted in the landscape; the outside you visit freely, the interior by reservation; easy path of 5 km along the lake.
A Baptism of the Malosso in the church of the ancient hospital.
Open only on educational occasions or events, by reservation, waiting for the end of the work
A large wooded spot in the Upper Milanese, to walk on the Way of Saint Augustine.
Walk over the lake between villages and olive trees, returning by train.
The largest engraved rock in the Alps.
The 19th-century theatre with a rich stage room; the first town theatre was in the Town Hall and in 1585 hosted a work by Bernardino Pino.

A centre of Longobard origin at about 271 meters, with many churches and chapels, including the Church Mother of the Holy Spirit, the main place of worship. In the lower part, towards the river, the murals tell the rural life (the pressing of the grapes, the harvest brought with the donkeys, the ginning of the beans); in the upper part suspended umbrellas and colored staircases.
The Baroque downtown.
The dunes of Italian cinema.

Historical stop of the Via Francigena, the ancient Borgo San Donnino is dominated by the Romanesque Cathedral with the facade of the workshop of Benedetto Antelami, between medieval gate, Gothic town hall and the Magnani theatre.

One of the largest squares in Europe, 88,620 square meters, reclaimed in 1775-76 by Andrea Memmo: the elliptical canal with 78 statues of characters linked to Padua and the University and the island Memmia in the center.
A family water walk a stone's throw from the village.

A quadrangular villa built in 1736 by Francesco Bonanno, prince of Cattolica, with the It houses the Renato Guttuso Museum, officially established in 1990, with works by the Bagherese painter and other artists; in the garden Guttuso's tomb, the work of Giacomo Manzù. Open every day except Monday (winter 9-13.30 and 14.30-19, summer 9.30-14 and 15-19).

Medieval village of Cilento, the village of the hotel is born from a settlement of Basilian monks, with the Ethnographic Museum and the WWF Oasis of the Grotte del Bussento, where the river re-emerges from the rock.

On Wednesday morning the market is held, with a part dedicated to food: cheese, ricotta, meats and sausages, organic seasonal products, sweets and ice cream; among the specialties beans, apricots, black cherry for ice cream, porcini in autumn and almonds in summer.
€13, under 12 €8, 0-4 years free

Collection of works inspired by the Divine Comedy, born from donations and legacies followed by the exhibitions of the Iconographic Museum Dantesco; among the authors present Sassu, Sughi, Cremonini, Kokocinski, Trubbiani, Tabuso, Tommasi Ferroni, Purificato, Mulas and Crocetti.
€10 (one ticket with the Museum of the city and the territory)
The main square of the village, overlooking historical buildings and the Matrice Church; in the center stands a sculpture of St. George killing the dragon. Without architectural barriers.

Outside the walls on the Cacultian hill, elevated to cathedrals as the second seat of Sabina after the Saracen destruction of Foronovo. In the material façade of Roman tombs, two Lusoriae tabulae and a Roman bas-relief with a seated emperor; inside the chapels of San Sisinio (1656) and San Saturnino (rebuilt in 1782) and at the main altar the Martyrdom of San Lorenzo di Vincenzo Manenti.

Monumental arch at the entrance of the village erected by the inhabitants in 1724 in memory of the flood of the Po of 1705, which devastated the fields, collapsed farms and houses and moved the river bed; the epigraph recalls the event and the construction of the church of the Blessed Virgin of the Fountain to protect the country. In the same year it was connected to the sanctuary by a tree-lined avenue, the alley, today Viale Italia. The monument has been the subject of a conservative restoration.
Sea, cliffs and memories of Cassiodoro.
At 2,086 meters, along the long-distance European path E5, it offers a 360 degree view of the surrounding mountains, from the Dolomites to the Ortles and the Tessa group.

Wanted by Agostino Chigi, the noble Sienese who at the end of the fifteenth century had rented the alum quarries; next, in the sixteenth-century convent of the Augustinian Fathers, the Cultural Pole with Civic Museum, municipal library and historical archive is located.
Sea and mining archaeology in a secluded corner.

Made by Count Ruggero after the victory over the Saracens, it is indicated as the first monastery built by the Normans in Sicily: a Benedictine-Cluniac church surrounded by walls, where the monk Silvestro lived. Abandoned after the first half of the eighteenth century, today it is a ruin on a hill about 3 km from the center.
The painting of the Belle Époque of the Ferrara Boldini.

The square-shaped crenellated tower on the main square is the symbol of the village, erected by the Astalli, Troili and Caetani families; the Caetani held the fief from 1297 to 1670 and remains of the ancient castle. To the village you enter the Door of the Sun and the Neapolitan Door.
Lanino and Tanzio in the heart of the village.
Under the Basilica of San Severo outside the walls, the early Christian catacombs that with those of San Gaudioso and San Gennaro make Health the underground neighborhood of Naples.
The painted rooms of the Dukes Caracciolo.

Ash of about 250 years, 23 m tall and with 480 cm of circumference, declared monumental tree, at the hamlet Rounzèi at about 1250 m; can be reached in 40-45 minutes from Fournais or, more easily, from the Park Montano in the beech wood.
Museum of the wolf established by the Municipality and the Ente Parco dell'Antola on the ground floor of the former rectory: an interactive path on the wolf and its relationship with man today.
Founded in 425 by Pietro d'Illiria on the Titulus Sabinae, on the Aventine.
Golden altar and view of the Sangro valley to the sea.
Re-exposed in 2013, he exhibits seventy puppets, one hundred scripts, costumes and sets by the genoese puppetist Angelo Cenderelli, with a theater for performances during guided tours.
Wild nature a stone's throw from Rome.
A Sunday between antiques and monuments of the center.
The "ideal city" of the Renaissance wanted by Pope Pius II in his native village, Corsignano: UNESCO historical center since 1996, in the UNESCO landscape of Val d'Orcia.

A wide porticoed road like a square, very colorful: there are the town hall with the bust of Garibaldi di Vela and the house rebuilt in 1755 where the Correggio was born and died; at the end the monument to the fallen of Bistolfi.
Roman tombs by the lake.
The Po flows slowly next to the village, among gorges, banks and rows of poplars; from the historic center start trails along the river for walkers and cyclists.
Two centuries of collections in the heart of the old city.

Under the cathedral churchyard, more than 900 m2 of remains from the Roman period (II-IV century A.D.) to the Middle Ages (XI-XII century), excavated from 1970 and opened to the public in 1995: shops along a paved road and a large building seat of professional associations (dendrophors, blacksmiths, centonary), documented by two bases, then a building of the VIII-IX century perhaps linked to the ancient bishop's complex and a circular baptistery of the XI-XII century with apse of horseshoe. Opened on 18 July 2025 with guided tours by the association Il Fondaco per Feltre; disabled access not guaranteed.
Terni's 20th-century living room.
The last spontaneous pinewood of Aleppo.
The passage between the two squares.
The tower that tells the fief of rice.

110 steps decorated with mosaics on the theme of peace, made by the French master Bruno Amman on sketches of international artists and completed in 1987 respecting the structure of 1925; the pavement depicts childhood games such as rope and ball and in the square a sculpture in the rock of Peppino Quinto shows children playing under the gaze of a mother who is nursing.

Easy walk, especially on paths and forest roads in the woods above the village, which shows the numerous open-air porphyry quarries and the sign of man on the landscape; a family variant starts from the Museo Casa Porfido and crosses the upper part of the village between porphyry, chestnuts and deer of the wildlife park.

Used from the 8th to the 3rd century B.C., with the maximum expansion between the 6th and 5th centuries: tombs \"a die" lined up in blocks along orthogonal roads, each of a family, whose name is engraved on the architrave.
Museum in Via Santa Caterina.

The area of ponds fed by the waterfalls, in the woods, with a monumental forest, a Byzantine-Romanesque church and the "is cumbessias," accommodation for pilgrims. At the end of May the feast of the saint with procession, launeddas, folk groups, festival and poetic competition; leads there the  "strada del rito" with works of Maria Lai.
The historic parish church of the plateau.
Sub-Saharan Africa to touch with your hand.
The battle of 1944 told by the memorabilia.
Frescoes from the school of Gentile da Fabriano.

Archpriest's church already existing before 1112, rebuilt in the fifteenth century in Romanesque-Gothic style and brought from three to four naves in 1610, divided by cylindrical and polygonal pillars; seventeenth-century bell tower by Giuseppe Alberti and atrium with coffered ceiling and frescoes by Antonio Longo. After the 2003 fire, the restoration brought back hidden paintings. Guided tours throughout the year with the Magnificent Community.
Frescoes from the Giotto school.
The medieval Jewish quarter.
The devotion of the Death of Hawk.
The most beautiful mosaics in Rome.

High fortress of medieval plant, probably of the second half of the eighth century, several times renovated: today it is mainly a late Renaissance building; of the two towers remembered by the sources there is no trace and of the walls survives a stretch in via Sottocastello. On a portal is visible the coat of arms with the lion rampant of the Della Leonessa; Giambattista Basile, governor of Montemarano in 1615-1616, completed the first draft of Lo Cunto de li Cunti. Restored in 2015, it hosts exhibitions, including the MuVIM, Ecomuseum of Wine.
Three medieval churches in a small village.

White limestone eyelashes overlooking the sea covered with Mediterranean maquis, shelter of reptiles and nesting birds; the Rilke Path, about 2 km panoramic on the Adriatic, connects Duino to Sistiana.
Higher than the village, wide meadows and woods reachable also by mountain bike, suitable for relaxation in nature.

The Ambro river forms about 2 km of jumps, narrow streets, high tunnels and heights up to 55 meters, with a very variable flow rate depending on the season; in the lower part stands the sanctuary of the Madonna dell'Ambro. The route, about 14 km, is recommended for experienced hikers.

Born as a defensive fortress around the 11th century on an alluvial terrace overlooking the plain, it is now home to the Town Hall. The front of the entrance, of an effortless age, preserves the porta carraia and the housings of the drawbridge; in the fifteenth-century wing there is a wooden Madonna of the fifteenth century and the frescoes of the school of Dodecanese of the brothers Franceschino and Manfredino Boxilio (Madonna with Child, Saint Lucia, Saint Biagio, Saint Francis), torn from the church of San Sebastiano, today Our Lady of the Ghiare. Guided tours on request in Italian, English, German and French.
A hill of amphorae.
The most famous Franciscan convent in Irpinia.
In the woods of the Zermula, an ancient spruce of about 180 years with the horizontal trunk supporting six vertical trees.

On the western coast of the Gulf of Taranto, long and wide expanses of fine clear sand bordered by Mediterranean maquis and a pine forest of Aleppo pine trees, with free stretches alternated with equipped beaches; turquoise and clear sea and sandy backdrop in slight slope, suitable for families. The resort has got the Blue Flag.
The monumental nativity scene in the sacristy.

Founded perhaps by Giacomo Caldora at the beginning of the fifteenth century, passed to Guevara in 1496 and to d'Avalos in 1573, recovered since 1970: it houses the art gallery (Michetti, Palizzi), the archaeological collection on the Frentani and Histonium and a Neapolitan garden of eighteenth-century plant with terrace on the sea.

Church of San Giovanni, completed in 1884 in neo-Romanesque style on a project by William of the Cell to commemorate a Marian apparition of 1496; facade with white and black stone bands, frescoes by Luciano Ricchetti, sculptures by Paolo Perotti (1970) and Giorgio Groppi (1987) and a wrought iron gate by the craftsman Leonardi of Grazzano. From the end of August to the end of September, the statue of Our Lady descends from the throne to the presbytery, and then goes back to the rite of the "risalita" .
The convent of Michelozzo for Cosimo de' Medici with the largest collection in the world of Blessed Angelico: the Annunciation at the top of the staircase and the frescoed cells of the friars.
He keeps the crib of Federico Brandani.
A medieval village between doors and towers.

On the first floor of the old primary schools, he reconstructs the war on the Russian front with panels, documents, photographs and testimonies of the veterans, with photographic documentation on the Battalion Ceva. Visits by reservation (Tel. +39 0174 391101).

Ancient fortified village on a hill, mentioned as Suberatum in a text dated 1096, with walls and two towers, the main church, the church of Santa Caterina d'Alessandria and a hermitica laura; destroyed by the earthquake of 1783, remains the ruins of tower-houses, the Baronial Palace and the ancient parish.
A romantic garden.
Sea and monuments together.
A thousand years of Pavese art in the castle.
The divisionist painter of the valley.

A small funerary sacellus, perhaps annexed to the primitive early Christian basilica, with square plan with bare columns that hold four arches; in the apse a marble pool, perhaps a Capuan fountain of imperial age, is an altar and traditionally welcomes the remains of the saint. The mosaics, dated between the beginning of the fifth and sixth centuries, cover the vault with branches of vine, birds and a golden crater on a blue background and the lunettes with the blessing Christ, the divine throne with the roll of the seven seals and the symbols of the Evangelists.

Country of the Serre Salentine between olive groves and farmhouses, about 10 km from the sea of Ugento, known for its artisan ceramics. The historic centre, with noble houses and courtyard houses, revolves around Piazza del Popolo with the Brancaccio Palace and the Matrice Church; in the hamlet Torrepaduli the Sanctuary of San Rocco and the night of the pinch between 15 and 16 August.
Palazzo del Cinquecento in the ancient village; on the noble floor it preserves Risorgimento relics belonging to Giuseppe Garibaldi.

In the former stables of the Franciscan monastery a path that follows the stages of the Passion with the statues in mache, about one and a half meters tall, that the local artist Antonio Russo (1836-1914) donated to the community in 1875; multimedia rooms explain the technique of mache.
Family walk with views of the Langa Astigiana.

Ring path of 5 km (about 2 hours) from Piazza Garibaldi through Loveno, Piamuro, Tobi, Cardano and Burgatto, in the gorge where the Sanagra flows between high walls: excavated sections in the rock and suspended bridges, not recommended for those suffering from vertigo.

Benedictine Abbey of Santa Maria founded in 1059, today dedicated to San Biagio, at the foot of the Sassotetto; it remains the single nave church with trusses and crypt, frescoed by the Master of Piobbico, Paolo Bontulli and Nobile da Lucca.

The first fauna centre of the Italian Alps entirely dedicated to the wolf, inaugurated in 2010: the center visit to Piazza Giustizia e Libertà and the fauna area in Casermette, home of the Maritime Alps Park.

Ancient mill transformed into a workshop where until the eighties the blacksmith Francesco Cortiana forged cutting tools for fields and woods with the water of the river Ala; today his nephew Mario tells the work of iron. It is reached by a short walk in the Ronchi Valley.
Private collection of sculptures, epigraphs and prehistoric weapons, recorded by MiC as an archaeological area.
A baroque box.

An ancient paved road of Roman republican era, 2,65 meters wide, that through the woods rises to about 1,000 meters to the place of the Temple of Lazial Jupiter on Monte Cavo, with panoramic views of the lakes of Albano and Nemi; on the summit stands a building built in 1783 by the Cardinal of York. At the Camps of Hannibal, where according to tradition Hannibal camped in the Second Punic War, it is possible to see the basolate.
The Sardinian art of the twentieth century.

Museum of rural art in a 17th century stone house in the oldest part of the country, dedicated to the three single sisters that the inhabitants called \"feman da la piza" . On the ground floor tools for agriculture, milk processing, chestnut harvesting and fishing, a large fireplace with branches and a nineteenth-century bedroom; on the upper floor tools for textile fibres and footwear, the model of a mill, a working frame and ancient school benches. Open in July Friday-Sunday and August every day (16.30-18.30), in the rest of the year by reservation.
Homage to the Championship on the ascent of Pordoi.
The mountain work to try with your hands.
Sacred art of the twentieth century.

In the castle, he exhibits the masterpieces of the ancient church of San Clemente, with ample space to the works of Antonio da Fabriano, the dossal of the Madonna of Mercy by Pietro Paolo Agabiti and the original of the Canovian statue of the Valadier Temple; he also tells Hannibal of the Genga, Pope Leo XII since 1823. Open Mon, Wed, Fri 9-12; Mar and Thu 16-18.
A Roman bridge of Flaminia.
The "small Versailles" built since 1723 for Francesco III d'Este and Carlotta d'Orléans; the south wing, the ruined chapel, the perimeter of the park and the oval pool remain.

Established in 1982 and re-arranged and expanded in 2010 on four floors, it is a geological-paleontological, archaeological and historical museum. The best known piece is the burial complete with a mesolithic hunter lived about 7,500 years ago, found in 1987 in Mondeval de Sora at about 2,150 m; next, the cast of the Pelmetto mass with dinosaur prints, a paleoveneta stele of Monte Pore, copies of the rock inscriptions of the Civetta and sections on the Neolithic site of Mandriz, on the Gothic alpine and on the mines of Fursil. It is part of the UNESCO Dolomites museum network; book-shops, cafés, libraries and educational workshops.
The antiques market on the third Sunday of each month.

Fortified village of the 14th century used as a storage of crops and shelter for people and animals during the raids: almost square plant of about 70 m of side (4,900 m2), eight blocks and 62 cells, today largely houses, with broad roads for the intersection of two wagons and no square. The only entrance is defended by a medieval tower-gate in river pebbles, open towards the inside and on four floors, then civic and bell tower (the bells passed to the new bell tower in 1928, the clock remained until 1942). In a cell survives the apse of the chapel of Sant'Evasio (later Santo Spirito), rural of the XI-XII century and documented since 1329, with frescoes of the first fifteenth century with intense colors.

Small museum next to the Matrice Church: in the underground environments, it exhibits the most significant finds of local ceramics dating from the 13th to the 18th century, recovered in the excavations of 1996 under the sacristy, among the remains of medieval houses. Tel. +39 329 437 8774.
Winter in the middle of summer, half an hour from the vineyards.
One of the great sanctuaries of the Catholic world.

Fully pedestrian walk of about 3 km along the gulf, born from the reconstruction after the earthquake of 1901 that destroyed the houses overlooking the lake and inaugurated in 1906; it connects the historical center, the square of the Town Hall and the pedestrian walkway, with views of the gulf in every season.
A patrician residence and a masterpiece by Carlo Scarpa.
The lake view.

The museum center Museums of Agricultural Sciences, established in 2011 in the Reggia, brings together the Botanical Garden, founded in 1872 and among the oldest in Italy, the Herculanense Museum, reopened in a multimedia way in 2009, and other scientific museums.
The Jewish Trieste.

Separates the village from the sea and offers views of the Gulf of Orosei, Mount Albo and the Cedrino; on the top a 12 meters bronze statue of Christ, reproduction of the wooden one, destination of pilgrimages. Walls equipped for climbing, hiking and mountain biking trails, 32 varieties of wild orchids and caves with fossil fauna.
Rebuilt in neo-Gothic style, with brick façade and stone columns of Quinzano; the bell tower, adapted in Gothic style in the 14th century, is the only remaining element of the ancient church.

Fraction and place of pilgrimage where Josef Freinademetz, missionary of the Society of the Divine Word died of typhus in China in 1908, beatified in 1975 and canonized in 2003, the first South Tyrolean saint. The winery of the farm was transformed into a chapel, decorated by the artists Kollreider of Lienz and Lois Irsara of Badia. Open every day at 8-20.
Urban art in the plain.
The hills of Barbera.
Clay, furnaces and a quarry back nature.
According to the tradition founded by San Francesco in 1215 in a secular wood, it preserves frescoes of the Giotto school; it studied Felice Peretti.

Narrow streets of white houses with small courtyards, external stairs, pergolas and arches; the district of sa Maddalena is the best preserved part. Along the course Grazia Deledda the prison well and the remains of the seventeenth-century residence of the Major; murals and cobbled streets.
The Underground Foggia.
A day in the forests of the Serre.
The collection of Saverian Missionaries started in the late nineteenth century by Bishop Guido Maria Conforti: bronzes, ceramics, coins and objects of daily life from China and mission countries.
The arcade living room of the walled city.

A half-moon of white and very fine sand about 150 meters next to Simius, protected by the mistral by two promontors and in front of the island of Serpentara, with cliffs for snorkeling; not far from the Roman necropolis of Accu is Traias (1st century BC-III century AD), about thirty burials in the pit, urns and amphorae.
The fort anti-pirates overlooking the port.
The fortress on the acropolis.
The church was born inside the walls.

At the highest point of the village, at 1,200 meters, on the site of a Longobard castle then enlarged by the Normans, with forms of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries; there you go up for the most important religious festival, on the third Sunday of September.
Palazzo del Cinquecento with internal courtyard, seat of Palazzo Lusi Archaeological Greek Exhibition (PLEAG).
Where the Fiat was born.
The view from the last step.
The museum of world cultures in the former Ansaldo industrial area of Via Tortona, among ethnographic collections, design and large exhibitions.
The peasant work of the past, with free entry.
The sea of the city.
The pope's hermitage on the Morrone.
Overlooking the square, in Gothic Ligurian with an octagonal tower of 40 meters and a Romanesque plan with three naves; it houses a wooden crucifix of Maragliano.

Ancient gold mine recovered and equipped for visits with the Interreg Italia-Switzerland Mineralp project, opened to the public since 2023 with guided tours managed by Geoexplora, to enter the mountain to discover ancient places and crafts. Dates and times on the mine site.
visits only by reservation (Comune di Ossimo, tel. 0364 41100)
Stone houses and churches on the border ridge.

Section of the diocesan museum opened in 2016 in the ancient chapel of Sant'Eligio: 1700 years of Teggiano's stone, with Roman funerary newsstands, medieval capitals, coat of arms, the arch of the Malavolta chapel and an Aragonese plate linked to the Conspira dei Baroni; the visit continues in the frescoed succorpe of Santa Venera. Closed on Monday.

Started in 1228, two years after the death of the saint, and consecrated in 1253: in the lower church Romanesque arches and frescoes of Cimabue, Giotto and school, Pietro Lorenzetti and Simone Martini (Chapel of St. Martin); in the upper Gothic church the facade in white stone with the rosette and scenes of the Apocalypse of Cimabue.
A vast seventeenth-century building remained unfinished, already castalderia estense, near the hamlet of Rovereto sulla Secchia.

Built between 1754 and 1768 on a project by the Barletano Giovanni Mancarelli, originally dedicated to Saint Anthony Abbot; the octagonal bell tower of 1588 has a dome covered with colored majolica. The Baroque interior with three naves has polychrome stuccoes, marble altars by Luigi Cimafonte, the ...Madonna del Cardellino of Giaquinto, choir in walnut and sacristy furnishings by Liberato Villani; in front of the church a seat of the sixteenth century.
Frescoes recently rediscovered.
€11 whole; €2 from 18 to 25 years; free up to 17 years; with Rocca and Verucchio Museum €14,50

Municipality of the Verona hinterland of Garda, about twenty kilometers from Verona; the Civic Archaeological Museum in the town hall exhibits prehistoric and Roman finds, while on Monte San Michele there is the Archeoparco of Bastia, with a medieval fortified settlement and some of the best views of the lake.
In 2025 began the restoration of the rooms of the noble floor; schedules and tickets on the site of the palace
the villa is closed to the public and opens only at events
The tower of Quasimodo's poetry on his brother Enzo.
Giant bench in panoramic position among the vineyards of Vignale.
In the former Town Hall, it tells how a village of fishermen and peasants has become a popular tourist destination throughout Europe.
The old water sawmill in the valley.

On a granite hill above the valley of Capichera, used from the 14th to the 8th century BC: mast with two side towers joined by a curved bastion, entrance architraves of about 3 meters and 7 tons, tholos room almost 7 meters high and a well in the courtyard about 7 meters deep. Around a village of almost one hundred huts on about 5 hectares, with a meeting hut; traces of wine were found in the jugs. Open every day 9-19.
Sea under the white cliff.

Borgo-museo dell'Ogliastra about 800 meters, at the foot of the limestone Tacchi, the birthplace of Maria Lai: her works at the Stazione dell'Arte and at the Washer, the cave of Su Marmuri, the waterfalls of Lequarci and Lecorci and the lakes of Santa Barbara.
Gardens near Porta Marina with the fountain in the center        • The woods of music by Tonino Guerra.

The Mallorchino is a sheep cheese aged over eight months, in 10-12 kg shapes, protagonist of the Majorchino Tournament, practiced since the seventeenth century: at Carnival 16 teams from three players roll the forms for about two kilometers. The hazelnuts, celebrated with a festival in October, come into sweets such as risu niru and cassatelli and in the hazelnut sausage; to try also baked ricotta, ravioli and the ncasciata of Ferragosto.
The village of the poetess overlooking the lake.
In the larger and airier district of Ceneda, the cathedral overlooks the square of the Museo della Battaglia.

Started in the fifteenth century and modified in the following century, it has an octagonal Romanesque bell tower with terracotta tiles; it retains a canvas attributed to Francesco Vecellio and the ceiling is by Beppi Spolaor (1947).
The panorama from the top of the city.
The most photographed cove in Puglia.

The park around the prehistoric cave used as a place of burial and worship since the Paleolithic, where the Woman of Ostuni was found; it dominates centuries-old olive groves and the Adriatic sea. In summer it is open with guided tours; paths only partially accessible.

A 17th century building in the historic centre, presented by the Ecomuseum as a home to a bourgeois family of the 19th century; it is one of the museum's locations along with the Ethnographic Museum, Sa Bovida and the Mura Museum.
On foot to the Mentorella in the footsteps of Wojtyla.
The river that disappears under the mountain.

Inaugurated in 2020 in the Galleria Borghese, in seven sections exhibits finds of Nomentum and Ager nomentanus: reliefs and Roman marble sarcophagi (1st century BC-II century A.D.) and materials of the sacred area of Casale Santucci, including an altar with a procession of bulls destined for sacrifice; the last section is a map of ancient marbles re-used in the alleys of the village.

At the highest point of the village the tower dating back to the ninth century, defensive and then part of a castle, with stretches of the ancient city walls around; in the center also the Zurlo palace, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1805 by Count Giuseppe Zurlo and his brother Biase.
The little chimney sweeps.

The central square, with the nineteenth-century statue of Tiziano, is surrounded by period buildings: the Palazzo della Magnifica Comunità and the Casa di Tiziano the speaker, today home of the Tiziano and Cadore Foundation.
Terraces with flowerbeds, trees and fountains overlooking the Strait of Messina, Calabria and the Bay of Taormina.

Built between the 13th and 14th centuries in the Visconti period, it preserves fifteenth-century frescoes of the Passion of Christ in the international Gothic style and the 17th-century canvas "La Gloria di San Carlo" by the Lambugnani brothers, which shows the Vimercate of the time.
The heart of the village and its viewpoint.

In the sixteenth-century noble palace renovated in the seventeenth-century, which housed the family of Giacomo Leopardi: archaeological collection with mosaics and Roman statues from Montefrancolo, picture gallery of Pollento painters, ceramics produced in Pollenza between 1810 and 1905, antique furniture, a collection of crucifixes and the Vespa Museum curated by Marco Romiti. In the same building library and historical municipal archive.
The crenellated tower overlooking the Treste valley.

The largest building in the historic center, built by the Orsini in the fifteenth century and today seat of the Municipality: the most visible sign of rivalry with the Colonna. Façade with crossed windows in travertine and loggia originally four arches, three of which preserved; on the noble floor, today council room, a large fireplace and two doors surmounted by the coat of arms Orsini in marble.
Climb into Bressanone's symbolic tower.
The museum designed for children, in the Santa Maria della Scala complex according to Visit Tuscany, with accessible routes.
Inaugurated on 22 May 1887 on the 83-metre-long 400-metre-long canal that connects the Small Sea and the Great Sea, it connects the Old Town to the Borgo.

Farmland fed by dozens of sources, including those of Biferno, the longest of the rivers entirely Molise; behind you rise Monte Gallinola (1.923 m) and Monte Miletto (2.050 m), the highest peak of Matese, with the slopes of Campitello Matese reachable from Bojano.

Borgata about 9 km from Cabras, with the cumbessias of the late seventeenth century for pilgrims around the 17th century church, set of spaghetti western between 1967 and 1990. Under the church an hypogeum frequented by the Neolithic, nuragic water worship, then Punic and Roman and early Christian sanctuary from the fourth century, with inscriptions in Punic, Greek, Latin and Arabic. On the first Saturday of September, the Race of the Scalzi arrives at dawn.
The Ladin culture of Val di Fassa.
Openings only for guided tours on some Sundays and for groups by reservation; the MiC card (2021) indicated the museums closed until the date to be allocated: check with the secretariat (0371 211140)
The Solimenas on the hill of the park.

It documents the crafts of the past, in particular those of the slippery and barber; the section of the ancient bicycle trades, with a private collection of vintage bicycles equipped for the craftsmanship, also makes known the arts of the masquerade and the watchmaker.
Understand the 1976 earthquake.

Also known as Santa Maria Assunta or della Fonte, already active in the sixteenth century next to the fountain of the square, with late Baroque façade and tombstones to the fallen of the two wars; inside the permanent exhibition Â The beautiful... of the reconstruction Â, with works recovered from the churches damaged by the earthquake.
The double-cap dome built without centimeters between 1420 and 1436: you climb between the two caps, next to the Last Judgment of Vasari and Zuccari, up to the lantern.

The Fratelli De Gasperi hut, over 1,700 meters on the Clap Grande, is reached with a path marked by the Centre Pian di Casa and is base for climbs in the Dolomites Pesarine; next, the botanical garden with about 200 species of mountain plants, between orchids and lilies.

Norman manor of the 11th century, passed to the Siginulfo in the 13th century; quadrangular plant with four angular cylindrical towers of the Aragonese era, one of which destroyed by the earthquake of 1456. In the 16th century the Loffredos transformed it into a noble residence; since 1825 it has been the Susannas, the Marquises of Sant'Eligio, who made it a country residence.
From the 13th century, today it is ruined, with the remains of the cylindrical tower and part of the walls.
The cemetery of the Roman artists.

The fifteenth-century, in the castle square, uses as an apse a medieval cylindrical tower. It preserves the table of the Virgin with Child of Barnabas of Modena (active 1361-1383), already in the sanctuary of the Rocchette, an apse fresco of the Baptism of Jesus of 1608 attributed to the school of Giambattista Paggi with the feudal Agostino and Cecilia Spinola, sixteenth-century paintings and a crucifix and a wooden Madonna of the workshop of Anton Maria Maragliano. Restored in 2008.

In the ancient sawmill where the beech of the valley was worked, today the Park's visit centre: it tells the history of the Val Fondillo and the work of woodcutters and mule trackers, with information on trails and services; it hosts cultural events and workshops for children.

Managed by the section of Genoa of the National Alpine Association, documents the history of the Alpine troops and the association from the foundation to today with photographs, documents, uniforms, badges and relics, with attention to the Alpine traditions of the Ligurian valleys. It has a library, two exhibitions (on the War of Liberation and on the history of the Alpine troops) and two audiovisuals, distributed between the Tricolor Hall, the Hall of Fighters, the Hall of Father Basil, the Hall of Delfo Pieramati and the Hall of Cuneense Division; guided tours available. The MiC card (updated to 2020) does not show usable times: contact the museum (tel. 010 936930, museumeglialpini@libero.it).
A Roman sundial that has been marking the time for two thousand years.
The peasant craftsmanship before the earthquake.
Volcanic stone and sculpted architraves.
The church for which Lorenzo Lotto painted Our Lady of the Rosary.
A table of Bartolomeo di Gentile in a walled village.
Waterfalls and paper mills abandoned in the green.

Dedicated in the sixteenth century and rebuilt in the first half of the eighteenth century, it now has an eighteenth-century appearance; above the main altar there is a pipe organ of 1785 and a polychrome marble panel dedicated to the patron.

Medieval center of alleys, stairs, churches and nineteenth-century palaces, with sections of the walls of the fourteenth century; going up from the seafront towards Via Mustazzo you will meet Villa Pisani.
Caciocavallo made and tasted on the spot.
Punches, plates and books by Giambattista Bodoni, the court printer who invented one of the most used characters in the world.
€27 in low season, €32 in high season; €38-42 with the Enzo Ferrari Museum
The Romanesque church inside the walls of Vigoleno, a village also known for the Vin Santo aged six to seven years.

Medieval stone village, founded in the first half of the 15th century, on the Ionian side between Monte San Michele and Monte Pizzuto, on the watershed between the valleys of Neto and Lipuda. Small houses gathered around small squares, the churches of San Nicola and San Domenico and, on the mountain above the village, the sanctuary of San Michele Arcangelo; the apotropaic stone masks on portals and windows recall the Albanian origins, linked to fifteenth-century migrations from southern Albania and Morea.
A quiet stop in the woods of Val di Sole.
The border towers on the Lima valley.
The oldest Montefiascone.

Centre of the Vibrata Valley with the Benedictine church of San Martino, one of the oldest in Abruzzo, and the mother church with frescoes of the miracle of the Madonna della Consolazione, which according to tradition saved the country from French sack in 1798.
The Gothic Cistercian in Lazio.

The largest historical garden in the province, over 13 hectares designed by the German landscaper Georg Ziehl and inaugurated in the early twentieth century as a thermal garden: avenues tree-lined with redwoods, cedars, beech trees, magnolias and species from various parts of the world, the Grand Hotel Imperiale and the liberty Villa Paradiso, already home to the spa society. Open every day; it hosts Ortinparco and the Christmas market.

Fortification of the Alpine Valley extended for about a square kilometer to about 2050 meters, with an anti-tank barrier about 250 meters long to dragon teeth; the name comes from ...plan mort , plain of the dead, today natural monument. Beach nicknamed "Tahiti," one of the most popular in Sardinia, in the locality of Capo Coda Cavallo almost in front of the island of Tavolara. White sand and blue-turquoise water, with rocks that attract marine fauna and make it suitable for snorkeling; it is surrounded by a large pine forest and small dunes. According to the source, Garibaldi left here on October 17, 1867 to free Rome. It is reached from the SS125 turning towards Capo Coda Cavallo and continuing on a dirt road.

Pavilion built in the 1960s in the Butti Park at the behest of the widow of the sculptor Giacomo Buzzi Reschini and reopened in autumn 2006 after the restoration, it presents an anthology of the Viggiuto sculpture of the twentieth century. The central halls are dedicated to Buzzi Reschini, with the monumental group "The good that lands the evil" and sketches of monuments; one room is dedicated to Nando Conti and another to Bottinelli, Cattò, Cedraschi and Freschetti, with the plaster model of the head of the Baptist whose marble is in the parish church. Admission ticket, accessible to people with motor disabilities; opening hours: Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 14-18.30, Wednesday and Saturday 10-12 and 14-18.30, Sunday 16-19, Monday closed.

The only astronomical observatory in South Tyrol, about 1,340 meters to San Valentino in Campo, run by volunteers of the Astrofili Max Valier association, with several telescopes and an observation platform; public tours all year round on Thursday and Friday evening (in summer from 9 pm), cancelled with covered sky. Next, the Peter Anich solar observatory with a special filter telescope to see the surface of the Sun and the sunspots (in summer visit Friday at 2 pm), at the Untereggerhof farm on San Valentino di Sopra; always mandatory booking.

The original nucleus was a farmhouse on a hill surrounded by turrite walls, developed after the thousand around a watchtower and defended by a castle with gate and drawbridge; the castle, of Swabian era, passed in 1464 to Della Marra and is now privately owned. In the Terravecchia palazzi gentilizi alternate with ancient houses whitewashed with lime, between narrow alleys, arches of buttresses and external stairs.

At the edge of Foresto, in the area of the Posta della Posta della Posta, where horses and carriages were changed along the Via Francigena. The interior and exterior frescoes, from the last quarter of the 15th century, are attributed to the Tolosano Antoine de Lonhy: outside an Annunciation on the triumphal arch re-emerged with the restorations, inside a Pietà in the apse, the Stories of Anna and Gioacchino on the vault and a series of saints. Visits by reservation (0122 622640).

The largest and the furthest from the shore of the Borromean Islands (330 for 220 meters), dominated by a large English garden designed by Filippo Cagnola, with magnolias, wisteria, citrus fruits and white peacocks, golden pheasants and parrots in freedom. The sixteenth-century palace, with greenhouses and family chapel, preserves porcelain, period chandeliers, family portraits, canopy beds and a puppet theater used in the mid seventeenth century to entertain guests.

Founded in 1993 and re-established in 2008 in modern and colorful environments designed especially for children, it is the visitor center of the Rio Torsero Reserve and exhibits fossils of the lower Pliocene collected in the reserve. The path starts from a self-guided paleontological wardrobe on fossilization and local geology, continues with reconstructions of the Pliocene seabed and fossiliferous blocks and ends in a shell-shaped room on geological time; an optical microscope shows rocks and thin sections. Outside a botanical garden on the evolution of flora; under 6 free, over 65 free at the museum.

The walls of 1379 that enclose the village, crossed by Via Socccini; the Porta Senese preserves the ancient doors, while the Porta Romana was destroyed in 1944.

Roman water still running.

Built in the 15th century on a Romanesque building and renovated in the 19th century, it has only one nave with two side hats. The main portal in green stone, with vegetable frieze, mozzarella heads and a two-faced gianus, is among the best examples of the Romanesque Saluzzo; a lateral portal bears the date 1462. On the right wall the cycle of the brothers Tommaso and Matteo Biazaci (1460-1470) and the octagonal baptismal font in white Zabreri marble, dated 1482.
At the entrance to the village, it dates back to the 13th century: it has a bell dating back to 1382 and fifteenth-century frescoes from the Umbrian-Marche school.

Byzantine crypt of the Madonna delle Grazie, known as Santa Cristina (IX-XI century), dug into the rock in a system of rock houses: it is the oldest church in the country and testimony of the Greek rite. It preserves the most ancient frescoes of Puglia with known date and painter, starting from the Pantocrator of 959 attributed to Teofilatto; outside a small Baroque façade.
Seaside town on the Adriatic known for its velvet beach: the Round Sea on the sand, the Roveresca Rocca dei della Rovere and a historic centre with the Annunario Forum and the Herculanean Porticos.

Museum of enterprise with the machines used to extract the essence and the juice of bergamot.

The oldest castle in the city, of Norman origin, on the island of Megaride: the legend of the egg of Virgilio, terraces on the gulf, Normandy and Maestra towers and the prison of Queen Giovanna; at the foot the restaurants of the Borgo Marinari.

In a former Altomedieval Benedictine monastery founded under the Longobard counts, already antiquarium municipal since 1934: the history of Isernia from the archaic age to the Middle Ages and a section on the italic sanctuary of Pietrabbondante, with the armour discs and the bronze lare.

Morellino di Scansano has been DOC since 1978 and DOCG since the 2006 harvest.

The 19th-century theatre, commonly dated to 1841, named after the Naselli family who built Comiso in the 16th century in County; the façade of Doric-Siculus portico in white stone of Comiso was completed in 1859 by engineer Sortino. Rebuilt in the late seventies saving only the facade, it was reopened on November 25, 2000 after the restoration of Salvatore Catalano and Salvino Palumbo and has 264 seats.

Next to the convent of San Francesco, built in 1345, it preserves a sixteenth-century holy water table decorated with aquatic animals and medallions and a wooden confessional of the seventeenth century.
The Calabrian baroque in the heart of Sila.

Comune dell'Alta Langa which houses the italo-Russian collection of pastel paintings donated by artists, the chapel of San Rocco with fourteenth-century frescoes of the Passion and, along the SP281, the fifteenth-century sanctuary of the Madonna della Snow.

On the coast of the Sorrento peninsula, the Villa Fondi de Sangro, built in 1840, houses the archaeological museum named Georges Vallet and a park in 19th century style on a terrace overlooking the sea, overlooking the Gulf of Naples and the village of Marina di Cassano.

Medieval village on a hill above the valley of Carpina and the Upper Tiber Valley, home of the leader Braccio Fortebracci: three gates and three districts, the Gothic church of San Francesco with the municipal museum, the Collegiate Church that preserves the Santa Spina and, in the surroundings, the Rocca d'Aries and the old Pieve.

Born from the collection of the Turin-based researcher Augusto Doro and the Society of Historical Studies in Cuneo, it has been a museum since 1996 and in 2011 it has been re-equipped with a multimedia path. It tells the story of agriculture from its origins to the twentieth century: maps and models about the birth of the rural landscape, the cultivation of cereals, frescoes and scenes of palaces such as Lagnasco and Stupinigi, the photographs of Paul Scheuermeier and Clemens Kalisher. Opened in 1999 in the former convent of St. James (XIII-XIV century), around the cloister. The central piece is the Golden Bronzes by Cartoceto di Pergola, a Roman group discovered in 1946 with two knights, two horses and two female figures, among the very few large golden bronze equestrian groups from ancient times, presented in an immersive room with lights and multimedia contents of the physicist Paco Lanciano. The mosaics and funerary furnishings complete the route, more than 200 coins, paintings and sculptures from the 14th to the 18th century (among others Claudio Ridolfi and Giovanni Santi) and the engravings by Walter Valentini. Opening hours: from Tuesday to Sunday 10-12:30 and 15:30-18:30, Monday closed.

The hilly village of the Tronto Valley is still surrounded by the walls of the medieval castle, with the sixteenth-century municipal palace and the civic tower, the eighteenth-century Sanctuary of the Madonna delle Grazie and the Museum of Sculpture born from the National Sculpture Contest; in the plain, near Pagliare del Tronto, the Oasis La Valle with the museum of peasant civilization and the gauze of the herons ashes.

The first fortress on the hill arose between the 10th and 11th centuries and was enlarged in the 13th; between 1515 and 1546 Neapolitan architects transformed it into a residence for Prince Pietrantonio Sanseverino. Bombarded by the French in 1806, it remains a tower and the walls, recently restored in part.
Deep rocky gorge dug by the Cannobino in the Cannobina Valley, dominated by the seventeenth-century church of St. Anne.

The oldest church in Muro is one of the oldest in the Otranto Land, dating back to the IX-XI centuries, partly built with the blocks of the Messapian walls. A single nave with semicircular apse, it contains frescoes from the XI-XV centuries, including a cycle on the life of St. Nicholas before 1087, dated from the Touring around 1040 and considered the oldest dedicated to the saint.

The largest noble residence in Catania, with sumptuous salons that also host the Bellini Festival and the south façade, baroque triumph of Arabic and puttini.

Mountain village a few kilometers from Cascia where you can visit the birthplace with a late medieval look, the marital house transformed into a chapel with a seventeenth-century painting desired by Cardinal Fausto Poli, the lazzaretto of the Madonna della Concezione, the garden of the miracle and the rose garden, and the sanctuary of 1948 designed by Oreste della Piana, with a white marble porch and three naves.

Narrow streets and campidanese houses with internal courtyards and large wooden portals; among the historic residences Casa Cocco, Casa Olla and Casa Casella. The Municipal Palace, dating back to 1860, houses the municipal library and the historical archive.

Country on the slopes of the Mottarone above Stresa, an elite holiday destination in the early twentieth century with a Liberty imprint, known for the Museum of the Umbrella and Parasole designed by Igino Ambrosini, the sixteenth-century temple of San Rocco and the church of the Madonna del Sasso on Erno.
Garden in Serra Perno with a collection of over 500 specimens of botanical and ancient roses collected by Professor Piero Amerio; it is part of the historical gardens of Piedmont.
The place linked to Ambrogio, Marcellina and the relics of the Magi.

Museum in the Sandhof, home of Andreas Hofer, the host and cattle trader became Tyrolean hero. The permanent exhibition "Helden & Wir" links historic heroes to those of today, "Miër Psairer" introduces to the dialect and character of the valley, and outdoors the Haufenhof shows the typical farm at the court of Passiria. Built at the beginning of the 11th century by the counts Guidi, according to the tradition of Matilde di Canossa, it is one of the most important Romanesque churches in Casentino. Three aisles divided by six monolithic columns in serene stone with all different capitals, work of Lombard workers of the twelfth century; the frescoes walls coming from the parish church of San Niccolò (Crucifixion and St. Nicholas with Saints) and a seventeenth-century canvas with St. Simon Stock receiving the scapular from Our Lady.

View of the Foro Valley, the Teat Hills and the Highlands of the Maielletta; the local craftsmen work wood for wool castings.

Ancient water mill in the village of San Rocco, on the edge of the municipal territory, where the beating of the wheat takes place; from here you reach the fields of buckwheat in bloom. In Teglio, the Accademia del Pizzocchero keeps the original recipe of the pizzoccheri.

Brescello, founded in the 4th century BC by the Galli Cenomani and then Roman city that controlled the traffics on the Po between the 1st century BC and II AD: it starts from the necropolis of Brixellum with original stele, then the copy of the funerary monument of the Concordi found in Boretto in 1929, the reconstruction of a domus with mosaic floors and the history of the excavations.

In the former fairy tale mill, more than 150 works by the teacher and artist Adriana Filippi, who between 1943 and 1945 portrayed the life of the partisans of Valle Colla: the memory of the resistance in Boves, fired twice by the Germans in 1943. Going up to the historic centre you pass under the arch of the Clock Tower to the picturesque square of the Vegetables, with a loggia of the sixteenth century well preserved; at the end of the village the churches of San Leonardo and Piccina.

In an ancient mill of a small medieval village just outside the center: original tools, the process of bakery and peasant civilization. The ancient heart of Milan between the Duomo and Cordusio, with the Palazzo della Ragione started in 1228, today exhibition space, and the curious "gallery of whispers" under the arcades.

Medieval village that preserves its character within thirteenth-century walls, with access by one of the three ancient surviving doors; the position made it a strategic fortification to guard the Valdinievole and defend Pistoia.

On a cliff a hundred meters high, founded by the Longobards around the Thousand and devastated by order of Napoleon; here was born Carlo Borromeo in 1538. The park, the Borromeo, has been reopened since 2011.
