Monumental fountain attributed to the sixteenth century, an example of the mastery of the Paolani chiseling: two asymmetrical tanks, one inside the other, fed by four protomes each, and an obelisk in local sandstone. Ethnographic house-museum, the rooms of the grandparents, in a manor house of the late eighteenth century a few steps from the medieval complex of Sant'Antonio: it reproduces the peasant house with the loom room, the bedroom, sa lolla (the goddess), the kitchen, the tool room, the wine warehouse and the oven room, and collects weaving, basketry, copper and wrought iron artefacts, still living crafts in the village.

Borgo del Fermano remained largely enclosed in the ancient walls of the castle, known for centuries as "lu paese de li coccà" (the village of the potters). The medieval cistern, the canvas by Vincenzo Pagani in Santa Maria Ausiliatrice and the Ceramic Museum are worth seeing.

A hilly village in the south-east of Tricarico, in the heart of the Regional Park Gallipoli Cognato Piccole Dolomiti Lucane, with ancient aristocratic palaces overlooking the alleys; it is known for May, the spring rite of the wedding of the trees, told in the Museum of Arborean Cults.

The church, with a baroque façade, contains paintings from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries; in the garden the marble statue of St. Francis of Fra' Remo Rapone.
Borgo dell'Amiata on a cliff of trachyte above the fountains of the Fiora, divided into the terzieri of Castello, Borgo and Montecatino; feud Aldobrandeschi and then Sforza.

Opened in 2000 in the Prioral Palace, it illustrates the phases of the city with originals and replicas: the copy of the polychrome mosaic discovered in 1780 in the octagonal room of the thermal baths (centaurs and Greeks around a head of Medusa, original to the Vatican Museums), a statue of Augustus from the basilica of the forum, funeral inscriptions of the Via Flaminia (I century BC-II century AD), an altar table of the 6th century and the only cast of the colossal head of the Jupiter of Otricoli, discovered at the end of the 18th century.

hedges, meadows and moats of the Treviso plain on foot.

Built between the end of the sixteenth century and the beginning of the seventeenth century at the behest of Francesco Gonzaga, bishop of Mantua; inside stand out the paintings of Andrea Mainardi called the Chiaveghino, of the school of the Camps.

Rebuilt in the nineteenth century after the destruction of 1806, reopened in 1829 and consecrated in 1833: it preserves an organ of 1863 and the Romanesque bell tower, the only rest of the church of Santa Maria Âd lacumÂ; on the square a fountain dated 1651.

According to tradition, it was born from an image of the Virgin painted on a pylon that, wounded to one eye by a thorn, began to bleed; already in 1585 the bishop of Asti described there a great turnout of faithful. Etruscan village founded in the fourth century BC near the border of Vulci, on the right of the Albegna, perhaps refuge from the Roman assaults or center of wine producers; it was conquered and devastated in 280 BC. The best preserved part is the 1 km long walls and about 4 meters thick; inside the remains of the small Temple of a farm deity, whose ex-vote are at the Archaeological Museum.
17th century fountain with three masks and bathtub used as a watering trough, next to the eighteenth-century church of the Addolorata.
Small town of the lower comasca, about 3,000 inhabitants, known for the fifteenth-century Sanctuary of the Madonna del Noce and for the Museum of the Horse toy, set up in the former stables Tornese.
Castle of the Perugino countryside with the tower of Porta Santa Maria, Piazza Coragino and the church of Santa Maria Assunta with the altarpiece of Perugino.
Municipal museum that collects objects related to the daily life and work of the local community, together with Neolithic finds.

The hypogeic Nuragic Temple, perhaps of the recent Bronze (XIV-XII century BC), in a rock split about 150 meters long: a staircase of squared basalt blocks descends into three ramps (24 and 22 visible steps) up to the water, with possibly shiny cavities and breast-shaped reliefs linked to the mother goddess. In Punic-Roman age it was the sanctuary of Demeter; just outside there is the Funtana de on Prantu, tholos structure with five niches.
Overlooking one of the largest squares in Italy.

Longobard fortification of the IX-X century, cited in 1137 when the Norman Roberto Morra pursued the abbot Rainaldo of Montecassino; he passed to the Giamvilla and the Caracciolo, who at the beginning of the seventeenth century made it a residence, and then returned to the Morra. Damaged by the earthquake of 1695, by the French looting of 1799, by the fire of 1911 that destroyed the library and by the earthquake of 1980, in the eighties it was donated to the municipality. The stone façade remains and part of the two circular towers at the entrance; in the atrium there is a Roman milestone of the I-III century.

Part of the fifth and last circle of walls, erected between 1330 and 1440 for 7,117 meters; with Porta Villalta is the only survivor of the thirteen gates of the city, with the path of a round lace.

The first circle, oval, has the oldest parts to the sixth century and the present masonry to the fifteenth; the second, of the thirteenth century, was adapted to firearms by Francesco di Giorgio Martini. The Bastione di Sant'Anna is today an Italian garden with geometric flower beds, and from the viewpoint along the walls you can see the Conero and the marina; you can also enter from Porta Fanestre and Porta Santa Maria.

Romanesque church built around 1170 as part of an important Benedictine complex, whose monastery was destroyed by a fire in 1183 and never rebuilt (signs are still visible on the pillars). It recalls the Romanesque Apulian of San Nicola di Bari, with the three apses enclosed in a straight wall and the façade in brick and white stone with circular window facing the Gran Sasso; the interior with three naves has cruciform pillars and wooden trusses. The frescoes of 1181 in the central apse show the blessing Christ in almond supported by angels, saints and scenes of the Old and New Testaments, including the Annunciation; it preserves a staurotheque with a fragment of the Cross.
Basilica-style building with three naves with Baroque façade, built on the family chapel of the Counts Valperga, with first news from the twelfth century. It is accessed from a large staircase.

The castle Sancti Severini, mentioned already in 1116, bishop's seat since 1580, was severely damaged by the earthquake of 1627 and rebuilt with new churches and convents, with low buildings usually on two floors and a chessboard expansion beyond the walls. Around Piazza Municipio characteristic streets and gentle palaces with coats of arms, the Palazzo dei Celestini and the Episcopio founded in 1668. Ruins on a height at the foot of the Tuttavista, above the plain of Cedrino: fortress of the 11th century on a previous Roman fortification, conquered by the Aragonese in the 14th century and abandoned in the 15th century. Municipality of Serra morainica between Biella and Ivrea, on the right of the Elven, which shares with Borriana, Cerrione and Mongrando the Natural Reserve of Bessa, the heaps of pebbles left by the Roman gold mine. Only village of the Municipality, five kilometers from the chief town. The village is known for its viewpoint; the main church of Santa Maria Assunta was renovated and expanded on a project by Francesco Patella.

One of the most beautiful castles in Molise, with its stories of horses and majolica.

A pilgrimage destination in Pagliara, center of Marian devotion and mother house of the Institute of the Franciscan Friars of the Immaculate Church; it houses a reed organ of 25 registers of the Venetian builder Alessandro Girotto.

Dedicated to the patron saint of Sora, who according to tradition was martyred on May 27, 275; rebuilt in the early twentieth century, it preserves a portal of the thirteenth century. The story of the saint is narrated on the bronze portal of the Anagnino sculptor Gismondi.

Stone tower house built around 1200 for defensive and residential purposes in the agricultural hamlet of Pradello; originally 28 meters high, it was lowered at the end of the nineteenth century to avoid its collapse. According to some scholars it belonged to the family of Christopher Columbus before the transfer to Genoa, and the documents indicate it as property of the grandfather. In 1957 he bought it and restored it as a Colombian Museum Molinari, Piacenza emigrated and then director of the Waldorf Astoria in New York; today he is from the Municipality and is visited only by reservation (328 8714929). From the museum starts a path towards Ebbio, in the red lands.
It overlooks the main square, where the Porta Grande stood; wanted by the Knights of Malta, several times renovated, it preserves small mills on the ground floor.

Municipality of Costa degli Aranci linked to Cassiodoro, which founded the Vivarium monastery in the gulf: on the headland of Copanello remain the  "Vasche di Cassiodoro" excavated in the cliff, while Caminia and Copanello are awarded beaches with the Vele Legambiente; in the village the Museo naturalistico Libero Gatti has a botanical garden overlooking the Ionian.

In four restored rooms of the seventeenth-century nucleus of the Duomo, finds from Tusculum and Tuscolane villas (an iron age anforet, a polychrome mosaic, frescoes, statues and coins), a medieval papal bull, majolica, seventeenth-century paintings and original documents.
Inside the city's most heartfelt party.
The church was born when the cave became a street.
The castle that gives the name.
The villa on the hill.
The story of the Valdesi told in their "capital."
Secular beech trees in altitude.
The most beautiful sculpture museum in Italy.

Promontory at the western end of the Cinque Terre that separates the bay of Levanto from that of Monterosso, with sandstone walls at layers overlooking the sea. On top of the Sepaforo del Mesco, used by the military until the Second World War and today abandoned, and the medieval hermitage of St. Anthony of Mesco, documented in 1380. It is reached on foot with two paths in the woods, from Levanto or Monterosso.
One of South Tyrol's best preserved castles.
For one of the most important painting cycles in Europe.
The country church with a Bourbon gift.
The green canyon of the Sentino.
The eastern front of the fortress seen from above.
The panorama of the Canavese.

A small town on the slopes of Monte Rullo Rosso, near the Falcone and Borsellino airport, feud granted by Frederick II in 1241, Baronia since 1556 and then county; you can visit the octagonal Mother Church with the frescoes of Giuseppe Trisca, the caves and the prehistoric necropolis of the territory and the House Museum Villa Africa of African ethnography.

A hill country on the Val di Cecina, documented by the 13th century but perhaps of Etruscan origin, linked to the quarries of the alabaster "Bianco di Castellina": this is where the central museum of the Alabaster Ecomuseum is located; around the village, with the Romanesque parish church and the remains of the fortress, five ring paths in the woods with a view to the sea and Corsica.
The Caetani garden on the lake.
The Mask's palace.

Roof built in August 1699, as a stone recalls, at the expense of the parishioners of San Grato and the territories of Tavernette, Scalenghe, Airasca and Marsaglia, on a land purchased by the Municipality in 1695, for the rest and shelter of residents and foreigners. Always accessible.
Lighthouse of the early twentieth century on the slopes of the Mount of the Madonna; next, a small coastal lake fed by fresh and brackish underground waters.
The traces of the Hebrew Enna.
16th century church on a square next to Piazza Minozzi.
A Roman façade on the square.

The nineteenth-century church was restored by the architect Sacconi; in the caves below there is a mechanical nativity scene of about 250 square meters, designed in 1992 by Fernando and Ilario Testa and Massimo Benedetti.
The Norman tower of Enna's siege.
Lungolago tree-lined of about three kilometers with restaurants, on Lake Bracciano, volcanic lake where motor boats are not allowed and you can go canoeing, sailing and windsurfing.

The road of Udine, derived from the torrent Torre and mentioned in a document dated 1171, crosses the municipality with the stone banks built by the Republic of Venice in the eighteenth century, called "Rosta Feracina" from the name of the builder; in Valle the road of Palma is detached. On the Tower there are the gripping works of the two roges.

Borgo della Langa Cebana in Bormida valley, with the castle of the Marchese del Carretto, the churches of the center can be visited by reservation and, on the hill, the sixteenth-century sanctuary of the Madonna della Snow.
History, art and devotion of the lower Valsesia in an eighteenth century castle.
A Renaissance polyptych in a hamlet church.
The village of Pope Leo XIII.
Tracks of the first century BC wall, when Novara became town hall with Julius Caesar, visible in Piazza Cavour and Via Solaroli.
The naval models.
One of Dante's castles.

House of the end of the nineteenth century in the square called "mesu idda" , of which Aunt Carmela was the penultimate owner: four rooms on the rural life with tools for wood, agriculture and breeding, the preservation of food, the attic of supplies and the corner of bread with the grinder moved by the donkey.

An important example of medieval town planning, connected to the neighbouring villages by ancient mule tracks suitable for excursions; the road to Panicagliora and Serra offers views of the castle between the peaks of the Apennines.
The 46-metre dome on the plain.
Panicale's embroidery.
A nineteenth-century fountain with carved faces.
Theatre of the eighteenth century: the project was entrusted in 1769 to Cosimo Morelli, who adapted the design of Bibiena.
One of the green oasis of the historic center, where you can walk among the rare species along with the Cappuccini Gardens and Public Gardens.

Born to pass on the knowledge related to the processing of clay, since 2001 it deals with the memory of the places, regeneration of furnaces and quarries, signs of man in the landscape, design in clay and art; it also includes an oasis in a renaturalized quarry, habitats of wild species. It offers guided tours, handicraft workshops and experiences. Open every day only by reservation (349 1396240); free for under 14, over 65 and Museum Subscription holders.
The last shop that still weaves Lorsica's damask.
The sanctuary of the saints of Lovere.

In the hamlet of Piagge, you can reach it with the Pilgrim's Path, a mountain path in the woods; here the founder of the Clarisse of the place spent a year in prayer, and today the cave is a small rock church overlooking the mountains of Cicolo.
A millenarian church in Romanesque-Maltildian style of the 11th century, with remains of frescoes from the 15th and 16th centuries; free access.
A historic park with a Roman tomb.
The temple of Livorno food.
A Roman sanctuary on terraces on the valley.

Venue of the Municipality from the thirteenth to the nineteenth century, with piazza Palazzo Vecchio, called "dei Pisces" for the ancient fish market, dominated by the Civic Tower, the oldest of Vercelli.

From the Ruata (1130 m), on foot or by car on dirt road up to the Lazarà hill, you climb to the Gran Truc (2360 m, iron cross), at whose feet is the Lauzoun lake (2050 m); hard and challenging climb, from a day, without springs from the Lazarà to the summit. The lake is also reached from the Gardetta between rhododendrons and alders, with a spring in half; above, the lakes of Conca Cialancia.

A village of about 700 inhabitants of Barigadu, near Lake Omodeo, with houses in red trachite and windows in Aragonese style, the 17th century parish church of San Pietro and, on the slopes of Mount Santa Vittoria, the Faunistic oasis of Assai with its small museum.

Marzolina is a soft and spicy goat cheese with an intense taste, which takes its name from March, when it was produced, celebrated at the end of June; the laine and ciciri are fresh pasta with chickpea sauce. Ausonia is also an important marble machining centre, with the Pearl royal.

The town of Media Valtellina known for the Park of the Rupestri Engravings, with the Rupe Magna and its more than 5000 figures under the remains of two medieval castles, and for the Villa Visconti Venosta, now a civic museum in a public park; in the historical center narrow streets with palaces, portals and fountains and the birthplace of the painter Cipriano Valorsa.

One of the nine sacred pre-Alpine Mountains UNESCO heritage: built in the mid-17th century and completed in 1710, it has fourteen chapels with 230 statues in stucco and terracotta, mostly of Agostino Silva, and frescoes by Carlo Gaffuri, Francesco Innocenzo Torriani and Giovan Paolo Recchi; the route climbs to the sanctuary of the Madonna del Soccorso (XVI century, modified until the eighteenth century). The sanctuary is not reached by car; parking space at the first and fourth chapels.
The heart of Agliano's thermal activity, where the waters to which the town owes its name and fame flow abundant.
Houses born from the rock under the castle.

Route of the Ulysses Riviera Park of 2.3 km (about 2 hours, difficulty E, 200 m of difference in altitude) from Piazzale Caboto: Via Faustina, San Francesco, the villas on the hairpin bends with views of the castles, the battery of Monte Orlando Lower up to the mausoleum of Lucio Munazio Planco on top of the mountain. Not accessible to disabled people.
Always accessible from the street

On two hills in San Salvatore, about 5 km from the village: a domus de Janas of the recent Neolithic, a nuraghe with a central tower in tholos, walls, three secondary towers and a dozen huts, silos and a hamlet of the mill, a tomb of Giants of the XV century BC with menhir still standing and a circle of stones of 12 meters. The site was used until Roman and Byzantine times.

Permanent exhibition established in 1989 in a wing of the Palazzo Perlasca-Pinchetti (1608), today of the Spalla-Gandola family, of which it houses the collections of stuccoes and chess in three exhibition sections. It is the only museum entirely dedicated to this sector, the art that has made famous the masters of the valley. Open in July and August on Saturdays and holidays 15.30-18; from May to October guided tours for small groups by reservation (tel. 333 1223598, museum.scagliolaintelvese@gmail.com).
Nature intact in the Circeo Park.
The peasant life of Sila in a school museum.
Three thousand years of history on the sea.
The Baìo, one of the oldest festivals in the Alps, told by its drapes.
The whole Tremezzina on foot, villa after villa.

13th-century tower in via Voltazzi, in the village of Nadro, to which was later flanked the noble house of the Gaioni family; the village is, with Ceto and Badetto, one of the three localities of the municipality and the gateway to the Engraving Reserve.
Panoramic path along the lake with heart-shaped installations and postcard views, where you can take a souvenir photo.
The cable car that connects Bolzano to the Renon plateau with a view of the Dolomites, where the earth pyramids are located.

In the seventeenth century Palazzo De Simoni, built on the remains of a medieval castle of which the tower remains, 27 rooms and over 4,000 objects between historical-artistic and ethnographic section: carpenter and slipper shops, tools of milk, fields and weaving, old skis, relics of the First World War, paintings, shovels and furniture, and a great diligence in service on the Stelvio until 1915 with carriages and sleds.
The panoramic balcony on the upper Val di Sole.
Two centuries of Sicilian fashion in a noble palace.

Theatre Augusteo expanded under Antonino Pio, with cavea of 110 meters to three orders for 7,000-10,000 spectators, dug and restored between 1999 and 2003; near, on the terrace of the hole, the cryptoporic of the syllable age with three arms with graffiti stuccos of names of poets and verses of Virgilio.
Trekking and biking on the Apennines.
The village-fortress against the Roman advance, reachable on foot from the valley of Lanaittu.

Rocca on a rocky ridge with steep walls, 300 meters above Palizzi Superiore, perhaps from the thirteenth century or built by the Ruffo in the fourteenth; born as a fortified building dug into the living rock, it has been renovated several times and is declared a national monument. It is the subject of a consolidation and restoration for the tourist usability financed by the MiC. View of the valley and the Ionian Greek coast.

Route of the Parco dei Castelli Romani from the Convent of San Silvestro (630 m) to the Sanctuary of the Madonna della Neve of Rocca Priora: 4 km, 186 m ascent and 99 m descent, about 1 hour and 40 minutes, difficulty T.
Opened on September 1, 2002 in the basement of the Castle of the Counts Friend, it collects evidence of the life of a time.
The mushroom rock in the heart of the country.

Selegas has the parish church of Sant'Anna with the parish museum of sacred art and the facades painted by the painter Liliana Cano. In the hamlet of Seuni stands the sanctuary of Santa Vittoria; in the territory was found the Mother Goddess of Turriga, today at the National Archaeological Museum of Cagliari.
The catwalks on the water between the herons.
The ancient Histonium overlooking the sea, half a kilometer from the coast: Palazzo d'Avalos with the civic museums, the Caldoresco Castle, Piazza Rossetti and the walks to the sea.
White stone walls, 4.8 kilometres long, completed in 1316, with 86 towers and 19 gates, including Porta Branconia, Porta Rivera, Porta Napoli, Porta Bazzano, Porta Leone and Porta Castello.
The monument of Ettore Ferrari of 1896 in Piazza Garibaldi, the second square of the city next to the Teatro Sociale.

Small church built in 1834 after an epidemic of cholera. It houses an altarpiece with a Madonna adoring Bolognese school of the early sixteenth century and, in a chapel, an Annunciation attributed to a pupil of the Nuvolone school.
Medieval ruins in the forest of the park.

The tower, part of the oldest, dates back to the 11th century and was raised around 1385 by Francesco il Vecchio da Carrara. It is located in the middle of the river Bacchiglione, on the border between Padua and Vicenza. In 1324 Padua donated it to the Carraresi; then passed to Venice and to the Vendramin, who transformed it into a villa (according to tradition there was guest Giorgione). Recovered in the eighties, it houses an exhibition space on the river Bacchiglione with finds from the late Neolithic to the modern age. Guided visits: tel. 351 8401432.

Also known as the Saracen Cave, it is a natural cave at the foot of a rocky wall closed by a wall in stone and mortar of the tenth century, often about 70 cm at the base, tied to Saracen raids; the excavations of 1979-1982 found traces of human presence in the Neolithic. Visit Cuneese indicates it as the largest fortified cave in the Western Alps.
Places of devotion of the border fraction.
The view of Angera.

Country at the entrance of the Varaita Valley, already of the Marquises of Saluzzo and then feud of the Porporato, seat of the Museum of the Harp Victor Salvi; in his churches and chapels he worked in the first fifteenth century Pietro da Saluzzo, the Master of the Villar.
Gold fillings and a set by Pietro Germi.
Porticato 15th century left of the Loggia di San Giovanni, from which begins the ascent to the Castle Hill.
An easy ride around the lake, between woods and the Dolomites.
The largest and most sumptuous noble residence in the city, wanted by Andrea Doria from the 1920s and decorated by Perin del Vaga; in 1533 the emperor Charles V stayed there.

The park of the villa, on the top of the hill called "castle" has 12 monumental trees and 160 species of rare and exotic plants, some centuries old, including a sequoia, a cedar of the Atlas and a rate about 20 meters high, with small tabernacles and caves scattered in the green. It hosts some sculptures of the route "Equilibri in natura" and, on the second Sunday of September, the National Bird Fair, which has been held for over 60 years.
The rustic villas of Vesuvius and their treasure.
Woods, sinkholes and memories of the Great War over the Piave.

Church of the 14th century built on the remains of a pagan temple, with a sixteenth-century Renaissance portico and portal in Catalan style, enlarged from three to four naves at the end of the 15th century. It houses a polyptych attributed to Antonello de Saliba or Pietro Ruzzolone, the Madonna degli Angeli in marble by Antonello Gagini, the fifteenth-century frescoes by the Spousalizio delle Vergini and Santa Caterina d'Alessandria and a frescoed crypt in the sixteenth century with scenes of the Passion.
A high-rise village between Messapian walls and castle.
A village of tombs with dice dug in a hill of tuff, some reused in Roman times; among the most important burials the Tomb of the Sphinx.

On the shore of a small lake about three kilometers from the village: the first church, seventeenth-century and dedicated to the Visitation, was enlarged in 1842 and today houses an inn, while the current sanctuary is of the late nineteenth century. On the first Sunday of July there is the Procession of the Christs, with the Ligurian and Piedmontese confraternities that carry great crucifixes around the lake; from here start trails towards the High Via dei Monti Liguri and the Armetta, Dubasso and Galero mountains.
Orvieto from above.
The sanctuary above Corniglia linked to the restoration considered miraculous of a painting of the Virgin, stage of the Via dei Santuari.

In the former church of San Francesco, part of the ancient hospital, which since the eighties hosted the National Exhibition of Contemporary Painting  "Santhià" promoted by the Pro Loco founded in 1962: the paintings awarded in various editions form the Civic Gallery of Modern Art City of Santhià, with over 350 works exhibited on the walls of the Auditorium. Rotating art exhibitions are also held at the Jacopo Durandi Cultural Centre.
Weighing on the Moon in a unique museum in Italy.
A Sunday in the open air in the Bourbon hunting woods.
The geological history of the Dolomites.
The watchman from the lake.
One of the monumental trees of Italy.
The fourteenth-century baptistery next to the Cathedral is now the seat of the Diocesan Museum, which exhibits its gallery in the Hall of Audiences of the Papal Palace.
Nature in the original state a stone's throw from the castle.
From the fishing port, the capital of clams, the boats depart to the Island of Love, a tongue of sand with dunes that change with winds and tides.
The castle of Queen Margherita on the walls of Sannite.
The Roman Tergeste in stone.

Inaugurated in 2008 in the 18th century Palazzo Mazzonis, in the heart of the Quadrilatero, with galleries dedicated to China, Japan, South and South-East Asia, Himalayan region and Islamic countries of Asia.
Museum dedicated to ceramics set up for a few years.

Established in 2009, it extends for about 7,400 hectares between Antrona Schieranco and Borgomezzavalle, from 500 meters up to 3,656 of Pizzo Andolla, with the Val Troncone, the Val Banella and the high Val Loranco. It includes the rare natural barrier lake of Antrona and four artificial basins (Cingino, Campliccio, Camposecco and Alpe dei Cavalli) and borders the Swiss reserve of Laggintal.

In the medieval Palazzo della Residenza the Resurrection of Piero della Francesca (1450-1463, restored in 2018), the Polyptych of Mercy, the fragments of San Giuliano and San Ludovico, the San Quintino di Pontormo and Robbian terracotta.

A path proposed by the Museum that climbs from the archpriest church to Pettenello in the woods to the castle and continues along Via Ricò towards Barbiano, with views of the Rio del Castello valley and Baganza valley, bordered by the calanchi of Maiatico who hit Garibaldi in April 1861; through Via Carroni you cross forests of chestnuts, oaks and maples, inhabited by squirrels and green peaks.
It is the tallest museum in Europe, 2950 meters away, which can be reached in summer by cable car from Malga Ciapela towards Punta Rocca.

Easy hike of about 2 km and 270 meters of difference in altitude (about one hour) from the locality Montallegro, with parking near a farm. The hairpin bends and an intermediate space with benches and grids open the view on the lakes of Varese, Maggiore, Monate and Comabbio; on the summit a chapel houses a statue of the Redeemer.

Anthropological demoetanological museum opened on June 2, 2004 in the restored medieval castle, in the Clock Tower: without permanent collections, it tells the cultural uses of stone from the Middle Ages to today, with monitors, panels, audio and showcases on geology from the plain to the mountain and a section on the processing; the castle itself, all in stone, is the main object exposed. MiC timetables: Monday and Sunday 10-17, Friday and Saturday closed; booking not required.

Regional park since 1975, born to retrain the outskirts north of Milan, of about 1,000 hectares between Milan, Sesto San Giovanni, Cinisello Balsamo, Bresso, Cormano, Cusano Milanino and Novate Milanese. Lawns with rows, groves (about 100 hectares of wood in the north-east sector), fields and wetlands, including the pond of Cinisello; the agricultural area of Balossa is a stopover and nesting place for migratory birds.
The dome overlooking the historic centre.
Mountain of legends for families.
The tools of the wood trade.
A mill from the 18th century.
The marsh crafts told in a fishing house on the river.

Borgo on a promontory on the Trasimeno between Torricella and San Feliciano, surrounded by walls from Perugia from 1312 against Henry VII and in the sixteenth century seat of the Apostolic Chamber, with the Fortress at the eastern entrance and the Porta Trasimena. In the church of Sant'Andrea a great Crucifixion of the late fourteenth century; at the entrance Villa Aganoor Pompilj, where lived the poetess Victoria Aganoor, and under Palazzo Schnabl, living room of artists and home of the musicologist Riccardo Rossi Schnabl, friend of Puccini. In September the Festival of Correspondence.
Medieval ruins overlooking the narrow of the Tagliamento.

Medieval nucleus with crenellated towers enclosed in the sixteenth century by the Marquis Giovan Battista de' Monti in a Renaissance fortress with four towers dedicated each to a saint and a cardinal virtue; in the seventeenth century he received the Baroque façade with allegorical statues and busts of leaders, in the eighteenth century became a mill and pasta factory. Today it hosts guided tours, events, workshops of the project "Il Castello Volante" , restaurant and coffee.

The Po golena, the heart of the territory, with the houses often on stilts between poplars and birch trees, offers walks, birdwatching and views of the river; the former Cava Puccio is an environmental recovery area with educational trails and nature trails.

Orto dell'Università Statale di Milano was born for the study of medicinal plants: today it hosts more than 600 species, with thematic routes to follow independently. Open from mid-April to mid-October with seasonal hours (in winter only by appointment); guided tours and paid workshops.

Church already existed before 1361, demolished in 1853-1854 and rebuilt larger, consecrated in 1868: it has five altars and an organ of 1931 with 701 reeds. The granite bell tower dates back to the second half of the thirteenth century.

Country of the Canavese on a hill on the right of the Dora Baltea, once on the border between Canavese and Vercellese: at the top of the historic center, with the remains of the shelter and nineteenth-century palaces, stands the castle of the Valperga with the museum of the instruments of the Inquisition in the underground; from the castle a path descends to the Dora.
The Resistance in Val Pellice told on the spot.
The oldest church in the area.
The highest peak of Friuli Venezia Giulia.
Romanesque, 1253, belonged to the Roman Hospital of the Holy Spirit in Saxia, whose portal bears the cross of Lorraine; remodelled in 1757.

17th century church in the center of the village, on a large churchyard on top of a small hill in front of the masse of Palazzo Spinola; you can climb there with a double ramp from the piazzale del palazzo.
Roman surgical instruments, still in their place.
Garibaldi in Rovigo.

The bell tower of Sant'Andrea, about 30 meters high, dates back to the 11th-XII century; once a beacon and a watch tower, it still has a clock attested in 1386 that the city portal defines the oldest working tower clock in the world. The vertical museum exhibits historical maps of the city, ex-vote, a stole of Cardinal Aristide Naccari and an astronomical route with astrolabe; from the top you can visit the mechanism and the bell cell.
MiC card (updated 2020) indicates "closed" every day: check opening (tel. 0773 841501)
A village gathered around the fortress.
The stones that paved St. Peter's Square, under their feet.

Designed by architect Zumpano, built from 1887 and inaugurated in 1909 with Aida: about 800 seats on three orders of stages and the historic curtain of Paolo Vetri with the arrival in the city of Louis III of Anjou and Margaret of Savoy.

In a palace designed by Vignola in the second half of the sixteenth century, on two floors the funerary furnishings of the Etruscan necropolis of Vigna la Piazza, Pianezze e Centocamere: on the first floor the daily life and the richness of the elites (room "I Segni del Potere" with the Tomb 31 and the "tomba della bambina") on the ground floor the funeral rite with the life-size reconstruction of a bedroom tomb and an original sarcophagus in monolithic tuff. It is part of the Museum System of Lake Bolsena; the ticket also applies to necropolis.
The imperial greatness of Benevento.

The town of Oltrepò Mantua, south of Mantua towards the borders with Reggio Emilia and Modena, entered the beginning of the 11th century in the Canossa domains; to see the Romanesque parish church of San Lorenzo, the small Archaeological Civic Museum with the Roman finds of the local excavations and the San Lorenzo Park.
A wooden crucifix of the sixteenth century.

Between 680 and 1,900 metres, the scattered municipality of the Alto Garda Bresciano Park with the hamlets of Turano, Armo, Persone and Moerna around the artificial lake fed by Toscolano; in Moerna the Botanical Museum Don Pietro Porta tells the flora of the valley.
The memory of the Resistance in val d'Enza.
Know the lagoon before we go out there.
Walking in an ideal 15th century city.

In the former Fenulli Caserm, 5,000 square meters on three floors and 33 rooms: uniforms, decorations, weapons, relics and a rich photographic archive from 1861 to today, with the gallery on the School of Cavalry and the room dedicated to Federigo Caprilli.
The Marian shrine of the diocese.

The city of the Acajas, dominated by the fourteenth-century Castle of the Princes of Acaja with its four towers; along the portico via Roma you will find the neoclassical cathedral of Mario Ludovico Quarini and the baroque church of the Battuti Rossi by Francesco Gallo, while panoramic avenues overlooking the ancient walls overlook the valley of Stura and the Alps.

Ecomuseum dedicated to the Walser culture of Campello Monti (Kampel), promoted since 1993 by the Walsergemeinschaft Kampel association with research initiatives; on the first Saturday of August it hosts the annual conference "Campello" and the Walser" .

Probably built at the beginning of the 15th century, it was bought by Lorenzo and Giuliano de' Medici in 1476; it was a hunting residence and center of the Grand Duke's Farm, which counted over twenty farms.

Pharmacy and liquor store with 17th century furnishings, vases and crystals, frescoed by G. Not with Pompeian themes; it preserves original showcases and containers of medicines and, in front, a living room decorated by Balbi once used as a guesthouse.

Cittadina del Biellese orientale sul creente Strona; in the hamlet Castellengo, on the edge of the plateau of the baragges, there are the castle of the Frichignono, the Romanesque parish church of the Saints Peter and Paul with late-Gothic frescoes and the Eco-Museum of Cossathes and Baragge; in the village the eighteenth-century Villa Ranzoni.
The house where "Dedo" was born, today the museum with documents and photographs of the life of the artist.
The Head symbol.
Built after the earthquake of 1783 in the hamlet of Santa Giorgia, instead of the church of Santa Maria del Soccorso, it houses the statue of Maria della Catena.
The Punic and Roman city.
Cagliari under the bombs of 1943.
The historic bay of the coast of Trieste.
The church of the Marquises.
From the tower you can see Amiata, Appennino and the lakes Trasimeno and Bolsena.
Reservation required according to the MiC card (updated to January 2022)
The mother church overlooking the Gonzaghesca square.

Village of the Anglona overlooking the valley of the Carrucana river, Martis is known for the Gothic ruins of San Pantaleo on a rocky spur and for the petrified forest of Carrucana. Just outside the village there is the waterfall of Triulintas, in the gorge of Badde Traes.

In the park: panels on woods, traditional architecture and history of the territory, flora and fauna with stuffed animals, the presence of man in the valley over the centuries; outside an ethnobotanic path.

Opened on 22 January 1994 for the fiftieth anniversary, in a hall of Villa Adele, it recalls Operation Shingle of 22 January 1944, when the Allies landed between Tor San Lorenzo and Torre Astura. Four sections (English, American, German and Italian) with medals, uniforms, flags, weapons, battle plans, motor vehicles and vintage photos, more photo library, tape library, library and hemeroteca; some finds come from the backdrops of Anzio, the wrecks of British ships Janus and Spartan and the hospital ship St. David. Closed on Monday, Wednesday only morning.
From here you can see Venice.
The oldest market in the city.
The Romanesque parish church of the 10th century, about 5 km from the village, praised by Giosuè Carducci and linked to the memory of Dante.
Built between 1322 and 1338 by Angelo da Orvieto, with rustic, octagonal pillars, cruising vault and a sixteenth-century staircase to the Council Hall.
Low sea between white rocks and a Spanish tower.
The historical Verona taverns.
challenging alpine excursion, check weather and opening of the Similaun hut (Südtirol)
The most beautiful village in Italy, the birthplace of Giuseppe Pellizza, where the fourth state was born: its workshop and reproductions of the works next to the landscapes that inspired them.
A masterpiece of the Nuragic age.
Tight and winding alleys, steep steps, courtyards and underpasses that reveal the Arab origin of the country.

In the lower Val Nure, Vigolzone joins the fourteenth-century castle of Anguissola to the hamlet of Grazzano Visconti, a neo-medieval village born in the early twentieth century around the castle and the large park of the Visconti di Modrone; among the wine hills are the Museum of Vine and Wine in La Tosa, the villa of Collegio Alberoni in Veano and the panoramic points of Chiulano and Bagnolo.
Nature and archaeology together.

It rises between the IX and X century as castle fortress and completed in Norman times, it is 27 meters high, with walls more than 5 meters thick on 4 levels. In 1333 the castle was donated to the Clarisses for the monastery of Santa Chiara; the tower maintained military function until 1657 when Duke Ippolito Revertera donated it to the monastery. National monument since 1931.
The herons in the gauze.

Built between the 11th and 16th centuries in local limestone, the main example of Romanesque of the valley, with the large wooden statue of St. Christopher and a pulpit of the 12th century on columns of red marble.
The peaks above Aosta.
Birdwatching on the lake at the confluence of Sangro and Aventino.
The Roman Bridge of Loneliness.
We'll weave it in the woods above the abbey.
A baroque villa reborn as a cultural center.

In the former Augustinian convent of Santa Maria Novella (founded in 1438, restored between 1998 and 2003) tells the story of Bracciano from the Etruscan settlements to the nineteenth century in five rooms: the Community, the Etruscan age, the Roman and early Christian age with part of the Panunzi collection, clients and artists with a work of Christopher States, sacred art with the ...Cristo Salvator Mundi attributed to the circle of Andrea Bregno. Next, the church rebuilt from 1765 on a project by Nicola Faggioli with the Assumption of Taddeo Kuntze in the apse.
Villa and historical park, heart of the Wine Fair.
In the village of medieval origins with Romanesque bell tower; inside an exhibition of wooden statues and liturgical furnishings, including a statue of the fourteenth century.

Irpino village dominated by the medieval castle at 820 meters, where Giambattista Basile was governor and sketched Lo Cunto de li Cunti; it preserves the medieval crypt of the ancient cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta with the relics of San Giovanni and two museums, sacred and ethnomusical wallpapers.

Reserve of about 10 hectares on the border between Caravaggio and Pagazzano, among woods, cultivated, water mirrors and marshy vegetation, around one of the oldest springs of the area. There live frogs, European mole and foxes and especially many birds, from heron ashes to kingfisher and barbarian. You visit only along the marked routes.
The tree under which he meditated Vico.

Probably started in 1498 on a central plan of the Amadeus: the bell tower of Paolo della Porta (1511-1516), the frescoes of Bernardino Luini in the main chapel (since 1525) and the dome painted by Gaudenzio Ferrari (1534); the façade was built in 1596 by Lelio Buzzi under the direction of Pellegrino Tibaldi.
The road is closed to traffic, flat, an hour of walk between rocks, waterfalls, meadows and woods along the emerald green waters.
The avenue of about 5 km of secular cypresses from San Guido to Bolgheri, made famous by Carducci and considered a national monument.
Archaeology, fossils and costumes of the city.
A karst canyon inhabited from prehistory to the Middle Ages.

The village, mentioned already in the lower Middle Ages, grew in the eighteenth century with fruit growing, viticulture and terracotta processing (the "tupin") and in the nineteenth century it reached 14 manufactures. In the center there are elegant residential buildings and the old well, symbol of the village, in addition to the parish, notable example of Piedmontese Baroque designed by Giuseppe Girolamo Buniva and completed in 1773, and the eighteenth-century church of the Confraternity of the Holy Trinity.
The symbol of the village.
Dedicated to the Fauglia painter Alvaro Marioni (1911-1999), author of many Tuscan landscapes.
The ancient Arab quarter of narrow alleys and facades decorated with majolica, where the Tunisian community lives and architecture and perfumes recall North Africa; it is known for its fish cuscus.
The big green lung around the Certosa.

The parish church of the 16th century with a Latin cross with a central dome, transformed after a lightning lightning in 1670 set the wooden coffered ceiling on fire. In the presbytery there is an imposing restored organ; it preserves wooden statues of the seventeenth century escaped from the fire and 17 rounds on canvas with Christ, the Apostles and the Evangelists painted by Thomas De Vivo in 1864.

Parish church built between 1871 and 1883, with a 46-metre-high dome collapsed in 1988 and rebuilt; in the left arm a Madonna with Child, Saint Anthony of Padua and angels of 18th-century Venetian school, by Giacomo Guerrini. Remember the role of Boretto as port of call of the Venetians on the Po.
Fellini in the open air, free.
The island stretches south of the center, called Spinalonga, with views of San Marco and the churches along the foundations.
The ancient and noisy morning fish market, reachable by climbing a staircase in lava stone next to Piazza del Duomo.
Cumulation with Aquaria, Museum of Fighters and churches €7, reduced €5, family €16
The concentric walls of the village.

A well-preserved bourgeois house of the seventeenth century: the kitchen with the fogolâr, the dining room with the Galvani ceramics of Pordenone, the room, the studio of lawyer Battista Bruseschi and a room with a set. It belongs to the parish of Saints Philip and James; openings on indicated dates, information to the tourist office.
Church made in a cave dug into the rock, where the Basilian monks lived during the life of retreat and prayer.
The park card indicates it closed (red usability bubbles, earthquake situation)
In the former house of the Humiliates, the Pinacoteca civica and the Historical Museum, with works by Mosè Bianchi, Pompeo Mariani, Anselmo Bucci, Arturo Martini and Marino Marini.
The historic spa, with deco buildings from the 1930s.

Under the hill of the Old Earth, about 120 meters of tunnels under the noble Guiderocchi and Malaspina buildings connect the cellars through hatches and ancient tunnels, used as dispensaries, shelters and escape routes.
The historic church built in 1629, with interesting apse and side chapels.
Contemporary art with views of the Pollino.

Born in 1967 as a private institution on the initiative of Giuseppe Giovanni Bellia, owner of the Vivai di San Bernardino, who in the seventies developed the collections of exotic plants, especially succulent, and sought rare species in Val Sangone. In 1989 the Piedmont Region bought it and joined it to the Museum of Natural Sciences in Turin; today it grows more than 2,000 species from all over the world and an expanded collection of wild plants of Piedmont. Free for children under 14 years of age and Museum holders; in the season 2026 open from 2 May to 30 September, Monday-Friday 9-12 and 13-17, Sunday 14-18, Saturday closed.
15th century church in the historic center of the village; next to it is the Museum of Sacred Art "Silvestro Frangipane" (Silvestro Frangipane), which also houses paintings from this church.
Park warns that descriptions refer to before the 2016 earthquake and that many historic buildings have been damaged

Abbey founded by the Marquis Aleramo of Monferrato about 950-960 and endowed by him in 961 and entrusted to the Benedictines; suppressed in 1802. The Baroque interior with a single nave, enlarged in 1580, has three chapels on its side: in the chapel of the Rosary the tomb of Aleramo with a fragment of pavement mosaic and two frescoes attributed to Guglielmo Caccia, in the chapel of the Jesuits a canvas by Andrea Pozzo with the death of Saint Francis Saverio (1670-1675), an Immaculate of the Hunt, the choir in walnut of 1591 coming from Santa Croce di Casale and the organ Lingiardi of 1860. The bell tower has the lower Romanesque-Lombardy; wooden portal of 1766. Free access during functions.
Built in the thirteenth century and transformed in the sixteenth century, it preserves four defence towers; linked to the Mandelli family, lords of the village.
€6 cumulative ticket with the archaeological area of Concordia, reduced €2 (18-25 years); free before Sunday of the month

Thematic path designed by Pro Natura Torino that connects the square of the Basilica of Superga, where a 1.6 m steel sphere represents the Sun, in Infini.to: 13 stations with planets on scale and information panels along the GTC track in the Natural Park of the Superga Hill, about 8 km, 3 hours and 20 minutes, 400 m of altitude difference uphill. Inaugurated on October 5, 2025.

Camerano is located in the heart of the Conero Park: from the paths in the woods you walk on foot, by bike or by eBike, between gentle hills, the river Aspio and Mount Conero, with the sea just a few minutes away.

Late-Gothic, one of the largest in the Alpine arch: choir of 1417-1451 and nave of 1497-1524, whose first stone was laid by Massimiliano I in 1497; mighty pillars in white marble, southern portal of Mattheis Stöberl and Baroque frescoes by Adam Mölk (1753). On the north side the Roman plaque of Postojna Victorina, found in 1497 digging the foundations.

English garden built in the nineteenth century by Count Agostino Pepoli next to the towers of the defensive system, with views of Trapani, the salt pans, the Egadi, the Stagnone, Mount Cofano and the Zingaro Reserve.

Isolated on a spur of erosa sandstone on the ridge between Val Tidone and Val Chiarone, it is among the most evocative and ancient castles of Piacentino: in the X and XI centuries belonged to the monks of San Savino, then to those of San Sisto until 1296, it was taken by Obizzo Landi in 1314 and sold to the Church in 1322. In the inner courtyard a well 50 meters deep; some rooms house a B&B.

Church of the sixteenth century, already mentioned in the pastoral visit of Mgr. Regazzoni of 1577, with a single nave decorated in the last century by the ponzonese painter Ivaldi called "il Muto" . It has a valuable 17th century high altar and side altars with 17th century paintings, including those of San Bovo and the Holy Rosary of Monevi; in the ancient sacristy a seventeenth-century canvas attributed to Beccaria. The outdoor porch was wanted in the eighteenth century by the Delfini family. Visitable during religious services.
Geopaleosito visitable, described as unique in Sardinia and with few comparisons in Italy; part of the recovered fossils is exposed at the Paleo Archeo Centro at the foot of the hill.

The fourteenth-century church on Corso Garibaldi, renovated in 1508 in a sober Renaissance style and defined as a museum church: it preserves the Madonna and Child in polychrome terracotta (1415 circa) attributed to Donatello after the restoration, his only work in Umbria, a Deposition of the Pomarancio, paintings attributed to Raffaellino del Colle, frescoes linked to the workshop of Luca Signorelli, a Robbiana terracotta, a wooden choir from 1550 and a Byzantine wooden crucifix of the late thirteenth century.

Guided tour of about 3 hours proposed by the Marble Museum: after the collection, a panoramic walk to the nearby quarry touches a lime furnace, the old piano charger, the derricks and the oil mill, and the work of Urban Art Groups up to 25 people by reservation (info@museodelmarmo.it); recommended period March-May and September-November, in case of rain, please refer.
The highest Gothic in the valley.
The castle of Carafa and Spinelli between vineyards and sea.
The Mantua countryside of Nievo in a 16th century villa.
Ancient Romanesque in the hills.
Path for experienced hikers with fords and exposed sections with cable; not recommended after heavy rains and storms

Renaissance belt commissioned by Onorato III Caetani in 1448 and completed in the first half of the seventeenth century, with the gates of the Well, of the Walnuts, St. Nicholas and Sorda and the bastions of the Torrenuova (at the tail of swallows) and of San Sebastiano with drawbridge. The route of about 1 km between ancient olive groves offers views from the Roman Castles to the Circeo and the Pontine Islands.
The most romantic alley in the village of San Valentino.
A three-headed hermitage, a copy of an ancient lost sculpture, in a circular stone tub surmounted by a capital with three lion faces.
€3, reduced €1,50
A stop in the books.
One of the most intact medieval squares in Emilia.

Theatre of the late nineteenth century overlooking Piazza Marconi, enlarged to a semicircle to embrace it, with boxes, loggia and refined decorations, once considered a jewel of southern Italy. The 19 sets were created by the sets of the Teatro San Carlo di Napoli and the curtain, designed by Ponticelli, represents the Challenge of Barletta; in 1876 the citizenship defended him from the rebels who wanted to set him on fire. After a period as a cinema it was reopened in 2012 after an important restoration; guided tours, tel. +39 080 5242244.
Carlo Levi's canvas.
Borgo della val Varatella, Orange Flag, known for the Toirano Caves with prehistoric traces of Bàsura and the ethnographic museum in the historic centre.
The Roman capitals.

Arid meadows where you will encounter the graves of Cellina, Meduna and Colvera, a place of community importance: steppe vegetation with orchids, wild thyme, flax of fairies and the rare Tatarian Crambe, with views of the Friulian Dolomites; flat paths suitable for cycling and an observatory of flora and fauna.
A Roman theater in the countryside.

Borgo della Bassa Parmense was born around the Rocca Meli Lupi, a 14th-century castle that became a princely residence and still inhabited by the family: inside the stuccoes of the Bibiena and the Galleria dei poeti; in the village the neoclassical synagogue with the Jewish Museum Fausto Levi and the Parmigiano Reggiano Museum in an ancient cheese factory.
MiC card (updated 2020) indicates closed daily; check opening with the Municipality (0963 351002)
Ponds included in the Special Conservation Area
The lower oval square designed by Biagio Rossetti, with the column and the statue of Ariosto, where you run the Palio.

Center closed to traffic around Via Roma, with a direct view of the Brenta Dolomites from the square. Palazzo Saracini is a noble Baroque residence of the seventeenth century, now a parish house, with double stone staircase and quadrilobed windows; the Casa del Dazio preserves medieval elements in the porch.
The fifteenth-century castle.
Small church excavated in a natural cave, hidden among the brambles in the area called "Cruci" .
Coast signalling lighthouse built on archaic structures and materials, identified by archaeologist Paolo Orsi during construction work.

In the castle Colonna Enriquez: a gallery with 60 works, 49 historiographic panels on the territory, an ornithological collection and examples of theater machinery for special effects; audioguides available.
The wine of Vigoleno, aged six to seven years, produced in the cellars around the fortified village.

On the hill above the hill, about three kilometers from the village, it was built at the end of the nineteenth century with the offerings collected by the hermit between Giuseppe Cetraro and the owners of the vineyards, because the saint is protector of the vineyards; diocesan sanctuary since 1997, with a single nave with three arched porch and bell tower. The party is held on the second Sunday of September.
A triptych of the early sixteenth century in a large nineteenth-century church.
Thermal baths become museum.

Porta Nuova, built in 1613 by the architect Ettore Smeraldi, combines the medieval and Renaissance parts of the village. In the center of Palazzo Chigi, of the eighteenth century, today seat of the Town Hall, and Palazzo Platonio, former residence of the Farnesian administrators; in the tuff are dug the medieval butts, wells used to preserve water and wheat.

Tower erected in 1540 by Pope Paul III Farnese to calm the struggles between the factions of the Nicelli and the Camia; it rises about 2 km from the village in the direction of Bramaino, on the hill above Bettola.
Enter the house where Cima was born.
A small 18th-century hermitage decorated.
The bread of the past.
The castle with two towers overlooking the village.
Romanesque church founded in 1275 that houses the Crucifix painted by Cimabue, a masterpiece.
Medieval residence attributed to Nino Visconti, judge of Gallura and friend of Dante, who cites him in chant VIII of Purgatory.
The memory of the secular bond with the Habsburgs.

Overlooking Piazza Vescovado, it is Caorle's oldest and most important building: it dates back to 1038, it is dedicated to Santo Stefano protomartire and stands on the remains of a early Christian basilica, in Romanesque style with Byzantine elements. There is a Roman funeral altar from the first century A.D., a 13th-14th century gold palace behind the main altar, a 15th-century fresco of St. Christopher, a baptismal font from 1587 and paintings from the Venetian school; Roman artifacts are exhibited at the apse.
challenging hike (about 15 km, 1,000 m of altitude difference), hermitage on almost inaccessible dinners, serves mountain experience
The Palace of the late 17th century in Kennedy Square, space for exhibitions and events open on occasions like the Golden Night.
Cycle path along the river Tronto from Ascoli Piceno to the sea, connected to the cycle path of Salaria.

Two easy and combinable routes, suitable for everyone: from the old village of Massurie you climb with moderate slopes to the Col de L'Piais, while the Truoi Arthith is a short walk through the meadows.
They're drooping over the harbor.
The rosette and the mosaic.

Renaissance village on the Lepini Mountains, at 630 meters, with one of the largest pedestrian historical centers in Europe that can be reached only on foot or on the back of a mule; the Borghese Palace, the church of Santa Croce and the Borghese Granaio with the Archaeological Museum, while on the Civita Plan there are polygonal walls and hydraulic works of the ancient city.

In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the historic centre underwent profound urban changes and many churches were rebuilt or renewed under the guidance of the Mesagnese architect Francesco Capodieci. The route recommended by the Municipality starts from Porta Grande (Porta Napoli), the rest of the ancient city walls, crosses Piazza Orsini del Balzo and Vico Castello until Piazza IV Novembre, the heart of the city, and passes through Porta Nuova, historical access that united the bourgeois quarter to the ancient village.
The view from the lantern pays off all the steps.

The museum is housed in the Swabian Castle, the last of the eight towers of the walls, called the Man for its key role in the defence of the city; in the thirteenth century its secrets were used as torture chambers for prisoners and condemned. It collects finds from the VI-IV century BC, largely from the nineteenth-century collection of Paolo Vagliasindi and mainly from the area of Sant'Anastasia, in the territory of Randazzo.
The convent that hosts the festival museum.
Born in 1637 as Teatro del Sole in the ducal stables, rebuilt by Pietro Ghinelli between 1816 and 1818 and named after Rossini in 1855; it hosts the Rossini Opera Festival.

Small fifteenth-century church outside the ancient walls, at the crossroads between Francesca and Cremasca, restored in 1979 by the Alps. In the presbytery the Trinity with the Apostles and the Assumption; on the walls a cycle inspired by the Sistine Chapel, from Creation to the golden calf, and in counterfaced the Last Judgment, of a painter perhaps near Callisto da Lodi.

The original nucleus, built thanks to a flourishing economy, preserves medieval houses with mullioned windows and porticos and numerous palaces of kind, including Palazzo Ginetti-Lucchini with seventeenth-century façade; there are also the church of San Rocco, with a 16th-century fresco, and that of Saints John the Evangelist and Baptist.
Summer concerts in the cloister.
The collection of puppets, puppets, scenes and scripts of the family of puppet makers Ferrari and other Italian and European companies.
the page Parma Welcome on Bardi indicates it closed for restoration
The Cathedral of Vow.

Hill country of the Lambetino mentioned from the fifteenth century as "Sancto Petro de Mayeda" , with the parish of San Nicola di Bari rose on the site of an ancient abbey of San Pietro , the historic districts of the Piazza , the Travone and Gibia and Palazzo Aiello , where in 1860 was guest Garibaldi .
To get to know the medieval Gallura next to the basilica.
A large church with a Tintoretto attributed.

Bronze statue of 1898 by the Roman sculptor Adolfo Laurenti, little bigger than the natural, made in two equal copies: one is in front of the Ministry of Finance in Via XX Settembre in Rome, the other in the main square of Bomba, where stood the Fontana Grande. It remained long in the hallway of the town hall and was placed in the square only sixteen years later.

It is indicated by the Municipality as the only museum in Italy dedicated entirely to the composer, who lived in Montalto from the age of five and set Pagliacci, inspired by a tragic fact he had witnessed as a boy. It contains documents, scores and testimonies related to Mattinata, Zazà and I Medici; it is located in the Dominican complex of the fifteenth century, today the Town Hall. Open Wednesday-Saturday 10-12 and 16-18 (Touring Club); tel. 368 7368634. Every year the country dedicates a music festival to him.
A Perugine table and towers in the village.
Neoclassical church at the entrance of the bridge, rebuilt in 1831.
The life of the rebellious camps in over 4,000 objects.

The square, the main meeting point of the city, was placed under the Barberini; the Fontana dei Leoni dates back to the first form in 1845 and in 1927 the sculptor Romeo Liberati replaced the terracotta lions with those in travertine.

At Guadagnolo, the highest town in Lazio (1218 m), the Marian shrine dates back to the XII-XIII centuries and is one of the oldest places of worship in Italy; entrusted since 1883 to the Polish Resurrectionist Fathers, it was visited several times by John Paul II. Nearby is the Cave of San Benedetto.
Herbs aromatic next to the abbey.
The Bembo frescoes in a lowland fortress.
Romanesque church once linked to the Benedictines of Montecassino, in the district of the Doge's Palace; it houses the venerable painting of the Holy Face.
Bread as a work of godly art.
The abbey's treasure and his pharmacy.

Country residence of the family of Lombardi, today municipal seat: in 1714 Elisabetta Farnese was hosted, betrothed to the king of Spain. In the Town Hall there is the multimedia exhibition space SEM, with the virtual visit of the archaeological area of Costa Balenae.
A UNESCO Venetian fortress entirely surrounded by water.

Born in 1974 from the donation of Mario Rimoldi's collection by the widow Rosa Braun alle Regole, it is located in Ciasa de ra Regoles on the Corso Italia, near the parish church. The collection, declared of cultural interest by the Ministry, includes works by Savinio, Garbari, Depero and Guttuso and important nuclei of de Pisis, Sironi, De Chirico, Semeghini, Tomea, Tosi and Campigli. Family ticket €15; cumulative for the three Museums of the Rules €12, reduced €8.
Trekking in the ruins of the Great War, under the Presanella.

On the promontory at the bottom of the cliff, at the beginning of the beach of Levante, it is probably the oldest religious building in Caorle, built on remains of the 6th - 7th century where there was a wooden church with three naves dedicated to St. Michael the Archangel. The current building, with a single nave with a palladian pronao style, is from 1751, wanted by Bishop Francesco Trevisan Suarez; the legend tells of fishermen who found a wooden statue of the Madonna and Child in the sea on a marble pedestal.

The hillside town of the Waldensian valleys, with the capital of San Bartolomeo: here rise the Lighthouse of Freedom of Gabetti and Isola, monument to the partisans of the Pinerolese valleys, the 19th century Waldensian temple and the Museum of Viticulture; isolated in hamlet Rostagni, the temple of Roccapiatta linked to the Waldensian resistance of 1686.
The zoo in the heart of Villa Borghese.
The fortified village of Dal Verme.

Rocky mountain with silvery rocks, whose appearance recalls that of the Moon, with limestone cliffs that dominate the Castle of Fosini; the area is protected by the Cornate and Fosini Nature Reserve. The Parco delle Colline Metallifere offers a network of very busy trails.
Rare example of Gothic architecture on the island.
A village with views of the villa.
Lake and high altitude pastures.
The shrine of the patron saint's feast.

On the Trentino shore of Lake Idro, a few minutes drive from the village, the beach of Porto Camarelle has the Blue Flag of Legambiente; the Biotope connects two beaches with a wooden walkway and is a refuge for many species of birds. Canoeing and kitesurfing are practiced on the lake; in Baitoni passes the cycle path of the Valley of the Churches.

Primitive parish church built under Urban VIII (1623-1644), restored in 1865 thanks to the German sculptor Theodor Wilhelm Achtermann, who left numerous plaster sculptures there; new restoration in 1994.
The Belle Époque power station.
The Roman Gubbio of Iguvium.
The fortress that dominates the village and the coast.

Municipality of Alto Casertano with the historic hamlet of Alvignanello, where the parish museum of sacred art collects statues, ex-vote, vestments and ceramic fragments of the local excavations; in the capital stands the parish church of San Leone Magno and in Alvignanello the convent of Santa Maria degli Angeli, built between the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries.

In the seventeenth-century stables re-arranged by Fuksas: finds from prehistory to the Middle Ages, especially of republican and imperial age, the plastic of the Tuscan villas and sculptures related to the cult of Bacchus, including the "Dioniso Braschi" .

Small village of shepherds and peasants at 290 meters on the northern slopes of the Majella, above the valley of Alento, born around the Longobard castle of Polegra and linked to the Benedictine abbey of San Liberatore in Majella, from which it takes its name (Terra dei monaci) .

Built in the nineteenth century, it contains works of Serresi workers: a wooden Crucifix of the Scrivo workshop, St. Joseph of Antonio Scrivo and statues of Raffaele Regio. The statue of the Assunta, of the Neapolitan school of the early eighteenth century, comes out in procession on the  "varia" by Bruno Barillari (mid-nineteenth century).
Rich in works of art, at Piazza Luca da Penne.
Romanesque inside the walls.
The flamingos are just a stone's throw from the center.

Byzantine fortification built in the first half of the 11th century on a rocky hill to defend against Saracen raids, a long refuge of the Regins; the name comes from San Niceto, an admiral of the Byzantine monarchy venerated in Sicily. It is indicated as the only pre-Norman military complex in Calabria still almost intact: ship-plant with the stern towards the Strait and the bow towards the Aspromonte, walls about 3,5 meters high, monumental entrance, two square towers and the remains of a cistern; from the top you can see the Etna. At the foot of the ascent the church of the Annunziata with the Christ Pantocrator frescoed in the dome, in recovery phase. Walk up to the Mediterranean maquis; free parking; guided tours through the Pro Loco (tel. This appropriation is intended to cover the costs of the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) and the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF).
The church of vow against the plague.
Small village with medieval buildings that have remained unchanged, indicated by Visit Tuscany as a stop in the territory of Capolona.
Military memory of the Africa campaign.
Numerous 17th century mills along the road from Britto district to Marina di Nicotera.
The trenches of the Great War between the spires of the Five Towers.

It preserves mainly Roman finds found in 1950 in the excavations of prof. Lino Vanuzzo: domestic ceramics, fragments of frescoes and mosaics and building elements, which suggest a settlement of some importance. The ancient sources here recall a mansio called Maio Medauco, near a branch of the Brenta.
Cemetery on four levels with marble and granite sculptures rich in esoteric and Masonic symbols, reached by a stone bridge with three arches.
The square of Bagno Vignoni is a bathtub of thermal water 49 meters long and 29 meters wide, already known in Roman times; it is not bathing, but at sunset the steam envelops the stone houses.

In the locality of origin of the Pico, a parish church built in the IX century, documented in 1044 and rebuilt in the XII century: seventeenth-century facade, fifteenth-century bell tower, an ambo attributed to the school of Wiligelmo supported by two telamones and a loggia of the XII century with baptismal chapel, palotto in Carpigiana scagliola (1686) and a Madonna of Venetian-Cretan school.
To understand one of the great tragedies of the twentieth century alpine.

It houses a wooden crucifix carved in the seventeenth century by Fra' Innocenzo da Petralia, venerated as miraculous; the stained glass windows and painted ceilings were destroyed by bombs in July 1944.

Stone fortress attributed to the judges of Gallura and already standing in the thirteenth century, disputed between the judges of Gallura and Arborea, passed to the Aragonese in 1380 and then returned to the Arborens; perhaps residence of the judges, also of Eleonora of Arborea. The square crenellated tower, the ruins of the walls and some cisterns remain. The name comes from the legend of the pigeon stuffed with the last broad beans that convinced the besieging Saracens to retire.

Church before 1163, with a bell of 1394. On the right wall of the presbytery the San Sebastiano of 1478, indicated as the oldest authentic work of Perugino, coming from the chapel of Mary Magdalene destroyed in 1779; there is also a Crucifixion of Tiberius of Assisi.
Centro arbëreshë seat of the Byzantine rite eparchy, with the Cathedral of St. Nicholas of Mira, the gjitonies gathered around the squares and one of the oldest salt mines in Europe.

A city dominated by the two Scaliger castles known as Romeo and Juliet, linked to Luigi Da Porto's novella; it houses Villa Cordellina Lombardi with frescoes by Giambattista Tiepolo, the ancient quarries of the Priars and the Museum of Archaeology and Natural Sciences Zannato.
The cultural lounge of the city, with the Valli and Ariosto theatres, the Palazzo dei Musei and the Parmeggiani Gallery.

First mentioned in 928 in an act of the Longobard princes Landolfo and Atenolfo, it has a radiocentric plan with two concentric roads, alleys to steps and medieval houses dug into the rock; the belt had twelve towers, of which few traces remain. You enter from a large arch with two frescoes of Christ and Our Lady and climb up to the tower at the top: 15.40 meters, square plan of 9 meters, walls 2.20 meters thick, damaged in 1496, dovecote in the nineteenth century and lowered in 1965, with the terrace today belvedere. In 1996, a bas-relief recalled the 500 years of reconstruction after the looting.
Excursions on the Picentini.
Romanesque countryside along an ancient pilgrim's street.

Beyond the bell tower, it marked the end of the fortified city: the name, of Arabic origin, means "outside the walls." There are the medieval church of San Biagio, that of Santa Lucia and San Nicolò, with an arch under the bell tower that was perhaps one of the city gates.

Established in 1931 at Palazzo Arpi: archaeological and ethnographic sections, picture gallery, lapidarium and the reconstruction of two daunie tombs of the IV-III century BC, the Tomb of Medusa and that of the Knights, with the mosaics of the House of lions and the Panthers of Arpi.
The country of the palace.
Industrial archaeology of brick.

At the hamlet Ruata (1130 m) there are the Waldensian church of 1888 and the former Catholic church with bell tower of 1853, today Sala Valdese del Teatro; from here start the paths for the Lazarà hill, the Gran Truc and the lake of Lauzoun.
From prehistory to peasant civilization.

Ethnographic museum opened in July 1981 in the former town hall next to the square: reconstruction of the typical house of Andreis, forge of the blacksmith, combs in bone, Easter ravenelle (cràceles), the working of the shoes and the objects in wood and bone of the "sedoners" , the walking craftsmen of the valley.

Of the castle (Castrum Mali) built by the Valperga di Masino around the thirteenth century on the hill at 343 meters, besieged and destroyed by the Spanish in 1652, there is only a quadrangular tower, today bell tower of the cemetery.
See the wildlife of the park closely.
Next to Charles V Castle, with 998 seats: born in 1737 and national monument since 1979.
The fossils of the Marche Apennines.
The civic heart of the city.
Church of the village dating back to 1260, among the places not to be missed indicated by Italia.it.
The historic garden of the villa, open to all, with shady avenues and secular trees; in summer exhibitions, concerts and workshops.

Ruins of the tower erected in the sixteenth century at the behest of Pope Leo X, with the bull ...Cum iniuncta... to control the often rebellious castle in San Ginesio... the last trace of the fortified castle of the thirteenth century... hosted castle and soldiers until almost the Napoleonic age.
Small village uninhabited on a spur of rock between gentle hills and bitter calanchi, compared to the leaps of Volterra; in the post-war period it became known for the murder of the

The first major building work of Corato, financed by the Decurinato citizen shortly after the foundation of the city, recognizable by the portal to acute sixth. Damaged by the earthquake of 1627, it was consolidated with a high arch, still visible, supporting the left side wall.
The basilica on the hill, overlooking the Montiferru.

Village of just under a thousand inhabitants on the limestone plateau of Su Taccu, with narrow and cobbled streets from which suddenly open panoramas on the valley of the Flumendosa; among the churches also Santa Maria (XV-XVI century) and Sant'Elena. Sources and river give a cool microclimate in summer.
In the Orangery of Villa Borghese, eighteenth-century "Casino dei Giuochi d'Acqua" surrounded by the Lake Garden.

Born from an initiative of Bishop Aldo Garzia in 1983, it occupies the former Seminary built in 1751 and restored between 1999 and 2004: about 900 m2 on three floors with fifteen exhibition rooms and multimedia stations.
On Piazza Colocci, home of the Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Jesi, with an art collection from ancient to contemporary; it is part of the urban museum network.
The sanctuary built in 1737 by São Paulo della Croce in the green of the promontory.
From €2 to €4

Marinar village of Costa Viola overlooking the Strait of Messina, capital of the swordfish and home of the IGP nougat; rebuilt in chessboard after the earthquake of 1783, it preserves the Aragonese tower of Capo Rocchi, the church of Carmine with the Museo Angelo Versace and the Castle Ruffo on the promontory of Marturano.

The castle remains an old ruin that dominates the village from above, panoramic point; Frederick II resumed it in 1226 after a siege, Queen Joan I sold it to the Aquilans in 1382 for 11,000 florins and in 1529 Charles V granted it to Gian Battista Savelli.
The King's Palace.
Large urban park on one of the seven hills of Cagliari, with outdoor gyms, rare plants and ponds, and the library Emilio Lussu.

Attested from the 13th century on the north-east side of the walls, it owes its name to the transformation of the Visconti; it was residence of feudal lords and Venetian podestà and store of food and ammunition. Quadrangular plan with four corner towers of different eras, blackbirds tail of swallows and squares, courtyard with Venetian symbols; the moat, fed by resurgences, today is a meadow, with sixteenth-century terragli on the north and west sides. Guided tours of about an hour and a half on the first Sunday of the month, even on towers and walkways, not accessible to people with mobility difficulties.
The southernmost village of continental Tuscany, closed by walls, a few kilometers from the sea; called "small Athens."

Born in 1977 in the basement of Palazzo Ubaldini (former stables, prisons and snowfields), it exhibits over 2,000 finds: mainly fossils of Mount Nerone of about 200 million years ago such as the ammonites, tools in silce, remains of the cave bear and of prehistoric elephants and minerals from various parts of Italy; a section on dinosaurs with skulls, eggs and claws from Mongolia and the United States and a room on human evolution. LIS video guides, interactive panels and audio content.
The power station in the mountains.

Ascent road towards the cathedral, flanked by noble palaces: at the beginning the Baroque palace Zevallos, at number 35 a palace with Renaissance elements; by detouring via Bixio Continelli you reach the fifteenth-century church of San Giacomo di Compostella.
The towers of the walls become houses.
The majestic castle overlooking the valley above Pratovecchio.
The dome of majolica that dominates the village.

In Praticello, the town hall, the church of San Matteo was built between 1690 and 1703. In the village of Gattatico the parish church, a modest church dedicated to St. Thomas of Canterbury, is of Romanesque origin and preserves some of its elements.
Island of the archipelago on the UNESCO site, with the church of San Venerio mentioned in the description of the good and the archaeological area of the monastery.
A castle of the beginning of the millennium in the Sabina countryside.
Canal dug into the rock on the shore at the promontory of Ansedonia, next to the deep cave of the Queen's Split.

Villa of the late seventeenth century of the Sorra family, probably designed by Giuseppe Antonio Torri with Francesco Maria Angelini, example of Emilian baroque with oval hall at double height, imperial staircase and chapel; since 1972 it belongs to the Municipalities of Castelfranco, Modena, Nonantola and San Cesario. The park, born in French and transformed between 1827 and 1850 in English on the advice of Giovanni De Brignoli, with fake castle ruins and towers, caves, greenhouses and pond, is considered the most important extensive romantic garden in the region.

Canavesian country without castle or walls, with a fourteenth-century shelter almost intact in the plan, defended by a medieval tower-door and with the frescoes of the first fifteenth century of the chapel of Sant'Evasio, next to the parish church of 1628.

The main square was created by the filling of the ancient fortress, which began in the first half of the nineteenth century and continued for over a century; it faces the "cappellone" of the Confraternita della Misericordia, started in 1837 on a project by Nicolao Pellegrini, with the external fresco of the Madonna del Carmelo. The name recalls the Nazi-fascist retaliation of July 5, 1944, when Attilio Biamonti was shot on the square and the fire destroyed the upper part of the village, a wing of the castle and the town hall with its archive.
Risotto in its capital, in fair season.

The footpath is 24 km from Carota (Pieve d'Alpago) to Sant'Anna di Tambre, which connects Alpago, Chies d'Alpago and Tambre to the base of the main mountain groups of the valley, with historical evidences and natural landscapes; between the intermediate accesses San Martino d'Alpago, Funes and Pian Formosa. The difference in height does not exceed 300 m, it is also designed for visually impaired people and two stretches can be traveled by wheelchair; a free app offers descriptive audio tracks.
An open-air country-gallery.

It dates back to the 12th century and is considered the oldest church in Val Gardena: Gothic exterior appearance, Gothic and Baroque interiors, with Gothic frescoes from the late 15th century presbytery, wall paintings on the life of St. James next to the pulpit and the carved high altar attributed to the brothers Vinazer-Pescosta (around 1750), with golden figures of apostles and angels.
