The sculptures on the altar are copies of local artisans, the originals are at the Museum Gherdëina. You can only walk along the ancient Troi Paian street; weekly guided tours in summer and winter by reservation at the Tourist Association of Ortisei.

Complex in the lower part of via Siracusa: Santa Marina combines Norman elements, an Aragonese fortification and Baroque decorations; St. Agatha, largely rebuilt in 1857, preserves an Annunciation by Antonello Gagini (1519), a Sant'Agata del Montorsoli (1554), a Madonna by Michelangelo Naccherino (1601) and the Christ Long, carried in procession on 23 and 25 August and in Holy Week.
The spiral climb to the viewpoint on the hill.
The largest and most famous fountain in Rome, built between 1732 and 1762 on a project by Nicola Salvi on the theme of the kingdom of the Ocean, made immortal by "La dolce vita."
The theatre of the Napoleonic age.
The Bass of the Marshes.

Cultural association dedicated to the cultivation, processing, promotion and enhancement of tea and its traditions, in an environment built according to the principles of Feng-shui. It presents itself as the only tea museum in Italy and has twice entered the Guinness of Records, for the collection of over 600 varieties of tea and for the largest teapot and teacup in the world; the Metropolitan City cites its tea room as one of the largest in Italy.
Walk through majolica and ceramist shops.

Wanted by the parish priest Don Fiore Borrelli, who designed it since 1952, opened in 1997 in two rooms of the Mother Church of Santa Maria della Motta and, after a restoration, reopened in summer 2007. The collections cover more than 4,000 years, from the Bronze Age to today: archaeological section, the rebuilt chapel of the old Mother Church, a picture gallery with the Madonna del Carmelo by Nicola Troisi (1690), sculptures of the seventeenth-seventeenth century, vestments and liturgical furnishings of the confraternities (XVI-XIX century) and the fourteenth-century coat of arms of Filippo Sangineto.
South Tyrolean Christmas par excellence.

In the Palazzo Viani-Dugnani, built between the Six and the eighteenth century and seat of the museum since 1909: collections of painting, sculpture and archaeology; at Palazzo Biumi-Innocenti the section on popular religiosity and ex-vote.

Local park of supra-municipal interest of about 1,400 hectares between Cislago, Marnate, Gorla Minore and Rescaldina, east of the Olona valley up to the pine forest of Tradate. Wood of robinies, silvestri pine trees, oaks, hornbeams, chestnuts and birch trees, with squirrels, peaks, owls and owls; cross it three streams (Fontanile di Tradate, Gradeloso or Bozzentino and Bozzente, the only one with constant flow even in dry periods). The seventeenth stage of the Way of Saint Augustine passes through.
The Marian shrine of Irpinia.
Birdwatching at dawn.

The lakefront, about 2 km long, runs between plane trees and palaces; the old port, closed by historical buildings, is crowned on the pier by a column with the Madonna. Under the porch of Caffè Clerici were found the writers Piero Chiara and Vittorio Sereni; Piazza Libertà has been the port of the boats since 1826, while via Felice Cavallotti, the ancient counter of the merchants, now houses ateliers and art workshops. More secluded, on the hill, Piazza San Francesco was the center of the ancient town.

Quadrangular fence in local stone with mast, two drawbridges and internal loggias; built in the fourteenth century under the Scaligeri, in the Venetian age it was the seat of the podestà and the Council of the Thirty and hosted the prisons until the early twentieth century. You can visit 12 frescoed rooms and the 6 cells of the tower.
Then the Liberty route through the streets of the village.
Since 1998 full protection: forbidden landing, bathing and anchor; it is observed from the Beach of the Knight with a guide of the park (SardiniaTurismo)
Apuan marble from prehistory to the quarry.

A 17th-century shrine dedicated to the Black Madonna of Monserrato, the city's companion, surrounded by four wings of porticos and with a fresco of the Crucifixion on the façade; from the churchyard you can see the plain of Cuneo and the Alps. Walk up from the centre in about 2 km along a Via Crucis of thirteen nineteenth-century pylons; in December and January it hosts the exhibition "Presepi di Monserrato" .
The door to the Supramonte.

Founded in 1997 in the former spinning department of the Cottonificio Carlo Ottolini (later Bustese), neo-Gothic brick building probably from 1891-1896: machines, products, documents and objects of the textile industry and other industrial traditions of Busto.
The palace-fortress on the square.
The memory of rural civilization in a villa on the Riviera.

Mountain area above Gandino with easy paths and longer routes to Montagnina, Pizzo Formico and Paralightmine, where the refuge offers 360° views; the regional portal signals it for trekking and paragliding. Infopoint open Saturday and Sunday 9-12.30 and 14-17.30; parking fee (Gratta and Sosta, €3).
The turquoise sea of the Costa Viola.
Green coniferous lung planted from the beginning of the twentieth century, suitable for walks and recreation.
To be combined with the Pinacoteca Podesti.

Designed in 1836 by Giacomo Moraglia and built in 1842-1845, it was inaugurated on 18 April 1845 with I Lombardi at the first Verdi crusade; Angelo Moia painted 18 scenes, the Morgari brothers the curtain, and Enrico Cassi realized the bronze bas-relief of Verdi. Over 600 seats with 62 stages on three orders; Arturo Toscanini also performed there. Today it is named after the designer Valentino Garavani.
The Pietà di Pomponio Amalteo.
Documented from 1248 and rebuilt in 1503, partly Gothic; it preserves a crude wooden statue of St. Ulrich of the 13th century.
Piano and music box playing again.
The view to the Monviso.

Marian Sanctuary attested from 1324, with origins related to an event similar to the miracle of Loreto; it was an obligatory stop for transhumant shepherds and the current appearance derives from a restoration of the sixteenth century.
San Marino on the horizon.
Baroque church built on the ruins of the ancient parish church of Santa Maria, with a Romanesque portal.
Roman Domus dating from the end of the II and the beginning of the I century BC, adjacent to the Domus del Leone.

Built on the previous church of Sant'Anna and aggregated in 1541 to the Lateran Basilica of Rome; it has two orders of granite columns, a stone portal and the dome covered with majolica. Inside a sixteenth-century icon and the wooden statue of Our Lady of Itria by Vincenzo Scrivo (1797).
The descriptions of the Park refer to the state prior to the earthquake 2016; the regional portal indicates center and monuments only partially accessible
The peasant life of the Prealps told room by room.
The woods of the white fir.

Rock sites in the surroundings connected by artificial caves, probable places of worship and early Christian burial: Contrada Rossa would have hosted a early Christian community, in Santi Quaranta and Peirito there are early Christian tombs.
A Lodron castle overlooking the Vallagarina.
The eighteenth-century reconstruction in Venetian forms of the Domus dominicata pomposiana, today the municipal library and headquarters of the Fondazione Bassani.

Cisterna pubblica di mezzo Cinquecento ascribed to Nanni di Baccio Bigio, perhaps according to design by Antonio da Sangallo il Vecchio, built for the community (the smallest "Cisternino" served Palazzo Di Monte). Two aisles divided by round arches, crossed by a metal catwalk; it is the second largest cistern in Tuscany after the nineteenth century of Livorno and today its water irrigates the hanging garden of the Town Hall. The visit inside is free.
The village of the mills on the water.
The finds of Mevaniola and the territory, in the abbey of Sant'Ellero in Pianetto.
In a restored seventeenth-century rural house, interactive route on traditional Valdostan medicinal plants, with games and workshops for children.

Opened in 2006 in the fifteenth-century Palazzo De Petra, called Casa del Leone for the Marzocco at the entrance: he collects paintings by Teofilo Patini (Castel di Sangro 1840 - Naples 1906), realist painter of the Abruzzo peasant life author of the social  "trilogy" (Vanga e latte, L'erede, Bestie da soma), and works by friends and students of the Aquila school that he directed. Tuesday-Friday 11-13 and 15-18, Saturday-Sunday 11-13 and 15.30-18.30, Monday closed.

Established in 1911 with the collections donated to the State by Senator Domenico Ridola: finds from the Paleolithic to the Middle Ages found in the territory of Matera, including vases with red figures of the V and IV century BC.

One of the oldest settlements in the Val Rendena, in the Adamello Brenta Natural Park between the Adamello-Presanella glaciers and the Brenta Dolomites: the Lodron Bertelli Palace with the Museum of the Malga, the Maso Curio, the hot springs of the ferruginous water of Sant'Antonio and, at altitude, the lakes of San Giuliano and Garzonè.

An easy ring of 5.5 km (about 1 hour and a half, suitable for mountain biking) in the Ticino Park: starts from the sports field of Coarezza and follows the ST/IP trail along the Strona river, among pine forests, oaks and chestnuts. Touch the dam of Porto della Torre, in operation since 1942 and today also hydroelectric power station, the Sass of Biss, erratic mass with rock engravings linked to the culture of Golasecca (IX-V century BC), and a panoramic point on the Ticino at the edge of the moor.
A natural corner beyond the beaches of Marcelli.
A Roman republican city intact in its enclosure of cyclopean walls.
Salt sources born from plasters.

It tells the sundials preserved among the old houses of Bellino, painted on private houses and chapels and along the paths, recovered since 1999 on impulse of the Municipality with European funds of the LAG Valli del Viso. Open in June, July and September Saturday and Sunday 15-18, in August every 15-18; in winter on call for groups (tel. +39 0175 689 629).
The stone parlour of the valley.
The hills of Bolzano wine.

One of the most important art monuments in South Tyrol: of pre-Romanesque origin, rebuilt in the 12th and 14th centuries with gothic cruising vaults. The 20 arches are frescoed between the end of the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries and show the passage from the Gothic to the late Gothic; famous is the presentation of an elephant (3rd arch) and the Adoration of the Magi (13a). It gives access to two hidden churches.
Frescoes compared to those of the Reggia and a hanging garden with snow.
Bears, wolves and eagles in the heart of the Apennines.
The "pantheon" of the Italians.
The Chinese room and travels of the traveling count
Contemporary art on Ticino.
Walk in the Legnago di Scaligeri and Venetians.

Historical building in the 16th century, with sandstone portal, porch with loggia and painted decorations on walls and wooden ceilings. It is a municipal property and houses the civic library and a classroom of the Verri Museum.
The Resistance told by the artists.
By bike on the banks between poplars and herons.

Built at the beginning of the thirteenth century by the Counts and passed to the Caetans in 1297, with large frescoed rooms; here in 1303 the emissaries of Philip IV of France attempted to capture Pope Bonifacio VIII, the episode known as the "slap of Anagni" .

The Teramano hilly town with the Acquaviva Tower, the circular church of the SS. Rosario and, in the hamlet of Montone, a fourteenth-century city walls with three towers and the sarcophagus of Bucciarello of 1390; in Colle Leone the astronomical observatory houses a museum of natural sciences.

The small museum of the basilica with vestments, illuminated codes, reliquaries, the fifteenth-century dossals and the antiquarium in the underground spaces with Roman amphorae and the remains of a domus.

Founded in 1960 and since 1999 in the former Jesuit College, it collects weapons, uniforms, photographs and original documents on the role of Salemi in the 1848 revolution and in the 1860 Mille expedition.
The Tour des Signaux, according to tradition, connected the castles of Grains, Villa and Verrès with colorful fires.
The organ of the Faithful and the relics of the saints patrons.
The shovel stolen in 1922 and found.

Borgo of ancient origins (the Bronze Age), mentioned from the IX century and then long in the Papal State, with a historic center of alleys, arches and remains of walls and towers. It's the "Paese del Presepe": the Monastery of the Orsoline houses a monumental nativity scene in 16th century terracotta and since 1982 Italian and foreign artists paint nativity on the walls of the houses.
The Gothic portal and the Paradise of Battistello.
Monumental oaks in the hills.
Romanesque church with a Madonna and Child of Neri di Bicci; in the former convent the Casa Chianti Classico with exhibition rooms and a route on the history of wine.
Church built in the form of trullo in 14 months in 1927 and very modified in the sixties, at the top of the hill along Via Monte San Michele.

Via Roma, traced in the mid-eighteenth century, is known for its workshops of torronari. The crispy name of the village is made with honey, sugar, egg white, vanilla and almonds, heated and processed in the torroneera, then cut and covered with dark chocolate; numerous Beneventano companies produce it according to traditional rules.

Church dedicated to Maria Assunta, already existing in the Middle Ages and rebuilt between the end of the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries: from a single aisle with three altars it passed to seven altars with continuous vault. In 1771 it was decided to replace the old sailing bell tower, damaged in 1744, with the current one; in the nineteenth century two small lateral naves were added. The treasure includes liturgical vases, a processional cross of the sixteenth century and a collection of relics.
47 paintings by an internationally awarded Piedmontese painter.
A portal finished at the Metropolitan.
The Savoy Forest.

A small harsh town whose Greek name, Skydon, means "place" from the dense woods, razed to the ground by the earthquake of 1783, it preserves the parish church of San Biagio and, in the nineteenth century Palazzo Ruffo, the library "Paolo Greco" and the Museum of peasant civilization.
In the deconsecrated church of San Donato, a temple dedicated to one of the great Piedmontese wines.
The findings of modern excavations on site.
The Nobel House.
Panoramic view of the coast.
A canvas attributed to the Morazzone along a devotional path.
It recalls the 16 insurgents of the place shot by Napoleonic troops in 1799.
Ayasse's throat.
Baths of the II century AD on the Puteolis-Neapolim street, discovered in 1939, with mosaic floors; available on request.
Of medieval origins, it rises at the top of the village and was rebuilt after the earthquake of 1905.

The fortified village closed by high medieval walls and towers, with arched alleys and stairs in the rock; in the church of San Pietro Apostolo an ivory crucifix of the sixteenth century attributed to Giambologna.
The flavors of Madonie at the market.
Exhibitions on the castle walls.
To be checked on the official website

Villa of the sixteenth century, now municipal seat; in its noble hall the Municipality organizes exhibitions with free admission, like that of 2026 on the lagoon landscapes of the painter Aldo Bergamini.
Lake in the Mont Mars Reserve, at the entrance of the Lys valley.

Born from a temporary exhibition owned by the Mussino family, it exhibits about 150 objects of daily use in three sections: chestnuts, hay and barn, the path from the tree to the lumberjack laboratory. Open on Saturday 15-16 and Sunday 10-11, or on request.

Ancient stùa with carved wooden walls wanted around 1740 by the archpriest Ludovico Rovereti, with tables, chairs, stove and numerous paintings; burned by Italian soldiers in November 1918, was restored in 1926-1928.
Birdwatching along the Enza.
Erected between 1590 and 1625, it preserves a fresco considered miraculous. In September the Palio dei Lumi concludes the Football in costume between the four districts of the village.
Built in the second half of the 1950s on a project by Giulio Brunetta, it houses a crucifix by Mario Pinton, a front by Carlo Mandelli and works by Paolo De Poli.
A high-altitude church.
The Rome of the towers.
On the western side, large sandy bays with calm sea.
The two-tone Romanesque basalt and red trachyte.
Church of the fifteenth century with works by Matteo Cesa, Cesare Vecellio and Andrea Brustolon, next to the Cloister of the Servites.
Autonomous building in the central Piazza Garibaldi, in a simple late Art Nouveau style: designed in 1919 by engineer Aldo Govoni, it was inaugurated in 1924.

The castle, built on a spur of rock before the Mille (XI century according to Discover Arezzo) to control the passage over the Arno, protected a bridge, an inhabited and a series of mills; remain the mighty crenellated mast and sections of the walls, which mirror themselves in the river and are seen from the walk along the embankment. Degradation and restoration of the Eight and twentieth centuries have changed its system. In the center the Palazzo del Podestà, Palazzo Ducci and Palazzo Subiani-Ducci.
The Sugarbread is a 132-metre-high scarf shaped by erosion, a natural monument; near, the Grand Canal of Nebida is a narrow valley between walls of about 100 meters that descend on turquoise waters.
Lombard Gothic with frescoes.
The fifteenth-century portal and the six-hour clock.

Strong in blocks of trachyte built in 1767 to protect the entrance of the port, in the area of Spalmadureddu; in 1898 it was converted into an astronomical observatory and since 2016 it houses a multimedia museum on the history of Carlofort.
€5, reduced €3,50; cumulative with the Castle €8
Where the Challenge was born.
The miraculous fountain of St. Julius, a stone's throw from the lake.
Sacred art in a border village.
The sounds of the Calabrian tradition.
A tribute to the poet of the city.

Late Baroque residence commissioned by the canon Giovanni Perego, humanist and art lover, as a place of holiday and family representation. It is located along the cycle path that crosses the square of Ronco Briantino and continues in the Park of Rio Molgora towards Carnate.
The remains of a temple outpost.
Closed to the public for bad weather damage, together with the Second Complex
Velasco and Serpotta in the mother church.
The oldest early Christian sarcophagus in the Marches.

Benedictine Abbey on the Via Claudia Valeria near the Pescara, wanted by Emperor Ludovico II: the Chronicon Casauriense gave its foundation in September 871 (873 second Abruzzo Turismo), with the relics of Pope San Clemente transferred from Rome with the consent of Adriano II. Damaged by the Saracens and the earthquake of 990, it was rebuilt by Abbot Guido in 1025, reconsecrated by Grimaldo in 1105 and rebuilt in the current forms by Abbot Leonate in the second half of the 12th century with Cassino workers. The three-arched portico precedes the bronze portal of 1191 to 72 tiles (48 original survivors according to Abruzzo Turismo); inside three aisles ambone of the twelfth century, candelabra for the Easter candle, fourteenth-century ciborium and crypt. Closed on Monday; open on Tuesday and Saturday 9-19.30, other days 9-13.30 (Sundays all from April to September, only 1a, 3a and 5a from October to March); with bad weather can stay closed, better call (085 8885162).
The symbol of the country and the view from above.
The summit from which Rome can be seen.
An intact peasant village, told by its inhabitants.
The historic center built in the fifteenth century on top of the hill, overlooking the Adriatic.
The sanctuary of the Egyptian gods in a Roman city-port on the Po.
45 min (climb)
The Gonzaghesco village overlooking the Garda.

The 6th century high-medieval building around which the Castellum Sancti Donati was born, destroyed by the Saracens at the beginning of the 10th century and rebuilt in the 11th century by the abbots of Farfa; place of worship at least until the 16th century, in the second 20th century the ruins were incorporated into an agricultural building. There are still niches with frescoes; today it is a stage of the Museo dell'Olio, with the Garden of Olives of the world.
A walk through the ducal buildings.
In Pievasciata installations and contemporary sculptures of artists from all over the world in a forest of oaks and holm oaks, along a ring path.

In Canonica there was the collegiate church of San Lorenzo, spiritual center of the parish church of Cuvio and the entire Valcuvia, linked to the main historical events of the municipality. The imposing bell tower of the 13th century remains.

Protected natural area of six hectares, a small naturalistic gem that protects biodiversity; from the natural observatory you can photograph small birds that frequent mangers and water troughs. The guided tours last about two hours (from 15 to 17); recommended boots, binoculars and camera.

Rebuilt after the earthquake of 1693, it has portal and three-cell bell tower with stone balustrade; the only aisle preserves a large altarpiece of 1525, by unknown author, with the Martyrdom of San Lorenzo.

Monastery complex of the seventeenth century with small church annexed, inserted in the perimeter of the ancient turrita belt; seventeenth-century cloister with columns with original pavement and well. In church a Madonna in glory with St. Matthew, St. Anthony of Padua and Cardinal Carlo Borromeo.
Discovered in 1929 in Marina di Maratea, it has a room of 70 meters for 20 with stalactites and stalagmites and is considered one of the smallest and best preserved tourist caves in Italy.

About 260 hectares at the mouth of the Candelaro, the last strip of the great marshes of the Capitana and SPA in the Gargano Park: freshwater ponds and brackish with Italian knights, fighters, pittims, chiurli and beccaccini. Information on visits to the Park Visitor Centres.

With 2120 meters it is the highest peak of the Reggiano Apennines and the second of the northern Apennines, with wide panoramic prairies on top; from the ridge, which shows some glacial circus, the view extends over Val d'Asta.

Modest eclectic country church, built by local workers and dedicated to the Madonna delle Grazie, with frescoes dated to the late Romanesque period. You can reach it by a rural path that comes off the road Façade Preti or from the locality Purraphele.

It leads with a Ghibelline tower and loggia, next to the remains of the ancient castle of Brunforte, lords of the village in the 13th century; from the outside you can see also the former Franciscan monastery on Mount Stalio.

Opened in 1973 after the death of the collector and painter Carlo Lamberti and enriched in 1988 by the collection of Giuseppe Novello, it occupies eight rooms on the first floor of an eighteenth-century palace (with stairs). It has 122 works from the sixteenth century to today: watercolors by Tranquillo Cremona,
In the Isola district, the 1500s shrine with a spring in the basement and the Napoleonic Foundry Eugenia, where the bronze of the Vittorio Emanuele II of Piazza Duomo is fused.

Artificial lake 600 m fed by the Acquabianca stream, just outside the Park of the Apuan Alps and about 5 km from Minucciano, with the ancient village of Gramolazzo on the shore and the hamlets of Agliano, Castagnola and Verrucolette overlooking. You can take a bath, a picnic with barbecue on the shore and rent sailing or rowing boats; from the lake passes the tour of the four lakes by bike (8.1 km, challenging).
The warrior's painted grave.
Lecce's living room.
Le domus de janas UNESCO.
Arab-Norman Palermo off the most crowded routes.

Borgo della Val Gandino has always been linked to the textile manufacture, which the Museum of the Textile  "Martinelli Ginetto" tells with working machinery; in the village noble palaces from the sixteenth century, the church of San Michele with the Madonna Addolorata dei Fantoni and, on a panoramic hill, the church of San Martino.
The story of the mineral resources of the Val di Cecina in a building of the fourteenth century.

The Pieve di San Clemente, the main church of the village with paintings and baptismal font, is the starting point of the Tour of the seven churches, a route of about 4 km that touches the Madonna del Soccorso, the Madonna del Carmine (ascending from Via Piave), San Giuseppe on the Corso Vittorio Emanuele III, San Sebastiano, San Rocco and the Madonna della Cava.

Small nuragic monumental source about 300 meters from Rebeccu: a paved atrium with seats along the walls leads, through a trapezoidal entrance obtained in a monolithic slab, to a basalt cell covered with tholos that collects the water vein. It remained in use until the late antiquity (a.c. fourth century coins) and in the Christian age there was engraved a cross.
The Langhe Donjon.
The panoramic village of the two seas.

Municipality of the Plateau of the Sun, in Valle Camonica, divided between Ossimo Superiore and Ossimo Inferiore; to see the archaeological park of Asinino-Anvòia, megalithic sanctuary of the Copper Age, the ethnographic Museum "Ossimo Yesterday" and the seventeenth-century and eighteenth-century parishes.
The finds of the territory.

Borgo della Baronia di Carapelle in the National Park of Gran Sasso and Monti della Laga, dominated by the Rocca Calascio, at about 1,460-1,500 meters the highest fortification of Abruzzo, set of "Ladyhawke" and "The name of the rose" with next to the octagonal church of Santa Maria della Pietà; in the village the Franciscan complex of Santa Maria delle Grazie.
Residence of the last years of Alfred Nobel, today museum; the gardens are free entry.
€10, reduced €2 (EU 18-25 years); cumulative €20
Perhaps the oldest sacred building in the municipality, in the 11th and 17th centuries, built on the remains of a pagan temple; decorations and Baroque paintings.

Long and with significant difference in altitude, on a ridge at almost 2000 meters, along the ancient path of merchants, pilgrims and warriors; reported as  "Sentiero dei Franchi" and, up to Col Bione, also with the signs of the GTA. It can be divided into two with an overnight stay at Col Bione.

Urban plant of Catalan-Aragonese era with low granite houses and ceilings with oak beams, frames of doors and windows carved in chisel in the oldest districts (Josso, Sa Montiga, Fruscu); next to Sant'Antioco the peasant houses with large portals and walled courtyards, the Muggianu house with two Aragonese windows and, among alleys and squares, the Magasinos, private cellars like that of the Su Conte palace.
One of the most beautiful squares in Italy.
Unpublished times, to be requested (tel. 0731 86030)
The park on Castagnola.

Built between the fifteenth and 1590 (date reported by the nineteenth-century parish priests) in late-Gothic forms with Renaissance motifs, on the model of San Giorgio di Pozzomaggiore: façade with cusp between buttresses and square bell tower, rosette and portal to the sixth, on whose architrave is carved a niche frieze, similar to the predella of a Catalan retablo, with Christ at the column between the Virgin, Saints Peter, Paul, Victoria and James. Inside a nave in four spans with vaults and the apse with key hanging depicting the patron saint.
The writer's grave.
A stop on the itinerary of places of faith.
One of the best preserved Doric temples in the world, in the heart of the Valley of the Temples; there the tripod of the Festival of the Almond in bloom is lit.
An icon of Italian rationalist architecture.
15th century ruins at the top of the hill.

In the lower part of the village the church of San Marco, without roof, with the perimeter walls and a rebuilt portal, rises on the Doric temple of Hercules (IV century BC), of which survive the rectangular cell and some blocks of tuff; the place is known for the views.
He was pierced from above on opening days.
Roman mosaics in church.

The center is built around the port, on which elegant buildings overlook, including the municipal palace of the late sixteenth century. On the side towards the lake are walled the balls of cannon fired against the country by an Austrian ship in 1866, during the Third War of Independence.

A wet karst area of 335 hectares, established in 1998 and managed by the WWF: from west to east Lake Murana, Lake Preola, the largest, and the three Round Gorghi between maquis, thorny oak and the wreck holm oak of the Bosco del Cantarro; rich in aquatic birds in migration, with wild orchids and the Sicilian marsh turtle.
The 11th century village was built next to the monastery, protected by high walls and ramparts, the first inhabited nucleus of Cava.
Mining port excavated in the rocky wall above the sea, with a tunnel of about 600 meters: an innovative work that allowed to load the minerals directly on the ships.

Frazione in panoramic position on the lake and starting point of excursions, including the Path of the Wanderer; it has three churches, the Immaculate, the Madonna of the Snow and St. Martin, of the thirteenth century, at the entrance of the village. The symbol is the wash-house in front of the Madonna della Neve, used until the sixties, where thanks to the volunteers \'burbinattÂ the water flows again.
Three hundred and several times renovated, once part of the walls; visits in occasion of openings and events.
The temple trace of the village.
A Byzantine crucifix venerated on the coast.
To walk or cross-country ski, with the view of the Grandes Jorasses.

Along the road to the Rocciamelone, between the 718 m of the church of the Madonna dell'Ecova and the 1275 m of Chiamberlando, were found rock engravings and graffiti testifying a pre-Roman settlement, probably Celtic.

Founded by Carlo Gesualdo in 1592, as the plaque on the façade recalls: a single nave church with the prince's coat of arms on the entrance arch and the altarpiece of the pardon of Carlo Gesualdo by Giovanni Balducci (1609), with the prince in prayer next to Leonora d'Este. The Capuchin monastery, enlarged in 1629 and restored after 1980, has cloister and garden and a museum dedicated to Saint Pio of Pietrelcina, guest between November and December 1909, with his cell. Visits in the morning by reservation.
Extraordinary closure until 31 March 2027 for PNRR (MIC) work
The canals surrounding the Medici pentagonal city, to be sailed by boat, with the association Livorno in Batello.
View on two lakes, between paragliding and memories of the Great War.

Rebuilt after the earthquake of 1908 with a twentieth-century façade that reinterprets Romanesque and Gothic forms, with the statues of Saints Paul and Stephen of Nicaea by Francesco Jerace. At three aisles, it has in the Chapel of the Blessed Sacrament inlays of polychrome marbles and a canvas of 1665 by Domenico Marolì; at the bottom of the right aisle the fragment of the column linked to the preaching of Saint Paul.

Protected wetland of 1,512 hectares on the Ionian coast between Noto and Marzamemi, with ponds, marshes and ancient salt pans, the tuna trap, the Swabian Tower and the beaches of Eloro, Marinelli, Calamosche and Vendicari.
An immense pictorial cycle.

Facade with an eighteenth-century appearance but completed at the end of the nineteenth century, with older bell tower; inside a Crucifix by Pietro da Rimini suspended in the apse and paintings by Mannerist painters of the late sixteenth century.
16th century wooden sculptures in a church restored in 2001.
The geological history of the Madonies.

Started in 1513 on a project attributed to Agostino Fondulo and concluded in 1525, it rises in the green about one kilometer from the center, on the place of the apparitions of the Virgin on Sunday Zanenga. The restoration of Amos Edallo (1964-1965) has recovered its original forms; it preserves frescoes by G.B. Dordoni, the wooden Madonna of Paolo Maltempo (1560), paintings by Angelo Bacchetta (1862) and an organ Serassi of 1836.

Set up in the ancient crypt of the Duomo, it collects works from the cathedral and other churches of Ravello, some no longer in operation; among the pieces of relief the so-called "Sigilgaida Rufolo." It is part of the complex with the Duomo and the Church of the Body of Christ.

To the south of the village, in a place rich in water and vegetation: documented from the thirteenth century, passed between 1294 and 1306 to the hospitable order of the Holy Trinity of Venosa and, by tradition, lived there San Cono di Teggiano. In 1514 Pope Leo X joined her to the Charterhouse of Padula, of which she became a grange; the new church of 1578 has baroque stuccoes and the Assumption on the high altar. Succeeded in 1866, in 1869 it was bought by the Barons Gerbasio and used as a residence of the settlers, storehouse and stable. On the first Sunday of August there is the pilgrimage in honor of San Cono.

Municipality of the high Garfagnana north of the Apuan Alps, largely inside the Regional Park, with the lake of Gramolazzo, the valley of Orto di Donna at the foot of Pisanino, the Romanesque parish church of San Lorenzo, the Hermitage with copies of the stele of the Bronze Age and, in Gorfigliano, the Museum of the identity of the high Garfagnana.
The evening walk on the bay.
In the Park of Memory and Peace of Fondotoce, next to the site of the partisan massacre of June 1944.
Castle and Basilian church on the hill.
The cathedral of Piazza Giovanni Paolo II, the ancient Piazza Pia, with the chapel of the Madonna del Popolo frescoed.
Opened to worship in 1632 and restored after the earthquake of 1783: central nave with transept and apse, two aisles on Tuscanic columns and, since 1800, two Roman mosaics.
Five kilometers of pebbles on the Adriatic.
It rises 2,390 meters overlooking a natural amphitheatre visible from the hamlet Tornetti, among the favorite destinations of the hikers of the valley.
The stories of the country told by his elders.
A rare round church with Gothic frescoes.
Prehistory and fossils of Valpolicella.
The church is located on a square overlooking the valley and Lake Canterno, known as the "terrazza della Ciociaria" (terrace of the Ciociaria), opposite, in Piazza Roma, the panoramic viewpoint.
Public square with the molten fountain and the outside of the church of Saints Faustino and Jovita, admirable at all times.
The sanctuary of the miracle.
The Langhe outdoor theatre.
Stage of the summer itinerary towards the high villages.
The most important monument of the village.

Founded in 1985 by AMC Italia in a wing built specifically in 1984 at the company's headquarters, it collects cooking instruments from all over Italy from the 3rd millennium BC to today: Roman and Apulian finds, terracotta pots and metal pots, the first pressure cooker (1930), metal-coated pots typical of the coasts and kitchenettes working in the 19th century, as well as a workshop of the rebuilt and working calderaio.
The view from the Dolomites to Baldo.
Alleys and views of the Castles.

Romanesque complex with raised and crypt dating from the 11th to the 12th century, bell tower of the late fourteenth century, frescoes of the 14th and 15th century in the presbytery and probably remains of the 10th century in the underground chapel.
Meet Ötzi.
Three centuries of churches in the center.
It welcomes those who come from Piacenza and recalls the battle of 218 BC on the Trebbia between Hannibal and the Romans, defeated also thanks to the surprise effect of the elephants.
The most famous of the about ten kilometers of coast of Gaeta, between fine and golden sand, small bays and cliffs, with crystal clear sea; to photograph the rock of the
The sixteenth-century villa with five chessboard bodies by the lords of Busseto, which houses a museum with the settings and atmospheres of Verdi's works.
A water cathedral under the square.
Over sixty historic trains on real tracks.
€13, reduced €8 (6-18 years)
Sanctuary designed by Giovan Battista Aleotti, remained intact in the earthquake of 1624 that destroyed Argenta.
Park with works by the artist Deva Manfredo immersed in the woods, signalled by Visit Tuscany in the territory of Casole.
Piero's Magdalena is in a corner, to be looked for.
The face of Lussu signed by Sciola.

The original village, born at the beginning of the eighteenth century as a rural agglomeration of Fabrizia's manor, was struck by the floods of the fifties and then abandoned; today few people live there. In the district of Campanaro, a small church houses wooden statues of Serrese workshop, including the Madonna della Natività, carried in procession on September 8th; the bell tower remains only the monofora.

A small museum and documentation centre dedicated to Cardinal Michele Pellegrino (born in 1903), his literary work and his pastoral activity. Visitable every day of the year according to the activities of the parish of San Bernardo Abate; it is advisable to book at least one day before (tel. +39 0171 719329).

A 149-hectare reserve on the left bank of the Albegna high valley, which protects the southern slopes of the limestone complex of Monte Labbro: woods, shrubs, limestone cliffs, springs, pools and porches, with large centuries-old trees such as black hornbeam, oak and linden. Reintroduction projects for red partridges, vulture heads and river prawns; a wet area was created for the billon by the yellow belly.
The fishermen's church overlooking the Adriatic.
On the edge of the park, the mill of Bert, of fifteenth-century origin, still in operation and visitable, and the mill of Bosa.

Country on the southern slopes of the Limbara, the land of Vermentino and the seat of the Time in Jazz festival: the Wine Museum with the Regional Enoteca, the ruins of the medieval castle of Montacuto, the seventeenth-century churches and the forest of Monte Limbara.
The medieval parish church with the San Cristoforo on the façade.
The chapel of the cathedral that preserves the Cincere of the Virgin, donated according to the tradition to St. Thomas.
One of the great Italian contemporary art museums.
the MonteCampion Ski Area card indicates the area in recovery and redevelopment in view of a future reopening

Municipality of Stura Valley, north-west of Genoa, formed by the two cores of Rossiglione Superiore and Lower and included in the Park of Beigua: the canyon of the Val Gargassa, the Museo Passtempo sul Novecento italiano and the churches of the village.
the Superintendence reports only extraordinary openings with free guided tour, without ordinary hours
The monastery in the bay.

From Valbruna (Hotel Saisera, 820 m) to the Nabois plateau (1,050 m) under the walls of the Little Nabois: 5.5 km easy (about 2 hours and a half) between red firs of resonance, precious wood for the violin, with panels on the theme, the small art park Other Memories, the Sabuata spring and the theme park of the Great War Abschnitt Saisera with trenches and Austro-Hungarian posts.
€6 round trip, single travel €4
Walking in the trenches of the Great War.

One of the major Italian deposits of copper and iron sulphides, active from the middle of the nineteenth century to 1962 and already known in the Bronze Age (a handle of pickaxes of 1876 is dated to the age of Copper). The rocks are ancient oceanic crust (serpentinite, gabricus, basalt pillow); the acidic mineral waters color the landscape of reddish deposits. You can reach it on foot or by car on the road that climbs from Santa Vittoria di Libiola to Tassani; management Mediterranean Services (0185 478603).

Water sawmill documented since the 16th century, with a piston technique introduced in the valley by the Republic of Venice for the trade of timber; the current building is from 1922, work of carpenter Dellagiacoma      \Giochelon of Predazzo, restored in 1985-1988 by the Ladino Cultural Institute. A segantino reached 30 tables a day of fir, larch and pine; it is still used by the inhabitants of the village and is owned by the ASBUC of Penia, heir of the ancient Rule.
The house of a painter from the Po.

Municipality of Bassa Reggiana known for the Terramara Santa Rosa di Fodico, a village of the Bronze Age of seven hectares with visitable summer excavations and a museum open all year round; in the village the church of Santo Stefano of the twelfth century and the monumental cemetery.
The bikes-boat of the streetwalkers of a century ago.
The walled village.
A fifteenth century church with remains of frescoes.
Today, the town hall has a cloister with a portico of twenty arches on octagonal pillars and 28 frescoed lunettes in the seventeenth century.
Small sanctuary next to a cave used by the first Christian communities for secret worship; the entrance of the cave is still visible, closed by a grate next to the facade.
The sunset on the gulf.
In the district of Santu Pedru, the piazza-monument dedicated to Sebastiano Satta, where his house stands.

Built around 1100 by Clementina, daughter of Norman king Ruggero II, it was restored in Renaissance style in 1480 as a patrician residence and passed in 1748 to the Rotondi, then to the d'Alena, lords of the feud until 1806. The façade dominates the square with a Renaissance loggia with round arches; in the courtyard a Renaissance staircase with colonnade rises to the noble floors, where there was a private chapel. In 1799 and 1860 it was the scene of clashes, and between 1943 and 1944 it hosted the German Staff, then Italian commands and American officers.

Masterpiece of the 18th century Marche according to the FAI, acquired by the State in 2022; the Ministry has allocated about 10 million euros for a first batch of restorations that includes the historical gardens. The Italian garden has fountains, water games, avenues, niches and statues. In summer 2025 the garden was opened a few Saturday afternoons, free of charge, with visits in groups of up to 30 people accompanied by Pro Loco and mandatory booking.
Small museum next to the sacristy of the neo-Gothic church of the Sacred Heart of the Suffragio, the "small Duomo of Milan," with documents and relics linked to the afterlife.
The language and life of the Walser of Rimella.
The Lanino.

On a height at the confluence of Magra and Aulella, it is the most powerful military work of the Lunigiana: Renaissance fortress with square plan attributed to Jacopo Ambrogio Malaspina (end of the fifteenth century) or to Giovanni dalle Bande Nere (1522), perhaps according to design by Antonio da Sangallo the Elder, already efficient in 1553. It was taken by the Spaniards on 24 December 1733 after three weeks of siege, it was the residence of the British Lina Duff Gordon and Aubrey Waterfield since 1920 and since 1977 it has been of the State, entrusted to the Municipality. Guided tours every 45 minutes without reservation; free for under 6 and residents.

According to tradition, it rises on an ancient pagan temple, where shepherds found a statue of Our Lady considered miraculous; the cult dates back to at least the 15th century and the present building is largely six-seventh century. In 1832 Ferdinand II of Bourbon and Maria Cristina of Savoy were married there; it is still a destination for pilgrimages.
Crafts, peasant civilization and the ex-vote for Saint Michael.

Landscape Museum inaugurated on December 21, 2003 by the University of Salento and the Municipality, with archaeological remains, rural buildings, dry walls and spontaneous flora. It encloses the archaic Messapian city surrounded by walls about 3100 meters long (often 3,50-4 meters, with moat) on about 69 hectares: village of the Bronze Age, reoccupied in the 8th century BC, fortified in the middle of the 6th and suddenly abandoned within the first decades of the 5th century BC. Three pedestrian and cycle paths (yellow, red, green) and at the entrance a panoramic platform, the Open from Tuesday to Sunday, 9-20 from May to September and 9-15 from October to April; closed Monday; groups and schools by reservation.
City of Etruscan origin on the Metallifere Hills, closed by intact walls, with one of the most beautiful medieval squares in Tuscany.
Marzemino and Figo Moro in the vineyards.

Active since 2009 to protect the landscape of the Valle dei Calanchi and the rural traditions related to biodiversity, organize excursions, educational workshops and courses on bees and honey. Visit by appointment and guided tours of the historic centre include the ascent to the Monaldeschi Tower, in the Ortale district, with 360 degree views of Lubriano, the Valle dei Calanchi and Civita di Bagnoregio. Tel. 327 0289027.
The eighteenth-century vanvitellian outside the door.

Remains of the twelfth century of what was one of the main points of control of the lower Empire Valley; Pontedassio was the capital of the castle of Bestagno, a feud under the jurisdiction of the bishop of Albenga, then passed to the Doria and the Savoy. The castle rises on an isolated ridge to the north of the village: the Province of the castle, the tower and the walls of belt, privately owned and in a bad state of conservation.
The political heart of the city.
Liberty and baroque in a hill country.
A baroque interior all stucco.
A Rimini school crucifixion.

In the sixteenth century house that hosted five generations of musicians, where Giacomo Puccini spent happy years of childhood: seven rooms on two floors with photographs, letters, autograph musical manuscripts, the baptismal robe, the bed in which he was born in Lucca and the vertical piano used for many compositions. The route also shows a country house with antique furniture and tools and a kitchen remained unchanged for about two centuries; the last refurbishing is in 2008.

Inaugurated on 7 August 1982 in the village of Pozzo, it was born from the collection of objects of rural life made for twenty years by Gelindo Lenarduzzi; the Municipality bought and restored a building to accommodate it provided that it remained in Pozzo, and the collection then grew with donations from citizens and companies. Among the pieces three handmade pendulum clocks, wagons and agricultural tools of the twentieth century and, the oldest, gramola and combs for hemp of 1810. Open on Sunday 10:30-12:30 (MiC card updated to 2020); audioguide.
Daily life in a home-tower.
The famous talking statue next to Piazza Navona and Palazzo Braschi.
The traces of the Roman Salaria.

Born in 1987 in the complex of the ancient lime furnace, after in the mid-seventies in the nearby quarry were found fossil fishes of the Cretaceous about 92 million years ago. The sections of geology of the Euganean Hills, mineralogy and the nineteenth-century collection of Count Niccolò Da Rio are flanked by an open-air path on the lime production cycle and a geological park with large boulders and models of prehistoric animals of life size.
Walks in the forest of the Meana Forest.

The town of Novarese on the edge of the valley of the Terdoppio: the hamlet of the Badia di Dulzago, 12th century abbey of the Augustinian canons became an agricultural village with the Romanesque church of San Giulio, the works of Alessandro Antonelli in the center, the church of San Vito a Cavagliano and the portico sanctuary of the Madonna della Neve.
Tower of the thirteenth century that served as a sighting and defense of a mill.

Born within the framework of the project that has restored the Mausoleum of Garibaldi in Aspromonte, it re-reads with multimedia technologies the iconographic material of the Fondazione Spadolini-Nuova Antologia, the Central Museum of the Risorgimento and the DIGIMA project to tell the campaign of Aspromonte of 1862, designed especially for young people.
A lunar landscape.

A marina town at the foot of Mount Etna with the port asked to the State in 1836 and started in 1906: in St. Peter's Square there are the City Hall and the neoclassical Cathedral, Minor Basilica since 1967; the oldest church is the Madonna of the Letter with its crypt, and the promenade leads to the fishing village of Torre Archirafi.
In the hamlet of Castel San Pietro, it is the first fortified residence of the local feudalist, documented from 1003-1009, restored by the architect Enzo Pinci.
Countryside and irrigation canals of the Bergamo plain a few steps from the village.
the MiC card reports every day as closed: tel. 0981 913341; italia.it instead places a Museum of Rural Civilization in the castle
The Romanesque church on the crypt.
Fraction with a tower of the fourteenth century; in the crypt of the church of Santa Lucia a fresco of the Nativity of the fifteenth century, and in the village a table of the Pagani.
The memories of the saint born in Capestrano.

Built in 1615 on the highest point of the country, probably on the site of an elymous temple of Venus and a mosque, with a Latin cross: the 1968 earthquake caused a large part of it to collapse, but the apse remained standing.
Built in 1314 by Federico d'Aragona, with quadrangular bell tower and, on the right wall, nine crosses believed to have come from the temple of Venus.
Garden established as a botanical garden in 1984, with rare specimens of tropical and equatorial flora.

Vizzini rises on three hills (Castello, Maddalena and Calvario) on the plateau of the Iblei, in Val di Noto, and is linked above all to Giovanni Verga, who set there pages of Mastro Don Gesualdo and of the novels. To see the Duomo of San Gregorio Magno, the Basilica of San Giovanni Battista, the Vergian palaces and the abandoned village of Cunziria.
The mother church linked to Celestino V.
Contemporary art in a mountain country.
One of the oldest churches in Sardinia.

Città dei Castelli Romani grew up around the Greek Abbey of San Nilo, founded in 1004 by Italian-Greek monks and still of Byzantine rite: basilica of Santa Maria with mosaics and icon of Theotokos, chapel of the Saints Founders frescoed by Domenichino, archaeological museum under the porch of Giuliano da Sangallo and a library of Greek codes.

Opened in 1981 and since 11 June 2021 in a new location in the historic center, it tells in eight sections the Roman Camonica Valley. Among the main pieces the Roman marble copy of the Greek Minerva of the 5th century BC from the sanctuary of Breno, two mosaics of the thermal baths (I-II century A.D.), a larch door from Pescarzo di Capo di Ponte (end II-early I century BC), among the best preserved of the alpine arch, and frescoes with water birds from the domus of Via Palazzo. Closed Monday and Tuesday; only electronic payments.
The objects of the house and work of the high Val Torre.
The living abbey of Finalpia.
Elegant façade, frescoes, stuccoes and gilding: a treasure of the Lombard baroque overlooking Piazza del Municipio.
Romanesque bridge with three arches on the Metauro river, indicated as a photographic point.
The Belvedere and the Passo di Monte Moro, already known to the Romans.

Built in local stone on the Lombard tower and enlarged by the Aragonese in the 15th century; in 1744 the Sangermano barons transformed it into a residence adding the right wing. Completely restored in 2006, at the base exhibition remains of the pelasgic-sannitic walls (IV-III century BC).

In Micottis (522 m) the fountain of the Podinkona with a stone wash-house and a votive ancon restored with a seventeenth-century altarpiece of Our Lady of Health; the "Štrijin ples " Dance of Witches" is a place linked to a legend about witches, with a cross that lights up in the nights before religious feasts.
Two routes of about 7 km: the ancient streets of the feud and the industrial archaeology of lime and cement.
Villa-farm of the II-I century B.C. about 2 km from the city: about twenty rooms around a central court, with tanks for winemaking (calcatory).
The Romanesque baptistery.

It preserves the sacred art collected over the centuries by the Confraternita di San Lorenzo: 18th century Ligurian nativity scene with wooden figures in vintage clothes, processional crucifix of the seventeenth century with silver finishes, the "Martyrdom of San Lorenzo" by G.B. Carlone and other Baroque canvases, a processional case of the Brilla, a nineteenth-century canvas by Veronica Murialdo, the large terracotta nativity scene by Luca Damonte and the paintings by Gino Grimaldi from the church of the former psychiatric hospital in Pratozanino.

The fortress, designed by Fioravante Fioravanti from Bologna for the Fortebracci in the highest point of the country, was destroyed in 1478 at the behest of Pope Sixtus IV: the remains of the mastium remain. On its ruins stands the former convent of Santa Caterina, seat of the library and the Municipal Historical Archives, which conserves papal bubbles from the 14th to the 17th century and the Statute of Montone of 1586.

The medieval old town is a maze of narrow streets and ancient houses, with souvenir shops and crafts. The tour stages are the castle and the cathedral; from the viewpoint of Piazzetta Petrone you can enjoy a beautiful view of the sea.
Traditional canal to walk and vineyards to explore by bike.
More than three kilometers of fine sandy beach, free and equipped, with many times awarded waters with the Blue Flag; the promenade is surrounded by green spaces.
Separate corner accessible from the village of Durano, with a series of lakes and small waterfalls.
A didactic garden to learn about trees and traditions in the valley, suitable for families and schools.

Borgo sulla spiaggia piedmontese del Lago Maggiore, legato a Alessandro Manzoni, che soggiornò volte a Palazzo Stampa Between 1839 and 1861: center historical with arcades and lakefront, the church of San Martino, the Sala Manzoniana, the fishing village of Solcio with the Romanesque oratory of San Sebastiano and the panoramic hamlets of Comnago and Calogna.

17th century palace on Piazza d'Armi, born as barracks and now home to exhibitions and events. On the tympanum a rare decimal clock of the revolutionary age, with day divided in 10 hours by 100 minutes of 100 seconds, system abolished by Napoleon in 1806.

In the hamlet of Rivoreta, it tells the life of the mountain communities of yesterday and today: the processing of chestnuts, the basis of the local economy, the production of coal and the tools for work in the woods, with annual rotational arrangements and a workshop of the toy for children. Visits by reservation.
On the hill of San Licerio, managed by Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo.

In Villa Centanin, about forty instruments (fortepiani, grand pianos, table and vertical) mainly of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, of German, English, French and Italian builders, plus about 120 ancient music-themed prints from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century. The instruments are restored to play as originally used in concerts of the Fondazione Musicale Masiero and Centanin.
Seven rural villages in one, at the foot of the Brenta.

The Castle-Forte dates back to the 11th century and preserves medieval characteristics, the Castle-Piano (Palace) dates back to the 14th century with frescoes from the 15th century. The park of about two hectares, in the Grandi Giardini Italiani circuit, has 40-50 meters high centuries-old trees, an elliptical stone pool, rhododendrons and azaleas in spring and summer hydrangeas; the avenue leads to the Chapel of Ognissanti. Group visits by reservation (tel. +39 335 5244080), at least 2-3 hours.
Regional Observatory of the Valle d'Aosta at more than 1600 meters in Lignan, base of scientific research, chosen for the low light pollution; guided tours and dissemination events.
The promontory of the historic center of Porto Maurizio, with the medieval district and great views, covered by the itinerary "Gira Parasio."
One of the highest bell towers in Cremonese.

In front of the bridge over Liri, it was commissioned in 1834 by Monsignor Ferrari to the architect Vespignani, from which the second name; the facade has Doric columns, pilasters and floral festoons. It is one of the historic residences of Lazio and on the lower floors is the definitive seat of the Archaeological Museum of Fregellae. You visit only by reservation.

Crystal clear lake between rocks and granite blocks in the western Sarentine Alps, from which the river Sagbach comes down towards Aberstückl; to the west the Verdinser Plattenspitze, to the north the view of the White Horn of Sarentino.

Piazza-garden overlooking the lake, with centuries-old olive trees, which joins the lakefront Falcone Borsellino to the port of Canottieri Salò; in the center a stele with the winged lion of Venice in bronze by the sculptor Salolino Aime.
The pope's parishioner, with Palma the Younger.
Small herb garden of medicinal and aromatic herbs, once cured by monks who assisted the pilgrims of the Via Francigena.
Geology read in the stones of the country.
The sanctuary in the vineyards.

Establishment about 4 km from the city, on a limestone hill, which takes its name from a large fig tree; frequented since ancient times as an alternative to the Taurine Thermal Baths. Five natural pools with clear and slightly bitter waters from 30 to 56°C, open all year round from 8 to 20 (until midnight from 12 June to 31 August); tickets only on site.
The Lucan traditions of Pollino.
The courthouse in the open.
The 18th century wooden Madonna.

Town on the hill of the lower valley of the Esino, home of Frederick II of Swabia (born here on 26 December 1194) and Giovan Battista Pergolesi, closed by a well-preserved wall: Piazza Federico II with the Cathedral of San Settimio, the Palazzo della Signoria of Francesco di Giorgio Martini, the Lotto della Pinacoteca of Palazzo Pianetti, the Pergolesi Theatre and, just outside, the Riserva Ripa Bianca.
Museum of nativity scenes and folk art in Lutago, reported by the tourist association of the valley.
A naturalistic path of considerable value on the limestone surface of Colle della Guardia and Monte di Maio.

The village of Alta Valsugana is 480 metres away, between the lake of the same name, the largest in Trentino, the orchards and the Centa torrent: in the center the magnificent crelata Corte Trapp and in front of the church of San Sisto, on Mount Rive the remains of the castle of Sicconi and towards the plateau the ancient road of Menador.
A parish documented for almost nine centuries.
The relics of Valentine's Day among rococo stuccoes.
A parish church mentioned already in 945.
An easy walk with picnic area.
The oldest church in the village, built with pebbles that give the name to Medole.

The most characteristic street, with the tower of the ancient Bishop's Palace of the fourteenth century; of the fourteenth-century walls remain the tower of Via Monte Grappa, a stretch in Via Facchinitti and the corner tower of Via Canuto.

A polygonal tower built by Carlo d'Angiò around 1278 on Mount Tilia, over 1,200 m, to control access to the plain of Leonessa: it is the last trace of the recently established castle of Ripa di Corno. You can reach it with a path in the woods for experienced hikers.
Napoleon's rooms at Elba.
A Roman theatre became a neighborhood.
The gold of Paris gift of a pope.

18th century palace with mythological frescoes, seat of the Wine House; it houses art exhibitions, concerts and cultural events. Around, the hills of vineyards of Marzemino, to be seen at best between the end of September and the beginning of October, in harvest.

On the Poggio dei Santi, about 600 meters on the Cava dei Volaci, a rock complex of the VII-VIII century made known in 1940 by G. Lamb, frequented for over a millennium and abandoned in the middle of the fifteenth century (the oldest graffiti is from 1445). In the eastern arches, the fresco of the Crucifixion with Our Lady, St. John and Longino, from the 11th to the 11th century. It is reached from the old state road 194 Vizzini-Ragusa for a path between dry walls.
The sea under the Gardens of Augustus.

The main place of worship of Praia rises at the foot of Mount Vingiolo, about 90 meters above sea, in three rocky cavities illuminated by natural light, reached by a long steps of pebbles of sea (53 steps according to italia.it). The statue of Our Lady was placed on a rock at the entrance in 1326; every year on 14, 15 and 16 August it is carried in procession to the country.

Benedictine Abbey of the thirteenth century just outside the walls, today a national monument; a stone inscription shows the date 1337. Two ogival portals, trilobed monofora, central nave with round arches; remain part of the frescoes of the 14th-XV century of the Eugubina school, including perhaps the oldest portrait of Pope Urban V, attributed to Matteo da Gualdo.
Sea and ruins on the head.
the MiC card indicates closed every day and the Park of Bracciano signals it open in exceptional way for guided tours: times to be confirmed
19th century church dedicated to the patron saint of San Vito.
The history of fishing and the sea.

It is the seat of the civil, judicial and economic power of the abbots of Fruttuaria, rebuilt in 1526 by Cardinal Bonifacio Ferrero, who installed a tick in a special tower (on the tower of the donjon the coat of arms Ferrero, a blue lion in the silver field). Purchased in 1801 by the lawyer Pietro Giuseppe Frola, it was rebuilt by Secondo Frola with the architect Camillo Boggio (veranda, portico and neo-Gothic tower since 1885); the northern towers, the prisons and the tower of the mint remain. He's from the city today.
The oldest parish church in the center.
Behind the church there is a panoramic square.
Protected natural area of local interest on an Apennine ridge, with mountain landscape shaped by water and wind, destination of hikers.
One of the most harmonious squares in Abruzzo.
A triptych of Gualdo's painter.

Country on the south-western shore of the Lesina lagoon, with the Visitor Centre of the Gargano National Park that brings together naturalistic museum, aquarium and ethnographic museum, and the Bosco Isola that separates the lagoon from the sea.
A country shrine with secular pilgrimage.
The sixteenth-century villa where Ludovico Ariosto stayed, with frescoed dressing rooms; open on Sunday afternoon.

The village rises on a hill on the left of the Tavo, with via del Baio connecting the castle to the mother church and the Gardens of Palazzo Antico supported by the ancient walls. Of the belt there are the Mordecai gate with an ogival arch and the Hospital gate (XV-XVI century) and the nineteenth-century Porta Castello and Porta Palamolla, near which are walled two stone balls attributed by tradition to the cannons of Iacopo Piccinino (1460); outside door the monumental Fonte Grande of 1838, next to the ruins of a source of the late sixteenth century.
A unique museum, designed for families.
A stop along the course.

At 811 meters, in a strategic position between Irpinia, Sannio and Puglia with views of the valleys of Ufita, Miscano and Cervaro: almost trapezoidal plant with corner towers of 13-16 meters in diameter and the ruins of the Norman mast; restored at the beginning of the 2000, since 2009 it houses the museum of Norman civilization.

Borgo at the confluence between Orco and Soana, gate of the Canavesian side of the Gran Paradiso National Park: it preserves the ruins of the medieval Ferranda and Tellaria towers, contended between Valperga and San Martino, and two museums, the ethnographic of the ancient crafts and the plastic museum pole in the former Sandretto factory.

Gallura's cork centre on the eastern side of Limbara, with stone houses and granite paved streets: the parish church of Santa Giusta with the Assumption of Andrea Lusso, the Diocesan Museum in the oratory of the Rosary, the Museum of Cork in the former Capuchin convent and, in the cork forests, the tomb of Giants of Pascareddha.
The valley where the cars don't come.

9th century church in sandstone with richly decorated facade, built on the remains of a pagan temple (dedicated to Dionysus according to italia.it) of the lost Roman settlement of Interamnia Poletina Piceni. On the nearby Colle Terme archaeological excavations have brought to light thermal plants of Roman age.
A walled village hidden in the woods.

Also known as Isola dei Conigli, a small island of naturalistic interest in front of the Rocca promontory, reachable by canoeing; it is one of the main subjects of the panorama from the cross of the Rocca.
A thousand years of history behind a baroque façade.

The village is surrounded by chestnut trees; above 700 meters, in Serro Grande and Serro Piccolo, dense woods of holm oak, over 1,000 meters white fir and beech, with strawberry woods between April and July. Around 1,000 meters the plateau of the Piani di Carmelia with the pine forests; at the Madonna della Salute pine trees about 25 meters high.

The town of Maceratese on the edge of the National Park of the Sibillini Mountains, of medieval origin, largely destroyed by the earthquake of 1799 and rebuilt in several hamlets: the abbey of San Salvatore in Monastero, the castle of Montalto with its three walls, the Madonna dell'Impollata in Sant'Andrea, the Carbonaia Museum and the Butterfly Garden.
A piece of Liguria transplanted in Sardinia.
Calm waters at the foot of the Alps.

A block of ancient Neapolis with thermal environments, between the end of the 1st century BC and the 2nd century A.D., re-emerged after the bombings of 1943 that destroyed the homonymous church; visible from the road, visits on request.
Here today the statue of the saint of serpars is kept.
View of the Valdichiana.

On the first floor of the castle, in rooms born for the activities of the port: works of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries donated by the rector and art enthusiast Attilio Moroni; the entrance hall is dedicated to the painter Biagio Biagetti.
Main square of the city, with urban layout of the first fifteenth century and surrounded by ancient porticos; in the center the statue of Lazzaro Spallanzani, work of Guglielmo Fornaciari of 1888.

Borgo dell'Alto Maceratese at the confluence between Potenza and Scarsito, with canals, washbasins and mill wheels: here you can produce paper from the middle of the thirteenth century, told by the Museum of Paper and Filigree, and a few steps from the center starts the path Li Vurgacci between waterfalls and pools.
From the churchyard, the view of the Apuan Alps and Mount Forato.
The view of the Liri Valley.

Ladin municipality at the foot of the Marmolada, in the UNESCO World Heritage Dolomites: in Sottoguda the fifteenth-century church, the tabies and wrought iron shops, then the gorge of the Serrai towards Malga Ciapela, from which the cable car climbs to Punta Rocca and the Museum of the Great War; in Laste the Gothic Santa Maria Maddalena.
The oldest church in the territory.

First archaeological museum of the Trompia Valley, opened in 2018 in the ancient Broletto di Mondaro, fifteenth century building with exposed stone tower that the excavation of 1996 dates after 1220, with portal fourteenth century on the ground floor. It exhibits finds and reproductions on the origins of the valley, coming from the Superintendence and the Civic Museums of Brescia; in the medieval tower the ethnographic collection of Costanzo Caim with agricultural tools of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. It offers educational workshops.
A stone of over 2,500 years in the middle of the square.
A small mountain village with a mild climate in the Monte Corno Nature Park, known for the rare

A medieval castle in the woods.
Sulfurous waters and salsobromoiodiche known by the Romans; you can also visit the underground springs.

The church of St. Mark, of Norman origin (XII century), is reached from Via Federico II; from here a steep staircase rises to the Castidduzzu, the ruins of a fortification with all probability Byzantine.
The 12th century Greek cross church.

A manor house of more than 1,200 square meters, also called Casa Vargiu, of the Vargiu family since the sixteenth century, today also a hotel spread: on the ground floor the environments of everyday life and the peasant trades of Sarcidano (tool room, bread and sausage storage, bedroom), on the upper floor the embroidering museum with clothes and family accessories. Paid access with guided tour included, at reception and restaurant times.
The streets of the medieval market behind Piazza Maggiore still bear the names of the guilds: Pescherie Vecchie, Drapperie, Orefici, Clavature. Meat shops, cheeses, fresh pasta.
The Romanesque on the path.

A church of duodecimesque origin, several times rebuilt over the centuries, with majolica dome and bell tower of the eighteenth century: the interior with three naves has a coffered ceiling of the sixteenth century and on the main altar a fifteenth-century wooden statue of the Madonna with Child. It is the most famous church of Maiori and keeps ex-vote linked to the local rites; from its churchyard starts the Trail of Lemons.

The tour of the center starts from Piazza Matteotti with its monumental fountain and touches the Civic Tower and the cathedral; in August the alleys of the medieval village host the Borgo Vecchio festivity with food and wine itinerary, singing and dancing.
The symbol of Salento tarantism.

Municipal Museum whose foundation was decided by the City Council on July 9, 1926; it hosts the exhibition "I culti della ferttura nel II millennio b.C." on the hypogeum 1036, with ceramics from the beginning of the Middle Bronze, a support for hourglass perhaps ritual and objects of ornament from the Neolithic to the Bronze Age.

A splendid example of medieval architecture, the cathedral was consecrated in 1153 in San Michele Arcangelo; with the bell tower and the remains of the castle is the testimony of the splendor of the village.
One of the most majestic Giants tombs on the island.
Walk through the streets of a Roman city.
The peasant life in the tower.
It can be reached on foot or by skiing on the glacier, accompanied by mountain guides.
The country lost in the earthquake of 1693.
The center of the village built on the Roman city.
Ori, Greek vases and the history of Ferrara before the Este.

Fortified preside over a relief in the center of the village, probably of the 10th century and rebuilt in the 11th and early 15th centuries; in 1381 Gian Galeazzo Visconti had the village fortified with a fortress and since 1449 Antonio Crivelli, infeudated by Francesco Sforza, rebuilt it with moat and tower guarding the drawbridge. The columns of the courtyard loggia are probably from marbles purchased in Stradella in 1549 by Cardinal Alessandro Crivelli. On the ground floor two frescoed rooms in the sixteenth century: a profane cycle of Flemish taste with seasons, zodiac and agricultural works and a religious one with the life of Saint Catherine of Alexandria and Dante's Paradise; in the library room a Roman mosaic. Since 1948 it has been the seat of the Municipality.
It tells the Jewish presence in Bologna; from here you can explore the alleys of the ancient ghetto, a few steps from the Due Torri.

The Abbey wanted by Carlo d'Angiò to celebrate the victory over the Swabians, destroyed by the earthquake of 1456; then abandoned, it became the home of the Franciscan Alcantarine Sisters, and today the complex combines Romanesque-Gothic, Baroque and modern styles.
Church with the Deposition from the Cross of Domenico by Bartolomeo Ubaldini called Puglio, his best work according to Vasari.
Tell me how you lived up here.

A land of the average Camonica Valley, for a long time among the most important in the valley for iron workshops and trade along the ancient Valeriana Street, of which the noble palaces remain; today it is known for the Musil, the hydroelectric energy museum in the central of 1910, and for the parish church of San Girolamo.
From the early sixteenth century, once a prison for clergymen; a bust recalls Garibaldi's stay in 1875.
The baroque cathedral of Longhena with the canvases of Palma the Younger.
Wine, San Barbato and stilts.

Founded by Saint Benedict around 520, it is the oldest existing Benedictine monastery and the only survivor of the thirteen of the valley: three cloisters (cosmatesque of the thirteenth century, Gothic of the fourteenth century, Renaissance), Romanesque bell tower and neoclassical church of Giacomo Quarenghi (1770). The tour is guided and lasts about an hour.

The city's golden ceiling.

Designed by Francesco Maria Preti (1701-1774) and completed by Miazzi, who reworked the project, it is indicated by the Municipality as one of the most successful examples of eighteenth-century Palladianism: a dominical body with central pronao and two ariosian side boats. In front of the façade the garden is surrounded by a fish pond, on the back stretches up to the slopes of Montello. The Benetton Group has been renovated on a project by Afra and Tobia Scarpa and by Prof. Mora.
The acropolis and the shrines of the Greek colony.
In the valley around the village there are two mills for flour and two paper mills, examples of industrial architecture that exploited the power of water, near the fishing village.

In the former convent of San Francesco, the collection of Don Ignazio Puglisi, who also painted the background canvases of his shows: over thirty puppets arranged in scenes and the traditional theatre; some pieces were exhibited at the Museo Teatrale alla Scala in Milan. The Opera dei Pupi has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2001.

A hilly town 8 km from Varese between the Morone and Casnione mountains, crossed by the Lanza stream: here you will find the Civic Museum of Natural Sciences .Mario Realini is located in Villa Braghenti, the Valle del Lanza Park with the quarries of Molera and ancient churches like San Matteo, from the Romanesque apse of about 1000.

Church parish mother of the country, popularly called "Church Great." The previous church was demolished from May 1, 1948; after years of obstacles the faithful gathered in a warehouse of the Consortium (1948-1955) and then in the crypt (1955-163), until the new church, designed by Marino Marrone and wanted by the parish priest Fr Peppino Gallo (1946-1966), welcomed the first celebration on January 27, 1963; it was dedicated on May 30, 1999. Inside a pictorial cycle of Sfrule-brown.

Path in the forest of Corongia, on a plateau overlooking the valley of the Flumendosa, among cliffs, labyrinths, pinnacles and caves covered by holm oak woods, badgers, terebinths and junipers, with wild peonies and orchids: the pinnacle On Bell Towers (84 m), the walls of Tinazzu up to 100 meters high and the cave Sa Corongia. Walking and mountain biking; equipped picnic area in Bauzzoni.
Medieval civic heart.

Borgo della Val Tidone on a triangular shelf between the torrents Tidone and Chiarone, feud of the Dal Verme since 1378: the Rocca, now municipality, houses in the underground the Archaeological Museum of Val Tidone, while on the dorsal towards Chiarone stands the ancient Fortress of Olgisio.
The frescoes attributed to Cozza.
Built in 1317 on the Palazzo della Torre: from the top the view ranges from the Langhe to the Alpine arch.
Meteorites and minerals.

Thermal complex facing the sea, on 15,000 m2 of greenery, which uses the mother waters and the sludges of the salt pans: inhalations with paediatric ward, broncholungal treatment and respiratory rehabilitation, aesthetic medicine and Spa Club. The first wooden factory opened in 1930, replaced in 1947 by a masonry building renovated in 1988.

The extension of an older oratory, renovated in 1477 after a pestilence, with a four-column portico of 1575; in 1630 it was lazzaretto. A single nave, with mostly votive frescoes and a 1634 altarpiece with the Transit of St. Joseph; recently restored after years of closure.
In the monastic complex of Sant'Eufemia della Fonte, founded in 1008, a path on the history and path of the legendary car race.

It starts from the hut Capanna 2000, in the territory of Oltre il Colle, and leads to the Passo del Branchino, with a view of the homonymous lake, through flowery meadows that color the slopes especially between June and July; from the hut 2000 it is also possible to walk as a family ring.
Waterfalls and caves in the Aniene gorge.
Baroque in vertical.
The Baroque Dauni Mountains under a majolica bell tower.

Built at the beginning of the fourteenth century in Romanesque-Gothic style, it belonged to a Carmelite convent until 1855; in the seventeenth-century convent there is an archaeological museum for the findings of Cuccurada.
The historic centre preserves churches and granite houses. The church of the patron Saint Theodorus was rebuilt in the middle of the twentieth century.
Arab-Norman Church with the mosaics of Ruggero crowned by Christ and the admiral at the foot of the Virgin.
Ticket: see the Museum of the History of Bologna (Palazzo Pepoli)

Overlooking Piazza Castello: Royal Palace with Kings' Apartments and Royal Kitchens, Sabauda Gallery, Royal Armory, Royal Library, Archaeological Museum and Shroud Chapel.
The baptistery next to the cathedral entirely frescoed by Giusto de' Menabuoi, among the cycles of the fourteenth century of Padua Urbs picta.

The noble residences that the aristocracy put at the disposal of the Republic to host ambassadors and dignitaries; registered by UNESCO in 2006 as "Genoa": the new roads and the system of the Palaces of the Rolls, today there are 42.
The oratory on the piazza del Santo frescoed in 1384 by Altichiero da Zevio with the stories of San Giorgio, of strong influence from Giotto.

At 1180 meters, twelve kilometers from Biella, the complex where the Black Madonna is venerated and where in the seventeenth century the best architects of the Savoy court worked; part of the Sacred Mountains UNESCO, with the Museum of Treasures.

Wanted by Carlo di Borbone and designed by Luigi Vanvitelli: 47,000 m2 on five floors with the Royal Scalone, the Royal Apartments, the Throne Room, the Palatine Library, the Court Nativity Crib, the Palatine Chapel, the eighteenth-century Court Theatre and the contemporary Terrae Motus collection.
